News.title: Antigua and Barbuda PM says Burnham should offer reparations
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The prime minister of Antigua and Barbuda has insisted Andy Burnham should agree to pay reparations over the UK’s role in the transatlantic slave trade, urging him to go further than an apology.

Gaston Browne warned there could be a repeat of the past “atrocities” in the future if reparations are not paid and said he believes Antigua’s next head of state should be Antiguan, rather than a British monarch.

It comes as King Charles visits the Caribbean islands ahead of the opening of a Commonwealth summit on Tuesday, which is expected to be dominated by talks about the issue of slavery.

open image in gallery King Charles will open a Commonwealth summit on Tuesday ( Reuters )

Mr Burnham has signalled he would be open to exploring the possibility of a formal apology over the UK’s role in the slave trade, but has shut down any suggestion that reparations will be paid.

But speaking to ITV News, Mr Browne said: “I understand the politics in the UK, in which it may be a difficult proposition for him to agree to any form of reparations, but that just does not negate the need for reparations.

“If there’s no compensation, there’s likely to be a repeat of those atrocities sometime in the future, and you can see what is happening globally already.”

Mr Browne’s views echo those of fellow Caribbean leaders, with St Lucia’s Prime Minister Philip J Pierre, chairman of the 15-member Caribbean Community (Caricom), reportedly saying the Caribbean-based economic and political bloc was “ready to engage” in the structured dialogue Mr Burnham offered.

“No British prime minister has gone this far before… we are ready to engage,” he wrote.

open image in gallery Prime minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Gaston Browne, has insisted reparations should be paid ( Getty )

But he added: “A dialogue that begins by placing reparations outside the room cannot be a complete dialogue.”

Mr Burnham has offered “structured dialogue” with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade and expressed “my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions” but has ruled out considering financial reparations.

But Tory leader Kemi Badenoch urged the prime minister not to apologise because she said it would lead to more demands for reparations, which UK politicians of all stripes have opposed.

Mr Browne said the Caribbean nations were not “coming for Britain”, suggesting money could be found in Britain’s overseas development budget.

Charles is making a nine-day tour of the Caribbean, and when he arrived in the Bahamas on Tuesday, his first leg, the King acknowledged the “great suffering of the past” and confirmed the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) would discuss the legacy of slavery.

Antigua’s prime minister said he had great respect for the King but spoke of his nation becoming a republic.

He told ITV News: “I can say to you, I am a republican.

“So if you asked me about my personal view, I would like to see Antigua and Barbuda become a republic… but I have to recognise and accept the fact that there are certain constitutional provisions to become a republic, and that, ultimately, it is the decision of the people to determine whether or not we become a republic.”

News.title: Trump has field day with Haley Stevens’ ‘brave’ flip against Abdul El-Sayed
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump heaped praise on Rep. Haley Stevens on Sunday after the Michigan Democrat broke with her party to endorse Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, calling her decision an act of bravery.

Stevens announced her endorsement in a video Sunday, two days before Election Day. She withdrew her support for Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, her former primary rival, after a falling-out over Israel.

“As you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away, and he's right,” Stevens said. “And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the U.S. Senate today.”

An hour later, Trump celebrated the endorsement on Truth Social.

“Wow, this is BIG,” the Republican president wrote. “Stevens, a Highly Respected Democrat, who narrowly lost in the Primary to Abdul Mohamed El-Sayed, and who has been breathlessly wined and dined by the Dumocrats to help in their Michigan Campaign for the United States Senate against Mike Rogers, has just ENDORSED Mike Rogers for Senate!”

open image in gallery ‘It’s a thing called bravery, and few people have it like just displayed by Congresswoman Haley Stevens!’ ( @realdonaldtrump, Truth Social )

“Haley said what few people are willing to say,” he continued. “She showed great and almost unprecedented loyalty to the Great People of Michigan with what she did. It’s a thing called bravery, and few people have it like just displayed by Congresswoman Haley Stevens!”

Trump has endorsed Rogers and repeatedly attacked El-Sayed, the Michigan-born son of Egyptian immigrants, as a “violent jihadist,” urging voters to “send him back to where he came from.”

El-Sayed, who is locked in a tight race with Rogers, brushed off his former opponent’s endorsement while speaking to reporters at a Detroit church Sunday.

“None of this matters,” he said, turning instead to the cost-of-living struggles facing Michigan residents.

open image in gallery Tensions between the Stevens and El-Sayed had simmered for months, particularly over Israel ( Getty Images )

Stevens, a centrist, lost by just one percentage point to progressive El-Sayed in August’s Democratic Senate primary.

Last month, she told CNN she would vote for El-Sayed, who has campaigned on removing money from politics and passing Medicare for All.

“I’m the weirdest loser in this country, okay? That Senate [primary] race was months ago. I hugged it out. Of course I’m voting for our Democratic nominee for Senate,” Stevens told the outlet.

But tensions between the former rivals had simmered for months, particularly over Israel. El-Sayed has called for the U.S. to stop funding Israel’s military and described its actions in Gaza as genocide. Stevens has rejected that characterization and voted against an amendment that sought to block funding for Israel.

open image in gallery On Friday, El-Sayed’s campaign reportedly asked Stevens to steer clear of all future campaign events ( Getty Images )

Stevens had also publicly urged El-Sayed to distance himself from streamer Hasan Piker, whose controversial comments include saying Hamas is “a thousand times better” than Israel and that “America deserved 9/11.”

The dispute escalated Friday when Stevens released a statement demanding that El-Sayed apologize for his comments about Israel and condemn an ad from an outside group that she described as antisemitic.

Politico later reported that his campaign had asked her to stay away from all future campaign events. She should steer clear “as not to distract from the central issues of the campaign,” one source familiar with the matter said.

The two had been scheduled to appear together Sunday, two days before Election Day. Instead, Stevens appeared alongside Rogers at a Detroit church before releasing her video statement.

After losing the August primary, Stevens is set to leave Congress in 2027.

News.title: Kimi Antonelli crowned F1 world champion after third-place finish in Mexico
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest Formula One world champion in history by clinching the title with third place at an action-packed Mexican Grand Prix.

Aged just 20 years and 68 days, Antonelli’s extraordinary march to the crown in his second season in the sport was completed under the Mexico City sun.

He only needed to finish ninth to get over the line but the Italian vowed to finish the job in style. He had to settled for a podium, as he became the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

open image in gallery

Lewis Hamilton ended a 1,197-day wait for pole on Saturday, pipping George Russell – the Britons the only drivers who could have prevented the coronation had Antonelli failed to score.

Max Verstappen claimed a sixth win in Mexico, as he fought off Hamilton at a second race start to clinch a third victory in four races and jump to second in the standings – 119 behind Antonelli.

Hamilton was furious after a first-lap scuffle with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc. Antonelli passed Leclerc to finish on the podium, with Lando Norris fifth ahead of Russell.

After a debut season where Antonelli struggled, even raising doubts as to whether he would complete it, few would have backed him to storm to the championship in the manner he has – with four rounds remaining.

Mercedes delivered the grid’s dominant car but team-mate Russell was heavy title favourite.

Antonelli responded to Russell’s opening win in Melbourne, with his maiden F1 success in China kickstarting a winning run of five races that gave him a title lead he has never looked like relinquishing.

As the Day of the Dead celebrations raged across town, F1 gave birth to its latest champion – the curly-haired kid from Bologna etching his name alongside the sport’s immortals.

open image in gallery

He has surpassed the mark of youngest champion by a staggering three years and 65 days ahead of previous record-holder Sebastian Vettel.

Hamilton, who Antonelli was chosen to replace at Mercedes, was three years and 39 days older than the Italian when he won the first of his seven crowns.

Antonelli’s thumping win in Austin last weekend – a sizzling demonstration of his champion credentials – made Sunday’s blast around the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez far more routine.

The 20-year-old arrived on Sunday hand in hand with younger sister Maggie and, with mum Veronica and dad Marco here, the Antonellis were ready to celebrate.

open image in gallery Antonelli arrives with his sister Maggie (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

He jumped into his car, after a hug from engineer Pete ‘Bono’ Bonnington and a kiss from mum, and set off from fourth on the grid to drive into the history books.

Hamilton started well to fend off Russell but Leclerc, from third, elbowed his way into the lead around the outside at turn four. He had to run over the grass to do so and Hamilton was sent wobbling, allowing Verstappen to move through.

“Pushed out by my own team-mate,” Hamilton fumed.

Russell plummeted to sixth and banged into Isack Hadjar but, while the carnage raged around him, Antonelli kept his nose clean to remain fourth.

Leclerc was hit with a five-second penalty. Hamilton grumbled: “He should just give the positions back.”

open image in gallery Hamilton was furious after an early coming together with Leclerc (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

There was worse news for Russell, now running fifth, who was slapped with a 10-second penalty for his bash into Hadjar.

Hamilton’s anger continued, saying: “The stewards are basically handing Charles this win.”

Leclerc had almost a five-second lead on Verstappen when the pair pitted after 27 laps, the Dutchman emerging ahead once the penalty was served. Hamilton stopped the next lap, rejoining 3.3 seconds behind Leclerc.

Antonelli now led and extended his first stint until lap 44. He rejoined fourth.

The following lap, Valtteri Bottas thumped into the barriers, triggering a safety car. Replays showed his front-left suspension failed down the straight.

Unlucky timing for Antonelli. “Ah f**k, man,” he moaned.

open image in gallery A performer dressed for Dia de los Muertos in Mexico City (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Hamilton pitted but the race was then red-flagged as the barriers needed repair. “We’ve got big problems, man,” Hamilton, who was promoted ahead of Antonelli again, said before storming into the Ferrari garage.

If Antonelli was feeling any nerves, a 33-minute halt and a second race start with 25 laps to go was enough to put them to the test – while the warring Ferraris were abreast again.

A fired-up Hamilton blasted past Leclerc off the line before banging wheels with Verstappen, the Dutchman staying ahead.

Leclerc locked up and was under-fire from Antonelli as the Italian pulled off a daring move to charge through. It was an overtake fitting of a world champion.

There was still time for more anxiety, Arvid Lindblad and Oscar Piastri crashing to trigger a safety-car restart, which Antonelli navigated.

The Foro Sol stadium erupted as Antonelli drove through on the final lap, triggering a fiesta to welcome in the history-making champion.

News.title: Kimi Antonelli cherishes ‘a day I will remember forever’ as he makes history
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kimi Antonelli cherished a “day I will remember forever” as he claimed his place in history as Formula One’s youngest world champion.

Aged just 20 years and 68 days, Antonelli’s extraordinary march to the crown in his second season in the sport was completed under the Mexico City sun.

He needed to finish only ninth to secure the crown and showed composure beyond his years to navigate a chaotic race, coming home third to become the first Italian champion since 1953.

A tearful Antonelli roared “we did it” over the radio before pulling up his Mercedes in the middle of the raucous Foro Sol Stadium, jumping out of the car and into the arms of his jubilant parents and younger sister Maggie.

open image in gallery Kimi Antonelli celebrates with his family after winning the world championship (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Antonelli joined Mercedes as a 12-year-old and the Silver Arrows’ protege, long-since lauded as a generational talent, realised his destiny by sealing a stunning championship win with four rounds remaining.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff greeted Antonelli with a huge bear hug.

“I would not be here without Mercedes or my family. I am speechless, trying to process what just happened,” Antonelli said.

“A day I will remember forever. So grateful, thank you so much. I am going to enjoy every bit.”

The race was won by Max Verstappen, with Lewis Hamilton second, meaning Antonelli shared the podium with two men who have 11 world championships between them.

There was a fitting moment as F1’s newest champion found himself on the shoulders of giants, Hamilton and Verstappen holding the young Italian aloft on the podium.

“I’m going to out with my family, friends and the team and we’re just going to enjoy all the way because this is a very special moment and one we will remember forever,” Antonelli added.

After a debut season where Antonelli struggled, even raising doubts as to whether he would complete it, few would have backed him to storm to the championship in the manner he has.

Father Marco, himself a former racing driver, has been by Kimi’s side throughout and thanked Mercedes for believing in his son.

“It’s unbelievable because after one year in Formula One with a lot of difficulties, arriving at this point and winning the title, there are no words to explain my satisfaction,” he told Sky Sports.

“It is very good for Mercedes as well because they believed in Kimi. It’s the best thank you Kimi can give to Mercedes for believing in him.”

News.title: Millions of popular coffee makers at Walmart, Target recalled after dozens burned
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Millions of Bodum French press coffee makers have been recalled after dozens of consumers reported burns, federal regulators announced recently.

The recall covers 5.9 million coffee makers across eight models with 8-cup and 12-cup replaceable glass carafes, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.

“The carafe can unexpectedly break during use if the glass carafe is damaged or cracked, including by use of a metal spoon to stir the coffee, posing a risk of serious burn injuries,” the commission said in a statement.

Bodum USA received 70 reports of carafes breaking, including 48 that resulted in burns to consumers.

“Consumers should stop using metal spoons or utensils to stir coffee in the glass carafe immediately and contact Bodum to receive a plastic Bodum stirring spoon and warning label,” the commission said.

open image in gallery The recall covers 5.9 million coffee makers across eight models with 8-cup and 12-cup replaceable glass carafes ( US Consumer Protection Safety Commission )

The coffee makers are manufactured in Thailand and Portugal and sold at Walmart, Target and home goods stores, as well as through online retailers including Amazon.com.

Bodum, a Danish-Swiss kitchenware company, was founded in 1944.

The Independent has contacted the company for comment.

News.title: The secrets behind Kimi Antonelli’s historic F1 triumph – and how Ferrari missed out on Italian superstar
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

It probably wasn’t quite how Kimi Antonelli envisaged his inaugural top-of-the-step moment. “Congratulations… Kimi Raikkonen!” bellowed long-time Formula 1 podium announcer Bob Constanduros, as the young Italian jumped onto the podium at the Shanghai International Circuit in March. Antonelli, the lad with a ruthless cutting edge intertwined with a feverishly boyish charm, gestured and laughed with his team down below.

While it was a comical blunder, comparisons to his namesake Finnish driver (sadly for this section, Antonelli’s middle name was not in tribute to Raikkonen) seem somewhat appropriate for the 20-year-old Italian who, on Sunday night, became the youngest Formula 1 world champion ever. Raikkonen, Ferrari’s last champion in 2007, was known as “The Iceman”, such was his cold, unflustered demeanour. And in just his second F1 season, Antonelli’s poise and serenity have been his biggest asset amid the season of his life.

Antonelli’s third-place finish in Mexico, off the back of his brilliant lights-to-flag victory in Austin last week, rather epitomised the Italian’s near-flawless campaign – and that of his forlorn Mercedes teammate, George Russell. While Antonelli made ground at the start in Mexico City, Russell dropped back and received a 10-second penalty after spinning Isack Hadjar. It rather summed up the Briton’s year.

open image in gallery Antonelli has not just beaten teammate George Russell this season but wiped the floor with him this year ( Getty )

A season which had Russell as the clear pre-season favourite – in the quickest car on the grid – has resulted in Toto Wolff’s Italian protege, the teen he trusted with filling Lewis Hamilton’s seismic boots, dominating the 2026 campaign.

And for Antonelli, it is a history-making achievement. At 20 years and 68 days, the Italian becomes the sport’s youngest-ever champion in its 76-year history, beating Sebastian Vettel’s previous record at 23 years of age. In quite the twist of fate, Antonelli was actually born on the same day that Vettel made his F1 race weekend debut in Turkey in August 2006.

Astonishingly, Antonelli also becomes Italy’s first world champion in 73 years, when the great Alberto Ascari won for Ferrari in 1963. Alongside multiple Grand Slam champion Jannik Sinner, he is now Italian sport’s biggest star.

His maturity, a year on from being in tears at Spa-Francorchamps after a disastrous qualifying performance, has been startlingly impressive, witnessed too by journalists up and down the paddock. At the season-opener in Australia, The Independent was present as Mercedes held a press event early on the first media day morning: the ultimate indication that a team is confident in their new car.

Typically with such events, there was a preamble before the driver Q&A: coffees, biscuits, small talk. Antonelli swooped over, shook every reporter’s hand and asked how their journey down under was, such was the Middle East travel chaos that had ensued days before. It’s the small details which stick in the memory of the sport’s travelling circus: Antonelli did similar at F1 75 Live last year in London, greeting members of the press room ahead of his rookie campaign. His affability, despite the no-holds-barred environment of Formula 1, is commendable and a credit to his parents, Marco and Veronica.

It was at three years old when Kimi told Marco that he wanted to try the racing simulator his father, an amateur racer in Italy who ran a racing team in nearby San Marino, had brought home. So the story goes: Kimi controlled the wheel, Marco the pedals.

Two years later, he started karting at a mini-bike track in Galliano Park in Forli, around an hour from his home in Bologna. At eight years old, he was scouted and signed to Minardi Management; at 12 in 2018 (the same year Russell won Formula 2), he signed onto Mercedes’ young driver programme.

open image in gallery Marco Antonelli has been alongside his son throughout his championship-winning year ( PA Wire )

Now the obvious question that hovers over the Emilia Romagna region: how did Ferrari, Italy’s team based in Maranello, 30 minutes away from Antonelli’s home, miss out on Italian motorsport’s next big thing? Then-team principal Maurizio Arrivabene insisted Antonelli was “too young” to be signed to an F1 team, despite a strong urge from Massimo Rivola, then-director of Ferrari’s Driver Academy. Mercedes did not need any invitation to swoop in themselves.

For a team like Ferrari, now notorious for questionable internal decision-making, that really does now look like an all-time fumble.

Yet Ferrari’s pain has proved to be Mercedes’ gain. Antonelli stormed through the junior ranks: from 2018 to 2022, he won an astonishing 18 different karting championships. His inevitable progression up to single-seater open-cockpit cars did not slow his ascent and, when he stormed to Formula Regional titles in the Middle East and Europe in 2023, Mercedes did not waste any time. Instead of the usual progression to Formula 3, Antonelli skipped that series and went straight into Formula 2.

By now, Wolff had a decision to make. Hamilton’s exit had left the Austrian executive on the back foot in the driver market and, when it became apparent that he couldn’t persuade Max Verstappen – the generational driver he always rued missing out on – to jump ship at Red Bull, Wolff ignored seasoned veterans of the sport and plumped for his own in-house generational talent.

It wasn’t a sure-fire thing as it now seems, though. Antonelli did not waltz through his F2 season, ultimately finishing sixth and winning just two races. Most memorably, he also smashed his Mercedes into the wall at Parabolica on his F1 race weekend debut in Monza, by which time it had already been decided that Antonelli would partner Russell in 2025.

“All good Kimi,” said a stunned Wolff in the garage. “All good.”

open image in gallery Antonelli was earmarked as a generational talent from an early age ( Getty )

open image in gallery Antonelli crashed in his first F1 practice session after just 10 minutes ( Getty )

Yet his on-the-limit driving, despite the costly repair work, was a sign of his killer instinct. And while his rookie F1 campaign ultimately had more downs than ups, this year’s generation of car – away from the ground-effect model which so suited Russell – alongside Mercedes’ newfound competitiveness at the top of the standings has given Antonelli a new lease of life.

Russell, in particular, has found his smoother driving style, breaking earlier with mid-corner speed, overheating these narrower tyres and leading to lower grip on a handful of tracks. Meanwhile, Antonelli, much like Hamilton this year, has taken to the 50/50 battery-engine combination with aplomb. While the likes of Verstappen and Lando Norris moaned about these questionable new cars, Antonelli kept his head down and worked with it. Throughout it all, he has eeked out every possible millisecond. It’s all about the margins.

And to win a championship, you need consistency. While Antonelli’s advantage in the last few weeks has been seismic, he has not waltzed to endless victories a la Max Verstappen in 2023. His standout statistic out of 19 rounds this year is not his wins (nine) but his podiums (16). Only twice has Antonelli finished outside the top five. Antonelli’s totting up of points has been relentless – and has not given Russell a sniff.

Of course, there have been standout moments: his win from pole in China (his first in Formula 1) set him on his way to five victories in a row, the last of which came at the sport’s crown jewel event in Monaco. Spa-Francorchamps in July too, perhaps the sport’s most dangerous circuit and where Antonelli toiled last year, saw the Italian absolutely dominate. Last year, the European summer season was a lesson learnt for the then-teen; 12 months on, Antonelli’s growth in stature and maturity was clear as day.

open image in gallery Antonelli was the first Italian to win at Monza since 1966 ( PA Wire )

open image in gallery Toto Wolff never wavered in his belief in Antonelli (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

But when the petrolheads look back on the 2026 campaign, Monza will be the flagship chapter. The Italian, who took an engine penalty, started at the back of the grid in 19th but stormed to the leading contenders by lap 13. Then, he gained 15 seconds over 21 laps on leader Russell and overtook him with a handful of laps remaining. The adoring tifosi, perhaps for the first time ever, celebrated wildly for a driver not decked in Ferrari red. And for Russell, it was a knockout blow.

And when the Briton’s engine failed at the end of the one-off round in Malaysia – it should be noted that Russell has not had any luck this year, with two DNFs costing him 40 points alone – it was virtually game over. Yet the margin extending to three figures in the last few weeks has been damaging for Russell, whose confidence is shot. And after Mexico, he has dropped behind Hamilton to third in the championship.

Yet on Halloween weekend in Mexico City, there were no Sunday scaries for Antonelli. With his father watching on proudly in the garage, there will be celebrations in the paddock though, bizarrely, team Mercedes are heading back to base in Brackley on Sunday night, turning down the temptation of a Mexican tequila bar.

But the next generation is now. At the start of the last regulation set, Verstappen stamped his authority and won four in a row. The more pertinent question now looms: how many world championships will Antonelli claim? With this era lasting until 2030, it could well be a very similar story.

News.title: Antonelli becomes youngest champion in F1 history as Verstappen wins Mexico City GP
News.content:
Welcome to our coverage for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. Today could be the day for Kimi Antonelli, the day he becomes a Formula One world champion. In fact it is very likely. All he needs to confirm the drivers’ championship is to finish ninth or higher. If George Russell or Lewis Hamilton do not claim victory then he is champion whatever happens. Given his season so far, it is difficult to see the title fight going to Brazil next week.

What chance of a decent race here today? The first few laps are often entertaining as the pack bunches up and there are plenty of chances to overtake early on. Generally the top four teams have been close together (last week in Austin excluded) and it is possible to overtake here, though it is not exactly easy.

Qualifying yesterday as an intriguing and close session. Hamilton secured his first grand prix pole for Ferrari, by just 0.009sec from the Mercedes of George Russell, with Charles Leclerc of Ferrari a little behind him in third. Then came Max Verstappen, Antonelli, Norris, Hadjar and Lindblad. Liam Lawson was disqualified on a technicality.

Ferrari have been an up-and-down team this season but have been strong without really delivering on it fully in the last few rounds. Could they secure a third victory of the season today? They do not really need to worry about losing second in the constructors to Red Bull or McLaren and Mercedes are too far out of reach in any case.

In any case, the biggest story is likely to be Antonelli’s coronation in Mexico. Hamilton has won titles here before for Mercedes, will the Italian give the Silver Arrows another fiesta in Mexico City? The race starts at 8pm GMT and we will be here for all the build-up, live updates and reaction from it.

News.title: Mikel Arteta’s smash-and-grab ends Arsenal’s 14-year Anfield hoodoo
News.content:
Arsenal’s version of the Yellow Wall (in their away shirts) was, indeed, hugely impressive – it is now six clean sheets from their nine league games and, despite all their pressure, Liverpool did not have a shot on target. That has never happened in the Premier League since such statistics started to be compiled in 2003 (422 games ago).

“That’s incredible. It did not feel like it on the pitch. Again, it’s the commitment of every single player,” Arteta said. And that was indisputable.

Even the expected second-half momentum, the expected surge of attack after attack as Liverpool faced the Kop, crashed on Arsenal’s backline. The visitors were so well-drilled that they stifled space – they refused to crumble.

Arsenal put their bodies on the line with blocks and tackles and a bit of time-wasting. There were dark arts, especially from both centre-halves with Gabriel going unpunished after claiming he was struck in the face by Isak early on – VAR anyone? – and the otherwise outstanding Ezri Konsa throwing himself to the ground after minimal contact from the Liverpool centre-forward.

In fairness there was also a bit of that from an increasingly frustrated Liverpool with Alexis Mac Allister going down after touching heads with Noni Madueke, having already tried to provoke Martin Odegaard with a hand to the head when the Arsenal captain was on the turf. That was not good from Mac Allister either.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton becomes oldest driver to claim pole position in 44 years
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, obviously. The big story this weekend is that Jimi Antonelli is almost certain to become the youngest world champion in Formula One history. To guarantee it he needs just two points, but if George Russell or Lewis Hamilton fail to win here then the title is his whatever he does. It has been a superb, strong and consistent season from the man who began the year as a teenager. He has not quite been faultless, but he has not been far away.

There are other stories floating around the paddock, too. Notably, Esteban Ocon has been dropped by Haas today for final practice, qualifying and the race, to be replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the weekend. Whether Ocon will continue in any other races has yet to be confirmed but you have to say that it seems extremely unlikely. More on that later.

Another line is the ongoing tension between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen after their crash in FP2 yesterday. It was certainly a strange one in which neither driver backed down, which resulted in contact, debris being strewn across the track and a red flag. Both drivers seemed unrepentant, though admitted it was clumsy. Lawson and Verstappen each receive a one-place grid penalty for the incident, which feels about right given how silly and unnecessary it all was.

But what about the competitive order on track? Since the summer break, and a little before in fairness, things have been unpredictable at the top. Mercedes have still, on average, been the best team but Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren have all had their moments.

What happened in final practice? It was Lando Norris who topped the timesheets by just 0.001sec ahead of Mercedes’ Antonelli. Charles Leclerc was a further tenth or so back for Ferrari followed by Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren, who was 0.195sec off his team-mate’s pace. Then came Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Isack Hadjar, Lawson and Arvid Lindblad. All drivers were within 0.6sec off Norris, which promises a close qualifying session. Let’s hope we get it.

News.title: Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points
News.content:
Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

News.title: Alex Mitchell injury blow for England but Northampton dig deep to win
News.content:
England were dealt a fresh blow ahead of their Nations Championship opener with Australia after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off early in Northampton’s victory over Gloucester.

Mitchell left the field gingerly 20 minutes into the action after picking up a suspected hamstring injury following an innocuous coming-together with Gloucester winger Will Joseph.

The Saints scrum-half has suffered a series of hamstring issues this year – this would be a fourth time he has picked up a problem – and he looked visibly disappointed as he limped off.

He suffered a left leg hamstring tear during England’s Six Nations defeat to Ireland which left him sidelined for two months and, in a cruel twist of fate, sustained another on his right leg during an England three-day training camp in Bagshot last May. He suffered the injury for a third time in England’s 73-8 rout of Fiji in July.

With Mitchell’s club-mate, Archie McParland, nursing an unspecified knock that forced him to miss Saints’ high-stakes clash with Gloucester, Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies next Sunday. McParland was the third-choice scrum-half in England’s Nations Championship squad, but Steve Borthwick may be forced to look elsewhere if Mitchell’s prognosis is serious.

News.title: Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

News.title: Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City
News.content:
This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

News.title: Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick
News.content:
The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

Sports.title: ‘I don’t forget’ – Piero Hincapie aims dig at Virgil van Dijk after Arsenal’s win at Liverpool as fans hail ‘petty king’
Sports.content:
Next

PIERO HINCAPIE appeared to aim a cheeky dig at Virgil van Dijk after Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0.

Kai Havertz‘s 13th minute strike was enough to earn the Gunners their first win at Anfield since 2014.

Hincapie, 24, came on as an 84th minute substitute for Christos Tzolis to help see out the victory.



After the match, the Ecuadorian posted pictures from the contest to his Instagram page, captioned: “I don’t forget..”



Initially, the carousel appeared to include a close up image of the gold Premier League badge on his shirt sleeve, denoting Arsenal‘s status as champions.

This appeared to be a jab at Virgil van Dijk, who posted a similar picture of himself after Liverpool’s 0-0 draw at the Emirates in January.

Arsenal fans loved Hincapie’s post, with one calling him a “petty king”.



While a second jibed: “What goes around, comes around.”

A third gushed: “I like how petty we are”.

Although another added: “One is a UCL winner, the other one can’t say”.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The picture of Hincapie’s sleeve mysteriously vanished from the post within a couple of hours.



Declan Rice commented on the post with a smiling emoji.

And Ezri Konsa added two flame emojis and a heart.

Hincapie’s post swiftly received more than 100,000 likes.

Arsenal’s win saw them return to the top of the Premier League table.

The Gunners are three points clear of Manchester City, after Enzo Maresca‘s side lost 1-0 to Brighton on Saturday.

Sports.title: ‘Embarrassing’ – Carragher blasts Mac Allister for ‘joke’ falling theatrics vs Arsenal and demands ‘this has to stop’
Sports.content:
Next

JAMIE CARRAGHER launched a scathing attack on Alexis Mac Allister after trying to get Noni Madueke sent off.

The Argentine, 27, could not stop Liverpool falling to a 1-0 defeat against Premier League table-toppers Arsenal.



And Mac Allister was involved in a major flashpoint after sparking a huge bust-up.

The midfielder screamed at Martin Odegaard and tapped the back of the grounded Arsenal skipper’s head.



Mac Allister, who missed out on a new deal in the summer, then threw himself to the floor when Madueke’s head brushed his.

But Carragher blasted the former Brighton man after attempting to reduce Arsenal to ten men.



The Anfield legend, 48, told Sky Sports: “I want Liverpool to win the game, but I’m delighted he [Madueke] didn’t get sent off.

“We have really got to be calling people out and saying, ‘this is embarrassing’.

“It’s ridiculous and it’s got to stop. I can’t stand it. If someone puts their head back and butts, then it’s a red card.

“But if it’s head-to-head and they touch, the other one goes down and the player gets sent off, as a game, call your own people out on it.

“It’s a joke from Mac Allister and it’s got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they can and red cards are being given for it.

“Whether it’s [ProRef supremo] Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers getting together, this has got to stop.”

Ex-Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge, 37, also hit out at Mac Allister’s shock theatrics.

He said: “He doesn’t headbutt him with any force. It’s a coming together and they’re both into it.

“He’s trying to bait him and that is league wide – that’s not just Mac Allister. Every player in world football – that’s the game.



“He knew exactly what he was doing and ultimately it didn’t work out for him. You tried to bait a man into something and he didn’t bite.”

Ian Wright, who joined Carragher and Sturridge on Sky Sports punditry duties, called for changes to be made in an attempt to stop stars trying to get opponents sent off.

The iconic Arsenal marksman, 62, added: “The first thing with Mac Allister is the way he goes over. He’s actually slapped Odegaard on the back of the head.

“The laws have to do something about this because that [Mac Allister going down] is trying to get someone sent off.”

SunSport refereeing expert Mark Halsey reckons Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni was lucky to avoid being red carded.

Sports.title: ‘He doesn’t know how to shoot’ – Heartwarming moment Mbappe comforts young fan struck in face by teammate’s wayward shot
Sports.content:
Next

KYLIAN MBAPPE has shared a heartwarming moment with a child hit by a teammate’s wayward shot.

The Real Madrid star took a moment to comfort the child after being accidentally targeted by a shot from Aurelien Tchouameni, 26, against Racing Santander.



Huge concern was raised for the young Racing fan by supporters after he was hit in the face by the ball during the 51st minute of the match.

Mbappe, 27, had already scored an 11th-minute penalty before further goals from Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande confirmed the 3-0 away win.



But the France captain was keen to make amends on his teammate’s behalf after the match.

He spent a moment in the tunnel with the youngster, explaining to the child on Real Madrid TV that Tchouameni needs to work on his accuracy.



Mbappe said: “It’s Tchouaméni’s fault.

“He doesn’t know how to shoot.”

The child appeared in good spirits as he shook hands with the Real Madrid striker.

Mbappe then shared a high-five with the child and ruffled his hair before walking away.

It has come just days after the Frenchman fell agonisingly short as Bayern Munich‘s Harry Kane claimed his first Ballon d’Or.

This left Spanish broadcasters stunned as Mbappe missed out on the title by just 41 points.

The Real Madrid star was then slammed for disrespecting Kane at the ceremony, as he appeared to ignore the England captain.

But Mbappe has let his on-pitch form do the talking for him as he helped Real Madrid cruise to a sixth straight win, rising to third in LaLiga.

Sports.title: Kai Havertz makes Premier League HISTORY as Arsenal star nets winning goal at Liverpool to end 14-year Anfield hoodoo
Sports.content:
Next

KAI HAVERTZ became the outright top-scoring German in Premier League history by bagging Arsenal’s winner at Liverpool.

The Gunners forward, 27, swept home Declan Rice‘s pass to hand his side a 1-0 lead on 13 minutes at Anfield.



Havertz’s goal was his 46th in 172 Prem appearances since moving to England in 2020.

It took him above compatriot Ilkay Gundogan‘s tally of 45, which previously was the record for a German player in the Premier League.



Gundogan, 36, achieved his haul in 221 appearances across two spells at Manchester City.

Havertz initially moved to Chelsea in 2020 as more of a midfield player.



The rangy star was eventually moved into a makeshift forward role and performed the role for the Blues as well as Arsenal.

Havertz scored 19 Prem goals in three seasons at Chelsea before signing for the Gunners in a £65million switch in June 2023.

He has since gone to add a further 27 to date for the Gunners.

Havertz’s best tally of Prem goals in a season thus far came during the 2023-24 campaign, when he managed 13 for Arsenal.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In third place on the leaderboard of German Premier League scorers is Brighton star Pascal Gross.

The creative midfielder has scored 34 goals in 256 appearances in two stints with the Seagulls.

Gross, now 35, initially moved to the Amex in 2017 ahead of their maiden Prem campaign under Chris Hughton.



He signed for Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2024, only to return to Brighton 18 months later.

Gross’ tally is one above Mesut Ozil’s of 33 – achieved in 184 appearances for Arsenal between 2013 and 2021.

The former Real Madrid star was also a prolific assister, laying on 57 Prem goals for his Gunners team-mates.



Uwe Rosler and Jurgen Klinsmann are next up with 29 apiece.

Klinsmann managed his haul in 56 games across two spells with Tottenham.

The legendary striker bagged 20 during the 1994-95 season after moving to White Hart Lane from Monaco.

After two seasons at Bayern Munich and a short stint with Sampdoria, Klinsmann returned to White Hart Lane on loan in the 1997-98 campaign, scoring nine times in 15 games to help save his beloved Spurs from the drop.



Rosler, meanwhile, scored his 29 goals during three seasons at Manchester City between 1993 and 1996 – including 15 in the 1994-95 campaign.

He would also go on to play 23 times in the Prem for Southampton, but did not score for the Saints.

Leroy Sane bagged 25 times in 90 Premier League outings for Man City.

The winger helped City to league titles in the 2017-18 and 2018-19 campaigns, scoring 10 times in each.



Sane moved to Bayern Munich in 2020 and now, aged 30, plays for Galatasaray in Turkey.

Brentford‘s Kevin Schade has 24 goals in 111 appearances for the Bees since joining from Freiburg in 2023 – and aged 24, seems likely to add many more.

Robert Huth is a surprise name at No9 on the list with 21 goals from 322 Prem outings.



Huth, now 42, won three Premier League titles during his career; two with Chelsea and memorably one with Leicester City.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His best season tally came in 2010-11, when he managed six for Stoke under Tony Pulis.

Rounding off the list is Lukas Podolski, the left-footed forward scoring 19 times in 60 matches for Arsenal between 2012 and 2015. Podolski, now 41, retired from football earlier this year following a spell in Poland.

Sports.title: Man Utd fans beg former star, 34, to rejoin club and rescue Michael Carrick after signing THREE dud replacements
Sports.content:

MANCHESTER UNITED fans have made a desperate plea for Casemiro to seal a sensational return.

But frustrated United supporters are begging for the five-time Champions League winner to make a shock comeback and rescue their season.



The Red Devils extended their winless streak to NINE games as they suffered a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday.

United fans flooded the comments section when Casemiro uploaded a snap onto social media promoting Inter Miami’s clash with New England Revolution.

One said: “Please come back to United.”

Another added: “You’re dearly missed.”

A third cheekily asked: “Any chance of a two-month loan to get us to 12-18 points?”

A fourth chimed in: “Casemiro please come back to United. They need you.”

Sheehan told SunSport: “Working with Wales, with Craig and the staff, has given me the bug to really get back into it.

Sheehan explained: “I spent time visiting clubs right across the continent to see how different cultures operate.



“I’ve started learning different languages’ just to add another string to my bow.

Sports.title: Three points from Arsenal’s win at Liverpool, including Saliba’s Konsa issue, Rice’s remedy and tactical dilemma
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL secured a huge win against Liverpool on the road to leap to the top of the Premier League table.

Mikel Arteta‘s men took the lead through Kai Havertz in the early stages of the match before weathering a barrage of Reds pressure to protect their three points.



A number of Gunners stars stood out in the thrilling clash at Anfield, but that is not to say there were not signs to learn and improve upon as the season rumbles on.

SunSport’s Simon Collings singled out three things we learned from Arsenal‘s triumph on Merseyside…



KONSA-QUENCES

The defence was at the heart of Arsenal‘s performance as they stole all three points at Anfield for the first time in 14 years.

Ezri Konsa put in a stunning performance alongside Gabriel at the base of the back four as he continues to build on his impressive catalogue of showings since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.

William Saliba is potentially set to make his return to contention in the coming weeks, and could be available for selection as early as after the November international break.

But the Frenchman faces a fight if he wants to reclaim his spot in the starting line-up.

Konsa has built up his relationship with his defensive partner this season, and deciding whether to split them up may prove a real dilemma for Arteta in the near future.

THINK RICE

Declan Rice continued to impress in midfield as he put the ball on a plate for Havertz at the back post to give the Gunners an early lead.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

That made it five assists for the season so far for Rice, who is adding a creative spark to his repertoire of skills this campaign.

But the impactful showing comes on the back of him receiving a rest in the midweek.

The quality of his performance at Anfield is proof that Arteta will have to carefully manage his minutes going forward this season so he can make the difference in the biggest clashes.

RACE FOR PACE

But while the back line and the midfield shone, there was a glaring issue at the other end of the pitch.



Liverpool had the visitors pinned back for large spells in the second half, but Arsenal lacked the pace up front to provide a danger on the counter attack.

The absence was especially stark watching the likes of Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak bombing down the channels for the hosts when they regained possession.

Arsenal were unable to exploit the space behind Liverpool’s back line when they cranked up the pressure in the defensive third, but a pace injection in the January window could make them a real danger on the counter.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk blasts VAR as Liverpool captain goes public after Arsenal penalty denial
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk blasts VAR as Liverpool captain goes public after Arsenal penalty denial

After Liverpool were beaten by Arsenal at Anfield, Virgil van Dijk let his feelings about the game's officiating be known

View 3 Images Virgil van Dijk did not hold back in his assessment of the referees (Image: X/Sky Sports Premier League)

Virgil van Dijk hit out at VAR in a prickly post-match interview after Liverpool's defeat to Arsenal. The Premier League champions overcame the Reds 1-0, courtesy of Kai Havertz's first half goal

‌



‌



Andoni Iraola's side were left furious when they saw two first half penalty shouts be waved away by both referee Andy Madley and VAR. The most controversial call came when Jurrien Timber grabbed Alexander Isak by his shirt while the £125m man was trying to get on the end of a dangerous cross from Bradley Barcola.

‌



Gary Neville believed it was a penalty and was left aghast when Isak did not even shout or protest the decision. After the match, Van Dijk blasted the officials operating VAR.

‌



When the incident was put to Van Dijk, he told Sky Sports: "It was a clear penalty on Isak. It’s a penalty but today it wasn’t meant to be.”

The reporter then asked if Isak should have protested the decision to alert the referee about the incident, Van Dijk hit back with some questions of his own, asking: "VAR doesn’t notice it?

"There are 50 cameras. Why does he have to complain when there’s so many cameras? Everyone has seen it. At the end of the day, it wasn’t given so congratulations to Arsenal.”

‌



View 3 Images Isak was pulled back by Timber as he looked to get on the end of a cross (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher was equally furious about the decision, saying VAR did not do what it was brought in to do. He said: "One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR do your job."

‌



Iraola also used his post-match media duties to event about some of the key decisions, saying the striker may have needed to dive to get the call. The Reds boss said: "There is a clear grab [of] the shirt.

"Alex [Isak] was just in front of him, he was going to head in front of the goal but couldn't because he had the shirt. I don't understand why they didn't call it, probably because he has not gone to the floor.

‌



View 3 Images Iraola spent much of the match protesting the decisions which went against his team (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

"I think the Gakpo one was not a penalty but the Alex one he was going to head the ball in front of the goalkeeper.

‌



"He grabbed the shirt. I don't understand why it wasn't called. You have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it. That's the problem we have with the game. Because he doesn't dive and go to the floor.

"The fact that you are even asking me if he should go to the floor, if he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100 percent."

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher fumes at Alexis Mac Allister and demands law change over 'embarrassing' act
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher fumes at Alexis Mac Allister and demands law change over 'embarrassing' act

Alexis Mac Allister's brazen attempt to get Noni Madueke sent off in the closing stages of Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool on Sunday infuriated Jamie Carragher

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister went down after going head to head with Noni Madueke (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has slammed Alexis Mac Allister for his "embarrassing" dive to try and get Noni Madeuke sent off - and called for unified action against play-acting.

‌



‌



Mac Allister was at the centre of a flashpoint in the second half of Liverpool's 1-0 defeat by Arsenal on Sunday afternoon. The Liverpool midfielder sparked a melee by slapping Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard on the back of the head while he was on the ground.

‌



Jurrien Timber and Madueke then confronted Mac Allister, who threw himself to the ground dramatically after a minor contact with the latter's forehead. Madueke had already been booked, but the officials weren't fooled, with Mac Allister and Timber given yellow cards by referee Andy Madley.

‌



The VAR Stuart Attwell said: "There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal”.

‌



Carragher was furious with Mac Allister's behaviour and called for it to be stamped out of the game. "I'm delighted he didn't get sent off there," he said after the full-time whistle on Sky Sports. "We have really got to be strong and start calling people out and say 'this is embarrassing'. It's got to stop, it's ridiculous. I can't stand it.

"This head to head stuff... if someone puts their head back and butts, of course, red card. But this stuff where they go head to head and if someone touches the other goes down and the player gets sent off... as a game, people in the Premier League, supporters, call your own out for it.

‌



"I'm a Liverpool fan and it's a joke from Mac Allister, it's got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they know they can, because red cards are getting given for it. Whether it's from Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers get together, stop getting red cards for this c***!"

View 2 Images Noni Madueke went head to head with Alexis Mac Allister before he dived

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Carragher was backed up by Gary Neville on co-commentary. "I don't think Mac Allister needs to go down like that but there's a little nudge with the head. A little inch forward can cost you a lot," he said while watching the incident play out.

‌



"Mac Allister's reaction is a bit over the top, I can tell you that. Get up. Embarrassing. It's Mac Allister's fault because he slaps Odegaard when he's down which is unnecessary.

"It's the little movement forward of Madueke's head they're looking at. I hope they don't go for a red card for it."

‌



Arsenal legend Ian Wright also called for the laws of the game to be changed to clarify these types of situations. "The first thing with Mac Allister is the way he goes over. He's actually slapped Odegaard on the back of the head," he said.

"The laws have to do something about this because that [Mac Allister going down] is trying to get someone sent off. Common sense prevailed because he [Madueke] didn't push his head into him, he just confronted him and Mac Allister tried to take that advantage to go down."

Sports.title: Arsenal aren't winning over neutrals but Mikel Arteta won't care after brave Liverpool display
Sports.content:
Arsenal aren't winning over neutrals but Mikel Arteta won't care after brave Liverpool display

Arsenal put on a defensive masterclass to snuff out the threat from Liverpool and finally get a win at Anfield. It was the kind of performance that title wins are built upon

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta celebrated a rare win at Anfield (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta will not win any popularity contests playing like this, but Arsenal might just win another title with such brave, heroic victories after they frustrated the life out of Liverpool.

‌



‌



Incredibly, this was Arsenal’s first Premier League win at Anfield since 2012 when Arteta was playing himself.

‌



That is how tough Arsenal have found Liverpool in the past 14 years which is remarkable as it was the scene of their greatest ever night when they won the title back in 1989.

‌



But at the final whistle, the travelling Arsenal fans celebrated like they had just won the title again because they know what this victory will do for their belief and hope of retaining the Premier League.

Kai Havertz provided the story of redemption as he got the winner just days after his nightmare and hat-trick of misses at Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup. Declan Rice was one of a number of standout performances as Arsenal battled and gave everything until Liverpool simply ran out of ideas.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola can count himself so unlucky because they hit the bar, missed a hatful of chances themselves and really should have had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s clear shirt pull on Alexander Isak.

‌



But titles are built on a slice of luck and days like these. Arsenal now go clear at the top and, while they lack some stardust in attack, they have real guts and work rate everywhere else on the pitch. They dug in and, at the final whistle, the Liverpool fans booed loudly in frustration but probably with some deep down admiration for Arteta’s battlers.

Quite how Liverpool did not score is anyone’s guess. But how many times have opponents said that already this season? They have won eight out of nine games and kept six clean sheets.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Kai Havertz put Arsenal ahead with a tap-in early on (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



That is a tribute to Arsenal’s defence and the rock solid partnership of Ezri Konsa and Gabriel with David Raya marshalling the back line with Jurrien Timber and Riccardo Calafiori outstanding in the full-back roles.

Last month, Arsenal won at Nottingham Forest and the debate was whether that narrow 1-0 win was the mark of champions or just plain dull. But there can be no debate this time. Arsenal fought while Liverpool more than played their part in what was an epic clash.

‌



This was English football at its best. Hard fought, entertaining and, yes, we wanted more goals and entertainment but it was still incredibly engrossing. It was also some reaction by Arsenal after their midweek humiliation at Fleetwood and it was written in the stars that it had to be Havertz who was the hero.

Arsenal went ahead after 16 minutes and it was Odegaard who set the tone by chasing down a loose ball in midfield. Bruno Guimaraes and Noni Madueke combined nicely before Rice flashed a low ball across the face of goal. There was Havertz at the back post to steer home from a tight angle and the Germany striker duly celebrated by cupping his hands to his ears.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal were superb at Anfield (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

But from there, Liverpool absolutely battered Arsenal. They laid siege to the visitors’ goal. This was the ultimate test - and Arsenal passed it again. It was like the Alamo. Virgil van Dijk and Isak both went close. Liverpool should have had a penalty but somehow VAR cleared Timber’s clear shirt pull on Isak.

‌



Liverpool coach Pablo De La Torre, part of Iraola’s backroom staff, was booked for his protests as the entire bench leapt up in disgust. They had every right to be frustrated. It was clear.

Florian Wirtz’s free kick smashed the crossbar and then Alexis Mac Allister headed over a gilt-edged chance from point blank range. After their bright start, Arsenal had retreated and were clinging on.

Article continues below

Iraola rolled the dice with Dominik Szoboszlai and Rio Ngumoha. But, in truth, they ran out of ideas on how to break down Arsenal’s defence. It became desperate when Mac Allister threw himself down under the slightest touch from Madueke. That was embarrassing.

But now the Premier League table makes for good reading for Arteta.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher fumes over VAR as Liverpool penalty agreement reached - 'Do your job!'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher fumes over VAR as Liverpool penalty agreement reached - 'Do your job!'

Liverpool had strong shouts for a penalty waved away during their showdown with Arsenal

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher and the Sky Sports pundits gave their verdict on VAR's role in the Alexander Isak penalty decision (Image: Sky Sports)

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher was left fuming that the video assistant referee missed a penalty shout against Arsenal. Jurrien Timber avoided being penalised for a penalty for an apparent pull on Reds striker Alexander Isak as he looked to head the hosts level.

‌



‌



Bradley Barcola delivered a tantalising cross which narrowly missed the Sweden international, however replays showed the Dutch defender had pulled his shirt. Liverpool fell behind inside 20 minutes after Kai Havertz tapped home with the visitors pouncing on sloppy play out from the back from the Reds backline.

‌



However, after falling behind, Andoni Iraola's side surged back putting the Premier League champions under pressure. Yet, the half-time analysis focused on how Andy Madley missed out on awarding Liverpool a penalty and hand them the chance to level proceedings.

‌



Carragher said: “One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR do your job."

Gary Neville singles out 'embarrassing' Arsenal star minutes into Liverpool clash READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The former stopper was responding to Daniel Sturridge who felt that Liverpool would have had a stronger shout for a penalty if the Swede made more of a big deal about the tug. He said: “If he [Isak] makes more of it, it's a penalty. I don't think he makes enough of it... It's clear and blatant."

‌



Following the interval, Gary Neville felt the reaction was Isak was "odd". He said: "The guys at half-time said Isak should not have to make more of it [his penalty shout in the first half].

"It's actually unnatural not to make more of it. When you get pulled and you're just about to score, you ordinarily complain like crazy. It's a very odd reaction from Isak."

‌



Ian Wright was among the contingent to represent Arsenal as part of Sky Sports' coverage. But the former Gunners talisman couldn't ignore that the North London club got away with a key moment.

He said: “He shouldn't have to make more of it. We can see it. As an Arsenal man, I'm glad we got away with it.

‌



View 2 Images Andoni Iraola was left angered with the decision not to award Liverpool a penalty against Arsenal. (Image: Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

“Unless I'm pulled back, I'm going to head it as much as I can. When he pulled him, it was just about enough as he would need to go down."

‌



After Brighton & Hove Albion avenged their Carabao Cup exit at the hands of Manchester City in the midweek, the Seagulls dented Enzo Maresca's sides Premier League title hopes with a 1-0 win.

A win for Arsenal would open up the gap in their title defence to three points after City suffered back-to-back defeats in the top-flight, following their 2-1 disappointment at the hands of Aston Villa last week.

Sports.title: Boy, 14, turns himself in to the police after vile Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland game
Sports.content:
Boy, 14, turns himself in to the police after vile Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland game

West Midlands Police have released a statement to confirm that a 14-year-old boy has turned himself in following a vile incident during Coventry's win over Sunderland

View 3 Images The fan appeared to hold up a photo of Bradley Lowery (Image: x.com/Roker Report)

A 14-year-old boy has turned himself in to the police after footage appeared to show a young Coventry supporter taunting Sunderland fans with a picture of Bradley Lowery.

‌



‌



Footage taken during Coventry's 3-1 Premier League win over Sunderland posted on social media went viral on Saturday. It appeared to show a young supporter showing the away fans a photograph of Lowery, a Sunderland fan who tragically died aged six in 2017 with cancer.

‌



The video sparked outrage, with Bradley's mum Gemma releasing a statement, and West Midlands Police have now given a significant update.

‌



A spokesperson said: “We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland yesterday afternoon. A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”

‌



Coventry City said in a statement: "Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action."

Bradley, who had neuroblastoma, touched the hearts of football fans with his bravery and his mum Gemma released an emotional statement on Sunday morning following the disgusting incident.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Lowery was a passionate Sunderland fan (Image: PA)

She wrote: "My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate. Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

‌



"I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt."

She added: "We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter? I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were.

‌



View 3 Images Bradley Lowery died in 2017 (Image: PA)

“I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don't, just for him to learn from this. Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.

‌



"What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did. Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

"Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever. That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.

Article continues below

"So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents. My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. #CancerHasNoColours. That is how I want the world to remember him.”

Sports.title: Erling Haaland's true feelings on Man City future confirmed by dad after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's true feelings on Man City future confirmed by dad after guilty verdict

Manchester City are facing serious consequences for systematically breaking the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period, leaving players like Erling Haaland in an uncertain position

View 2 Images Alfie Haaland discussed his son's reaction to the guilty verdict (Image: Viaplay)

Erling Haaland is purely focused on playing for Manchester City and is not concerned by the possible punishment the club faces, according to his father Alfie.

‌



City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period and are waiting the outcome of an appeal. An independent commission found the club guilty of 114 of the 115 charges, saying they had used "sham" contracts to disguise funding of more than £830million.

The club have always maintained their innocence and are confident of clearing their name. But the bombshell verdict has cast a shadow of doubt over Enzo Maresca's side, who could be relegated as punishment for the club's past financial cheating.

Haaland has reportedly been calming his teammates down about the potential consequences and his father has given an insight into the striker's mindset. "Erling thinks about playing as much football as he can and concentrates on that. I think it’s more those of us outside the pitch who think a bit more about it," Alfie told ViaPlay.

"Well, it has been circulating for quite a while, hasn’t it? So finally something came that was concrete, which it is possible to fight against for City as a club.

"Obviously, these are serious allegations, but now there is an appeal case pending to be heard, so I think we have to stay calm, keep our cool, and wait to see how it turns out."

Haaland Snr was then asked whether he felt it would be unfair to punish the current players over financial irregularities which happened between 2009 and 2018. He replied: "Yes, in a way, one might feel that having to potentially take punishment for something done many years ago… yes, I would say so."

View 2 Images Erling Haaland could be relegated with Manchester City due to the guilty verdict (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Asked if he knew anything more about the appeal, Alfie said: "Nothing more than what’s in the media. And there is an awful lot written there, and very one-sided, I would say, right? Because it's hard for Manchester City to come out right now – with an ongoing appeal – and defend themselves.

"So we hope they get a fair hearing, and then we’ll see if they manage to prove that they are innocent, eventually. Now we just have to wait and see. I think they’ve done more than well to stand tall through this, because of course they have faced plenty of accusations. So I feel the player group has handled it very well.

"We also have to remember that these are things that allegedly happened quite a few years ago. The players today had nothing to do with it. So they’ve played well. They lost their last match, so it’s time to get back to winning ways."
