Sports.title: Premier League stars warned as homes of three stars burgled while playing
Sports.content:
Premier League stars warned as homes of three stars burgled while playing

Everton striker Thierno Barry was relieved that his family was not home during the latest raid. Man Utd captain Bruno Fernandes and England star Morgan White-Gibbs were also targeted by burglars in recent weeks

View 4 Images Bruno Fernandes saw his home ransacked by masked robbers during Manchester United's 4-1 loss to Como last month (Image: Adam Davy/Press Association)

Premier League footballers have been warned to be extra vigilant after the homes of three stars were burgled while they were playing.

‌



‌



Everton striker Thierno Barry admitted that he was relieved that his family was not home during the latest raid.

‌



His warning came after Man Utd captain Bruno Fernandes and England star Morgan White-Gibbs were both targeted in a matter of weeks.

‌



Barry's Greater Manchester home was burgled last week.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Everton's Thierno Barry spoke out after his home was targeted as he played against Newcastle United (Image: Peter Byrne/Press Association)

‌



Donald Trump dealt stinging legal defeat over Epstein birthday book days from Midterms READ MORE :

The 24-year-old Frenchman said: "Things could have been much worse," as his partner and toddler were watching him against Newcastle United.

Barry admitted: "Maybe I've been too open about my family's life and mine, potentially putting them at risk.

‌



"It was all just to show my lifestyle and inspire others through my journey and success, hoping to motivate them to do the same.

"My childhood was never easy.

‌



"I've always believed that when you give yourself the best possible chances, there is always hope.

"Unfortunately, in life, there are people and things beyond our control.

‌



"This has been a lesson for me. The most important thing in life is to look after and protect the people you love. That's what truly matters. Everything else is just materialistic."

View 4 Images Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White was also targeted by burglars (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



His partner Charlene added: " If anyone has seen or heard anything suspicious, or has any information that could help, we would be incredibly grateful if you could get in touch.

"We are also willing to offer a financial reward for any information that helps identify those responsible.."

‌



The partner of Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White also spoke of their harrowing experience last week.

Britney De Villiers said: "Our home was burgled a few days ago and after hearing about another one, I feel it's important to warn others.

‌



"It's incredibly unsettling knowing that homes are being targeted. Please be extra vigilant, make sure your security systems are on whether you're in the house or not and report anything suspicious. "Thankfully, nobody was home when it happened and material things can be replaced but it's a horrible feeling knowing someone has violated your home, especially when you have young children.

"Please stay safe and look out for one another." Bruno Fernandes saw his home ransacked by masked robbers during Manchester United's 4-1 loss to Como last month.

‌



A Cheshire Police spokesperson said: "At around 8.30pm on Wednesday 21 October, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

‌



"Officers attended the scene, but upon arrival, there was no trace of the suspects.

"Officers discovered that a burglary had occurred at the address and several items were stolen."

‌



View 4 Images Jack Grealish was one of the stars targeted in the past by burglars (Image: Ian West/the Press Association)

Man City's £100m signing Jack Grealish, currently on loan to Everton, had £1m worth of jewellery and valuables taken in a raid in 2023.

‌



Former Man Utd star Victor Lindelof was also targeted.

The gang who targeted Grealish are also believed to be behind raids on Prem ace Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Love Island stars Molly Mae Hague and Tommy Fury. Dubbed them the “Balcony Burglars”, they use ladders to target balconies connected to the master bedrooms of each mansion.

‌



England ace Raheem Sterling raced back from the Qatar World Cup when raiders stole £350,000 worth of watches from his house. Lindelof's wife and two kids locked themselves in a panic room when their home was raided in January, 2022. Man City's Joao Cancelo was attacked by robbers in front of his wife at their property in the city weeks earlier.

Balconies were a favoured method of access as the raiders knew jewellery, watches and designer handbags were close by, with the raids carried out within minutes. Oxlade-Chamberlain and Little Mix singer Perrie Edwards were burgled by a gang at their £3.5m mansion in Wilmslow, Cheshire four years ago.

Article continues below

The couple, at home at the time, did not know they had been targeted until they discovered items of jewellery and handbags missing.

Sports.title: Defensive 'masterclass' and elite Rice - how Arsenal ended Anfield torment
Sports.content:
Not since 2012 - when current boss Mikel Arteta was commanding Arsenal's midfield on the pitch - had the Gunners won on Liverpool’s patch. That curse has finally been broken.

Winning at Anfield is a rarity, especially for Arsenal. But Arteta's side were ruthless at both ends of the pitch, a tactical triumph for the boss and one that underlines his side's champion mentality.

"I love when there is something that we haven't done for many years," beamed the Spaniard, who praised his players for a defensive performance he called "remarkable". If Arteta wanted to make a statement, he succeeded.

Despite being pinned back in a first half dominated by Liverpool pressure, the visitors restricted their hosts to zero accurate shots - the first time on record the Reds failed to land at least one attempt on target at home.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Liverpool and Arsenal.

"In the end, that defensive line, the way we stick together, that togetherness we have, is undefeated," midfielder Declan Rice reflected. "It's nothing I've ever seen before." Nine games in, Arsenal's title defence is going perfectly to plan.

Jamie Carragher was equally impressed by Arsenal's resilience: "To come to Anfield and be put under that much pressure and not have a shot on target from the opposition, or Liverpool not get a big chance given the money they have spent on their attack, is outstanding.

"When you think about Arsenal winning titles, especially in '89 and '91 with Tony Adams and that famous back four, I think we're getting close to putting this back four in that conversation."

Gary Neville called it a "defensive masterclass", likening Arsenal's nous to that of a side styled on Jose Mourinho's unique compactness.

The Gunners also won 18 fouls, Jurrien Timber, Martin Odegaard and Noni Madueke all responsible for drawing three apiece - a tactic used to stifle Liverpool's momentum. Ezri Konsa won all eight of the duels he contested.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Declan Rice sends a low cross across the box to the far post, where Kai Havertz delivers the finish to put Arsenal ahead against Liverpool.

Such application and exertion is what pleased Arteta most.

Under him, Arsenal have gone on to win 81 per cent of league games in which they have opened the scoring - the masters of preserving a lead.

He added: "Not only for the victory, but for the way we've done it, the spirit that we showed, the way we carried this shirt, this badge. It's a commitment of every single player in every action to deliver those kinds of stats.

"And that's the magical part about this game, that it can take you to really bad places, but four days later you have an incredible opportunity to do something historic, and we've done it."

'World-class Rice the best in Premier League'

Image: Declan Rice won player of the match for a standout performance at Anfield

While Carragher was impressed with the Gunners' collective effort on Super Sunday, he singled out Rice for particular commendation, calling him a "world class" talent.

The midfielder delivered one of his most complete performances of the campaign so far, providing the assist for Kai Havertz's winner and anchoring the middle third in a way that prime Arteta would be proud of.

He was the defensive shield Arsenal needed when Liverpool were generating a headwind and made crucial interceptions in the pressure moments.

His 62 touches were the most of any Arsenal player. "He's one of the best midfield players Arsenal have ever had," Carragher added.

"They've obviously had some great ones. He's right up there with the best of them. He's the best midfield player in the Premier League by a long way. It's not even a debate."

Sports.title: How Antonelli has rewritten Formula 1's record books
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has its 36th world champion after Kimi Antonelli clinched his maiden title by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The Italian youngster has reached the summit of motorsport in just his second season at the top level after a stellar campaign in which he has won nine races for Mercedes.

And while a world championship triumph for any driver is notable, Antonelli's first title carries particularly strong historical significance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix as Antonelli became the first Italian world champion since 1953

Beating Vettel's 16-year youngest benchmark

Formula 1 has a new youngest world champion in the sport's 76-year history.

After holding the record for 16 years, Sebastian Vettel spell as F1's youngest-ever champion has been beaten - by a full three years.

F1's youngest world champions Driver (season) Age 1) Kimi Antonelli (2026) 20 years and 68 days 2) Sebastian Vettel (2010) 23 years and 134 days 3) Lewis Hamilton (2008) 23 years and 300 days 4) Fernando Alonso (2005) 24 years and 58 days 5) Max Verstappen (2021) 24 years and 73 days

Vettel was aged 23 years and 134 days when he won the first of his four world titles with Red Bull in 2010. Antonelli clinched his maiden crown aged 20 years and 68 days, a record that may well stand for decades - if not, all time.

Antonelli also follows Jacques Villeneuve (1997) and Lewis Hamilton (2008) in winning his first F1 title in just his second season competing at motorsport's top level.

Ending Italy's seven-decade wait for another champion

Antonelli has also made history as an Italian driver in F1.

Considering an Italian won three of the first four Drivers' Championships following F1's inception in 1950, and Ferrari is the sport's most successful team, there had been a dearth of individual success in recent decades before Antonelli came along.

Antonelli is Italy's first world champion since 1953, when Alberto Ascari clinched his second and final title.

Italy's F1 world champions Driver Year Giuseppe Farina 1950 Alberto Ascari 1952, 1953 Kimi Antonelli 2026

Antonelli's nine wins this year have already put him second to Ascari (13) in the list of Italian race winners.

One of those wins came on home soil, at Monza in September, which made Antonelli the first Italian winner of the Italian Grand Prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

The other records Antonelli has beaten

While Max Verstappen's win as an 18-year-old at the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix remains the youngest for a driver in F1, Antonelli is the only driver to win multiple races as a teenager.

He won six races before his 20th birthday in August.

He did become the sport's youngest polesitter (China) and the youngest to lead the world championship (Japan) this year, along with the youngest to claim a pole-win-fastest lap hat-trick (China). He is also the youngest to achieve a Grand Slam - which requires a driver to add the lead of every race lap to a hat-trick - in Monaco.

In addition, he became the first driver to win his first five races in succession thanks to an unbeaten run from China to Monaco.

He was already the youngest driver to lead a race and claim a fastest race lap, feats he achieved as an 18-year-old in 2025.

Sports.title: Antonelli crowned world champion as Verstappen wins wild Mexico City GP
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history as Max Verstappen held off Lewis Hamilton to win a thrilling Mexico City Grand Prix.

Antonelli finished third to secure the F1 Drivers' Championship with four rounds to spare, becoming the first Italian world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

The 20-year-old avoided all the chaos in one of the most action-packed races of the season and was hugely emotional after the chequered flag.

"We did it, we did it. I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family, so I'm very grateful for this moment and it's one that will live forever," said Antonelli.

"I'm speechless. I'm trying to process what has just happened."

Youngest F1 world champions Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes - 20 years and 68 days (2026)

Sebastian Vettel, Red Bull - 23 years and 134 days (2010)

Lewis Hamilton, McLaren - 23 years and 300 days (2008)

Fernando Alonso,, Renault - 24 years and 58 days (2005)

Max Verstappen, Red Bull - 24 years and 73 days (2021)

Meanwhile, Verstappen took advantage of a big fight between the Ferraris of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on the opening lap to claim his third win in four races.

Pole-sitter Hamilton went side by side with Leclerc through the tight Turns 1 and 2 before Leclerc attacked again into Turn 4 around the outside.

Both drivers went off the track but Leclerc went across the grass to take the lead, allowing Verstappen to capitalise by overtaking Hamilton.

Leclerc was handed a five-second time penalty but a furious Hamilton said "the stewards are basically handling Charles this win" on the radio.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive a dramatic opening lap as Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was given a five-second penalty after overtaking Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the Mexico City Grand Prix

Verstappen crucially stayed within five seconds of Leclerc before the only round of pit stops to take the lead as they pitted together, but appeared to have an inferior car compared to the Ferraris, and was on aging soft tyres.

However, the race was stopped when Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas suffered a huge crash into the barriers as his suspension failed, leaving a standing-start restart with everyone on fresh tyres with 26 laps remaining.

Leclerc got a poor launch from second so Hamilton attacked Verstappen into Turn 1, with the pair making contact as the Red Bull driver came out on top in the exchange.

Even with a Safety Car for Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad crashing after tangling with McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Verstappen did just enough to keep Hamilton at bay with Antonelli, fittingly, just behind the two F1 legends in third.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Valtteri Bottas suffered a suspension failure in his Cadillac as he crashed heavily into the barriers during Sunday's race in Mexico City

Leclerc battled his way to fourth with flat-spotted front tyres from a lock up on the restart, while McLaren's Lando Norris finished fifth and Mercedes' George Russell sixth.

Russell had earlier served a 10-second time penalty for colliding with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar on the opening lap, which dropped him out of the podium fight.

Piastri was seventh ahead of Alpine's Franco Colapinto, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and the other Alpine of Pierre Gasly.

Britain's Oliver Bearman was in contention for points until Audi's Nico Hulkenberg ran into the back of him on the restart while his Haas team-mate and F1 debutant Ryo Hirakawa, who replaced Esteban Ocon from Saturday, was 13th.

Sports.title: Sale secures Grand Final title and Brown crowned Road to Mallorca No 1
Sports.content:
Julien Sale produced a dominant final round to secure victory at the HotelPlanner Tour’s Grand Final, while Hamish Brown topped the Road to Mallorca rankings.

Frenchman Sale, who was guaranteed promotion to the DP World Tour before the season finale in Mallorca, posted his second 65 of the week to reach 22 under par, four strokes clear of the Brown, who narrowly held onto solo second to capture the season-long title.

Sale ends the year second in the rankings and will now step up to golf's DP World Tour for the first time in his career.

He becomes the fifth player from France to win the Grand Final after Clément Sordet (2017), Benjamin Hebert (2014), Mike Lorenzo-Vera (2007) and Nicolas Joakimides (1997).

Image: Hamish Brown (left) and Julien Sale (right) celebrate successes at the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final

The 29-year-old started the day with a one-stroke advantage and fired four front-nine birdies to take control at Club de Golf Alcanada.

A gain on the par-five 12th further extended his advantage before he dropped his only shot of the day on the next.

He responded well, however, with three birdies in his final six holes helping him to his second HotelPlanner Tour triumph of 2026, after his win on home soil at the Le Vaudreuil Golf Challenge earlier this year.

He said: "Coming this week, I didn't have much stress because I knew I was inside the top 15 and the goal was to win the tournament and obviously try to finish number one on the ranking.

"I was going to have fun already tonight but now I'm going to enjoy it even more with my family here."

Sports.title: Isak's non-penalty and Madueke-Mac Allister 'headbutt' - were big calls right?
Sports.content:
There were two big flashpoints during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool, demonstrating the good and bad sides of VAR.

Kai Havertz's early goal was enough for the Gunners to win at Anfield for the first time in 14 years, but there was plenty of action elsewhere in an enthralling encounter.

Read on to find out what our Super Sunday pundits had to say and tune into Ref Watch at 11am on Monday for the views of former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher...

Isak denied penalty: 'VAR, do your job'

In the first half, Alexander Isak had his shirt pulled by Jurrien Timber - but did not react to the contact.

None of the on-field officials gave it as a foul, and neither did VAR.

What did the pundits say?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright discuss Liverpool's penalty shout after Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt as the striker attempted to head the ball.

Jamie Carragher: "One of the best goalscorers in the league is pulled back seven yards out and it stops him heading the ball - why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR, do your job."

Ian Wright: "He shouldn't have to make more of it. We can see it... Unless I'm pulled back, I'm going to head it as much as I can. When he pulled him, it was just about enough as he would need to go down.

"VAR is wrong in this instance. If they gave that penalty, I wouldn't sit here and say 'I can't believe they gave that'."

Gary Neville: "It's actually unnatural not to make more of it. When you get pulled and you're just about to score, you ordinarily complain like crazy. Its a very odd reaction from Isak."

Daniel Sturridge: "Unfortunately, he (Isak) has not fallen over. You're supposed to fall over, put your arms in the air and show the referee you're mad about it... to me, his reaction is almost like 'VAR, do your job'.

"But they've not done their job. He shouldn't have to make more of it - clearly, he shouldn't. Everyone can see that his arm is stretched, he [Timber] is holding him with a stretched-out arm."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Liverpool and Arsenal.

The Liverpool view

Andoni Iraola: "The Isak one is a clear penalty. We can all see that he holds the t-shirt. The ball just goes one centimetre in front of Alex. Alex is going to hit the ball in front of the goal."

On whether the player needed to go down: "The fact that you are even asking me that shows he should have gone to the floor. If he does, they call the penalty 100 per cent.

Asked whether he will tell Alex to go down next time: "Yes, definitely."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking after the 1-0 defeat to Arsenal at Anfield, Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola suggested that Alexander Isak would have been awarded a penalty if he'd gone to ground and claimed that he'll be instructing his players to do so in future.

Virgil van Dijk: "I've seen it back and I've seen it given as well on other occasions. Today it wasn't meant to be.

"The VAR doesn't notice it? There are 50 cameras. Even more. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras? It is spotted because everyone's seen it.

"In the end, it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal."

From Arsenal's perspective, Mikel Arteta said he had not yet watched the incident back and had no comment when asked by Sky Sports.

Iraola: Liverpool should have had second penalty Andoni Iraola believes Liverpool should have been awarded another penalty in the first half.



Christos Tzolis had his hands on Cody Gakpo's hips as the Dutchman went down, but both on-field and VAR did not give it.



Iraola said: “The Gakpo one is sustained holding.”



However, on Sky Sports co-commentary, Gary Neviille said: "It was clumsy from Tzolis. I don't think Gakpo would've got there, he was well ahead of him. There's not enough in it."

Madueke-Mac Allister 'headbutt' - and why VAR made the right call

Carragher: "I want Liverpool to win the game, but I'm delighted he [Madueke] didn't get sent off.

"We have really got to be calling people out and saying 'this is embarrassing'. It's ridiculous and it's got to stop. I can't stand it.

"If someone puts their head back and butts, then red card. But if it's head-to-head and they touch, the other one goes down and the player gets sent off, as a game, call your own people out on it. It's a joke from Mac Allister.

"People are trying to gain an advantage because they can and red cards are being given for it. Whether it's Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers getting together, this has got to stop."

Sports.title: ‘We have to tell them to go down’: Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for Liverpool
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola said he will instruct Liverpool players to go down in the box in future after Alexander Isak was denied a penalty during Arsenal’s first win at Anfield for 14 years.

Liverpool were beaten by Kai Havertz’s early strike after a poor clearance from the goalkeeper ­Alisson but had two penalty claims dismissed by the referee, Andy Madley. The first, a shirt-pull by the Arsenal defender Jurriën Timber on Isak, prevented the ­Sweden international reaching Bradley Barcola’s cross. The second, a hold by Christos ­Tzolis on Cody Gakpo, was reviewed by the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell, but rejected.

Isak stood his ground when held by Timber and Iraola claimed that counted against his team. Asked whether Isak should have collapsed in the area, the Liverpool head coach replied: “It’s a shame you ask me this question but, honestly, yes, we have to tell them to go down because they’re not going to call it otherwise.

“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.”

Iraola accepted the reasons for ­dismissing the Gakpo penalty claim but believed they were inconsistent with the explanation for not ­awarding the Isak appeal. “I think there are two situations and they are a bit related,” he said.

“The Isak one is a clear penalty. He is going to head the ball in front of the goal and they grab him where ­everyone sees the shirt. The ball just goes in front of Alex and I don’t see the reason why [it isn’t given]. ­

“Probably because he doesn’t dive or he doesn’t go to the floor. It shouldn’t be a reason not to concede a penalty. The Gakpo one, I think it’s a sustained holding but I understand their argument and I think they are right when they say the ball was too long in the air and Cody wouldn’t have arrived to the ball.

“But then you’re basically ­accepting that the first one is a ­penalty, no? You cannot use the ­argument in both ways differently.”

Iraola’s post-match mood ­contrasted starkly with his childhood friend Mikel Arteta. The Arsenal ­manager, who claimed not to have seen the Isak incident, was elated by his team’s reaction to their Carabao Cup exit at Fleetwood in midweek and his first win at Anfield in charge of the Gunners.

Arteta said: “It feels better as a manager [to win at Anfield] because it has been such a long time without this feeling. I am extremely proud, especially given the conditions we arrived to the game.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The defeat against Fleetwood looks like the end of the world but then you have to pick yourself up. That is the beautiful part of this game. Four days later you have to come to Anfield, and play against this manager, this team who are in a good moment, and so I am so proud of what my team has done.”

Arsenal have now won at four grounds where they did not win when securing the title last season – Anfield, Villa Park, the Stadium of Light and the City Ground.

“This is a mission we didn’t complete for 14 years,” Arteta said. “There were reasons for that. Some were ­psychological, some were related to the quality we showed on the pitch, and some were decisions. We knew we had to nail all of them. We knew we would have to navigate periods where we had to suffer.”

When informed that his team had denied Liverpool a shot on target in a Premier League game for the first time in 16 years, Arteta said: “I didn’t know about that stat but that is incredible. It didn’t feel like that at the time, they are a team that shoots a lot so you have to be good at denying them space and blocking shots. To do that against this team is remarkable, I would say.”

Sports.title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller
Sports.content:
Goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City to escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter with London City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to before kick-off.

The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been impressive.

Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City manager, praised the ability of his team to win in different ways as needed, after three games in eight days. “We said afterwards, the players should be so proud of what they put into this game,” he said.

“We’ve learned we’re a great team who can keep the ball for 75% of the game and win that way, or we can win like this. That quality to win in different ways is good to have, but the players also have to adapt to that and feel it’s OK to not have the ball all the time, take pride in defending and only having three or four chances but finishing off those chances.”

Before kick-off, cameras showed London City’s superstar summer signing Alexia Putellas opening the boot of her car and taking out a heavy leather-clad square item, her third Ballon d’Or safely encased inside. The Spain midfielder did not present her trophy to fans in the stands before kick-off, instead choosing to put it on display so supporters could queue to have their photo taken with it.

The only nod to the player’s stunning individual year, in which she won the quadruple with Barcelona before joining London City, was on her feet, the geometric gold on her custom Ballon d’Or-themed boots glinting on their first outing.

There have been jokes aplenty about the unlikelihood of the world’s premier individual award heading to its new Bromley home. To reach the stadium from Hayes Lane, you pass a field of horses on your left. London City Lionesses are not Barcelona, and they have become the home of the Ballon d’Or winner by default rather than being the key component of that individual success.

Except, based on the season London City are having and the ruthless ambitions of the owner, Michelle Kang, the idea that the club could produce a season that delivers them collective success and individual success off the back of it feels less distant than it did just a few short months ago.

Against the champions, London City more than held their own, the opportunity to move level on points with their opponents and league leaders Chelsea an inviting incentive. Their threat was evident within 30 seconds, when the Manchester City defender Rebecca Knaak was forced to turn Lucía Corrales’s cross wide of the far post just ahead of a waiting Isobel Goodwin.

Neither team has impressed defensively this season, each only managing to keep one clean sheet in the Women’s Super League, and it made for a thrilling encounter, the high lines and aggressiveness of both attacks delivering a showstopper.

Making her first WSL start for the home team, with Elene Lete hitherto preferred, Mary Earps made a huge statement with an impressive double save from a Knaak header to keep the game goalless going into the break.

View image in fullscreen Mary Earps dives at the feet of Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

City broke the deadlock despite London City dominating and it was their most influential player who delivered. Hemp flicked the ball into the run of Shaw and with her first touch, she took it past Earps before she switched the ball on to her right foot and fired in to become just the third player to score in eight consecutive WSL starts.

A deserved equaliser arrived in the 72nd minute, when Fernández was at the near post to meet a corner and her assured header sent the ball looping in at the back post.

The celebrations were emphatic but they were short-lived. This is a new, more resilient Manchester City, one that survived various scares last term to secure a second WSL title, and they re-established their lead two minutes later, when Hemp stretched out a leg to poke in Mary Fowler’s cross from the right to secure the win.

That London City could feel aggrieved at having not taken something from the game was a testament to their performance and how quickly progress is being made. The home team had 23 shots to City’s seven and 52 touches in the opposition box to City’s 13, but critically the visiting team were clinical when it mattered. Converting two of their three efforts on target and showing the edge needed to battle at the top.

Sports.title: WSL roundup: Arsenal stall despite Russo strike; Chelsea’s James suffers injury
Sports.content:
One shot, on target and in the back of the net, was all it took for Aston Villa to reopen the wound that Arsenal had been carefully trying to stitch back up.

Despite almost 65% possession, 28 shots to one, and 56 touches in the opposition box to four, Alessia Russo’s 85th-minute goal meant Arsenal were only able to salvage a point against Villa after back-to-back wins in the league and Champions League had appeared to have kickstarted their season.

The worst possible scenario for a team that has struggled against low blocks arrived in the 25th minute, when Lynn Wilms found Chasity Grant, who fired low into the bottom corner. It was a hammer blow to the home team, with Villa knowing exactly what to do next: stick 11 players behind the ball and frustrate the Gunners.

Russo’s late goal spared Arsenal’s blushes a little, the forward flicking a header in at the far post from a Stina Blackstenius cross, but the reprieve delivered by Arsenal’s victories over Tottenham and Benfica has been rolled back.

The Gunners have an incredibly tricky run of fixtures coming up, with Liverpool away followed by Barcelona, London City and then Lyonnes. And, despite the back-to-back wins, they haven’t been able to resolve the problems in the final third that have plagued every performance.

The pressure will be back on head coach Renée Slegers and there are questions to be asked about some decision making. However, with similar problems present under Joe Montemurro and Jonas Eidevall before her, maybe it’s time to look beyond the head coach.

Elsewhere Lauren James was forced off with an injury in the first half of Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton. The England forward was replaced by Erin Cuthbert in the 35th minute with the away team 4-0 up. There were five different goalscorers with Melvine Malard getting two. The coach, Sonia Bompastor, said: “It is too soon [to know] about Lauren’s injury. I spoke to her at half-time and it seems to be her hamstring so we will have to have a proper assessment tomorrow.”

Tottenham climbed to fourth in the table after a comprehensive 4-1 win at Birmingham City. The Spurs midfielder Drew Spence set a new all-time WSL appearance record with 2017 to move one above the former Chelsea defender Millie Bright. West Ham were also 4-1 winners, over Liverpool, in their third league win of the season, leapfrogging their opponents in the table to move up to 10th.

Annabel Blanchard gave Crystal Palace the lead at Brighton with a glorious long-range effort but the visitors could not hold on and strikes from Caitlin Hayes and Sophie Peskett completed the turnaround 2-1 win for Arturo Ruiz’s side. “I think that these three wins in a row will be key for the rest of the season and we are in a very good moment,” Ruiz told the club website. “And I think that we are showing what we want to do in terms of our energy. The first half was very good even though we conceded a goal.”

Sports.title: European football: Mbappé penalty helps Real Madrid stroll to sixth straight win
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.

The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.

Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomandé were also on target to keep third-placed Madrid within three points of the La Liga leaders, Barcelona, who thrashed Alavés 6-1 on Saturday.

José Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind Atlético Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.

Real Sociedad’s four-match winning run came to an end after they lost 2-1 to Athletic Bilbao thanks to first-half goals from Inaki Williams and Alex Berenguer, who scored a penalty.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter Milan after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points.

Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M’Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win.

Como moved back into the top four as they eked out a 1-0 victory at home over bottom side Venezia on Sunday for a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions.

The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. The Como captain, Lucas Da Cunha, converted in the 43rd minute for the French international’s first goal of the season. “This is the type of match we found hard to win last season,” Da Cunha told DAZN.

Second-half goals from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga ensured Juventus returned to winning ways with a 2-0 victory over 10-man Napoli, who had Luca Marianucci sent off in the second half as they slipped to their fourth defeat of the campaign.

Lyon and Paris FC both won to close in on the defending Ligue 1 champions, Paris Saint-Germain, with the capital team defeating Monaco 3-1.

View image in fullscreen Lyon’s Corentin Tolisso embraces coach Paulo Fonseca after scoring the second goal against Angers. Photograph: Manon Cruz/Reuters

Lyon won 2-0 at home to Angers with goals in each half from Ernest Nuamah and Corentin Tolisso, as they bounced back from a 2-0 defeat away to PSG last time out.

The seven-time French title winners are third in the table, three points behind PSG and one behind second-placed Lille. Lyon’s win came amid reports that their coach, Paulo Fonseca, is close to leaving the club to return to his native Portugal.

“I know that I will be with the players tomorrow morning but beyond that it is hard to say,” Fonseca, who was in tears as he embraced his backroom staff at the end of the game, told reporters. Fonseca is reportedly a target for Sporting, whose coach Rui Borges is under pressure.

Paris FC are fourth after getting the better of Monaco at the Stade Jean-Bouin. Lassine Sinayoko, the Malian international forward, scored twice late in the first half for Paris FC before FolarinBalogun pulled one back on 65 minutes.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick to stay in charge of Manchester United for Roma game
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is poised to remain in charge of Manchester United for the Champions League game against Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday.

United have not won in nine games and have made their poorest start to a season since 1988, but Carrick’s position is expected to be reviewed again during the international break after the next round of Premier League matches, in which United host Aston Villa next Sunday.

The 45-year-old head coach came close to losing his job last Monday when Jason Wilcox and Omar ­Berrada met at the training ground to discuss his future. The director of football and the chief executive decided ­Carrick should be given a chance to turn form and results around.

Carrick’s side are in 17th with seven points, above the relegation zone only on goal difference.

There remains a view within the hierarchy that Carrick can still transform fortunes, with United’s travelling support still backing him at the end of the defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. After the game the head coach indicated that he expected to still be in position for the Roma match. He said: “We’ve got to move forward and win matches, it’s as simple as that.”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes, Manchester United’s captain, looks dejected after the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Eddie Howe is Wilcox’s preferred candidate should Carrick be sacked, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle manager is open to taking up the position, subject to negotiations. He would cost about £3m in compensation to Newcastle.

Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.

Sports.title: Scottish roundup: Falkirk shock Celtic; Hibernian beat Hearts in semi-final
Sports.content:
Celtic slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk on Sunday to ramp up the scrutiny on manager Martin O’Neill after a run of three wins in 10 games. The Scottish champions had the chance to extend their lead at the top of the table to seven points, but never recovered from conceding a third-minute opener to Ethan Ross.

Scott Tanser scored a second before half-time and the Bairns even had a third goal ruled out by a video assistant referee review for handball against Jacob Murrell. The majority of Celtic’s struggles this season have come in European competition as they crashed out of the Champions League qualifiers and have lost all three Europa League group matches.

But sloppy defensive errors and a lack of a clear tactical plan are beginning to cost them domestically as well. Rangers could now close to within one point of their Old Firm rivals should they win a game in hand.

“We’re still in a decent position at this minute,” said a defiant O’Neill. “I keep out the noise at the end of it all. A tough one to take because I know we conceded two goals but we could have scored six or seven dead easily.”

Falkirk had not beaten Celtic since March 2007, but were well worthy of a fourth consecutive victory to move up to fourth in the table. O’Neill recalled Cameron Carter-Vickers to the heart of his defence, but that decision backfired when the American international presented the ball to Ross to slam home the opening goal.

Quick Guide Scottish Premiership roundup: Saints dedicate draw to dismissed Steward Show Simo Valakari dedicated St Johnstone’s battling 2-2 draw at Kilmarnock to the goalkeeper Toby Steward, who was dismissed in the 14th minute (pictured) after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty area. Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point. The substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair, who came on at the expense of Taylor Steven, also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh. Valakari, the St Johnstone manager, said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’ But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor, who I needed to take out straight away. “We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility. Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a sweeper-keeper for those long balls. In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.” Alfred Johansson admitted he was left to sweat as Motherwell broke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win over St Mirren. Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth. Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players. He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games. It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all." Press Association Photograph: Andy Buchanan/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The former Celtic goalkeeper Scott Bain was inspired in the Falkirk goal to deny Haissem Hassan and Camilo Durán, while the Colombian forward also struck a post as the visitors pressed for an equaliser. But Celtic’s leaky defence was exposed once more on 38 minutes when Tanser raced forward from left-back and drilled low into the corner.

O’Neill twice rode to Celtic’s rescue last season to take interim charge, 20 years after his first spell at the club ended. The Northern Irishman then signed a one-year deal in June.

Yet murmurs of discontent among the club’s fanbase have increased in recent weeks with many now calling for a change. “I’ve managed this team now for about a year, give or take a month or two, and I’ve managed before,” said O’Neill. “We’re still top of the league. We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. A mile behind on two or three occasions as well.”

Marink Reedijk secured his first win as Hibernian manager with a memorable 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts at Hampden.

View image in fullscreen Jamie McGrath wheels away after scoring Hibernian’s second goal. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

A frenetic Edinburgh derby got up and running in the fourth minute when the Hearts attacker Cláudio Braga headed in from a corner, only for Martin Boyle to deservedly level in the 19th minute with a poacher’s goal. A compelling encounter continued and the midfielder Jamie McGrath put the on-top Hibernian ahead three minutes before the interval.

Although Hearts retained a threat in the second half, a stout defensive display by the Leith side means they will meet Rangers in the final at Scotland’s national stadium on Sunday 13 December. Hearts had won the four previous meetings between the teams at Hampden, in 2006, 2012, 2020 and 2022, but this was Hibs’ day.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

On Saturday, Ryan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke down Aberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earn Rangers a place in the final.

Aberdeen restricted Rangers to one shot on target in a low-quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eighth goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park.

The 23-year-old Naderi later tried to share the glory, saying: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team. I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.”

View image in fullscreen Ryan Naderi: a happy man. Photograph: Jamie Johnston/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

It was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance. The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well. So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones! As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”

Sports.title: Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts?  | Andrew Beasley
Sports.content:
No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change.

The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.

Michael Carrick remains the favourite to be the next manager to leave his post. He is unsurprisingly followed by the managers of the clubs who occupy the relegation zone: Pierre Sage of Crystal Palace, Sunderland’s Régis Le Bris and Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest. It seems almost inevitable that Carrick will leave soon so the more interesting analysis lies among the bottom three.

Sunderland sit 20th and are predicted by Opta to finish there. However, they have had a testing start to the season. Le Bris’s side have faced five of the current top seven clubs, the joint-most along with Liverpool. The manager also has enormous reserves of goodwill after taking the club back to the Premier League and then into Europe.

Despite their tough schedule, Sunderland came into the weekend within one expected point of Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham before losing 3-1 at Coventry with the xG count 1.8 to 0.7 in their favour. It was a familiar outcome for a side that has scored 6.2 goals fewer than expected this season.

With Sunderland’s next five league opponents being Chelsea, Aston Villa, Tottenham, Liverpool and Newcastle, the challenge of staying up will not immediately get easier. At least their chance‑converting woes are not as bad as those of Nottingham Forest.

Their shots have been worth 14.7 expected goals, the fourth most in the division after the matches on Saturday. But not once in a game this season have the goals they scored at least equalled their xG, let alone surpassed it. It is a finishing issue, not a question of opposition goalkeepers having super-human performances against them.

The analytical step above standard expected goals is xG on target (xGOT). It measures the likelihood of an on-target shot becoming a goal based on chance quality and shot placement. Forest’s xGOT this season is 7.4, little more than half of their expected goal tally.

This inability to test goalkeepers severely enough explains why Glasner’s men have scored just six times. They are squandering almost one goal per game on average according to their expected goals, a significant shortfall. None of the 96 teams in Europe’s big five leagues were worse than 0.5 goals per match below xG last season, which suggests Forest’s luck should turn for the better.

Is Evangelos Marinakis patient enough for that to happen? Forest’s expected goal data is much stronger for Glasner than it was under any of the four managers their owner fired last season. Whether he pays attention to such numbers is a different issue.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Glasner hinted at a physical deficiency in the squad after defeat at Brentford. “We are outrun by the opposition in every single game. We have to change it,” he said. Distance covered data from Fotmob suggests that is not quite the case, albeit Forest have been outrun in their past five league games. Both the underlying xG data and physical statistics are worse at Glasner’s former club Crystal Palace though.

As expected goals have a far greater bearing on future performance or results than running stats, those numbers are the greater concern. Equally, Palace’s average of 96.9 sprints per match is the fewest in the Premier League (after Saturday’s matches).

The club have been through similar teething troubles with new managers before. Palace’s previous two appointments that occurred between seasons were Frank de Boer and Patrick Vieira. The former was sacked after only five matches in all competitions in 2017, the latter won just one of his first nine league games four years later before recovering to finish 12th.

While Palace are a little wasteful in attack, they have not been as bad as Forest or Sunderland. Their defence is a much bigger problem, which is unusual as Sage’s Lens conceded the fourth fewest expected goals in Ligue 1 last season. Palace are second worst for that metric in the Premier League in 2026‑27, rock bottom if penalties are excluded. Some of that may be down to starting seven combinations of players in the back three because of injuries and Axel Disasi’s three‑match ban, but it is imperative that a manager overcomes such inevitable difficulties.

Palace host Liverpool next weekend. They return after the international break with potentially winnable games against Coventry and Hull. Will those fixtures represent a good opportunity for Sage to kickstart his reign or an excellent chance for his replacement to hit the ground running? Only the chair, Steve Parish, will know the answer but Palace are the strugglers who look most in need of managerial change.

Sports.title: Boy hands himself into police after Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland match
Sports.content:
A 14-year-old boy has “handed himself in” to West Midlands police after a video posted on social media appeared to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland with a photo of Bradley Lowery during the Premier League match on Saturday.

Sunderland fan Bradley captured the hearts of the football world when he was diagnosed with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer. He died aged six in 2017.

Coventry said on Sunday that they were investigating the video footage and Bradley’s mother, Gemma, issued an emotional statement through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children.

West Midlands police said: “We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland [on Saturday] afternoon.

“A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course. We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”

Coventry said in their earlier statement: “Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.”

Gemma Lowery said her “beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate” in her statement. She posted on Instagram: “Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

“I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between.

“So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

“We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?”

Lowery added: “I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t, just for him to learn from this.

“Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.”
