World.title: Lagos teacher wins N10m Maltina prize, gets apartment from Sanwo-Olu
World.content:
Lagos teacher, Busayo Adeyemo, has won the 2026 Maltina Teacher of the Year award, receiving a N10 million cash prize and a three-bedroom apartment from the Lagos State government.

Ms Adeyemo, of Lanre Awolokun High School, Gbagada, Lagos, emerged winner at the 12th edition of the competition organised by the Nigerian Breweries-Felix Ohiwerei Education Trust Fund (NB-FOETF) on Friday in Lagos.

Apart from the cash prize and apartment, she also received a Honda HR-V, an all-expenses-paid overseas capacity development training, a one-year supply of Maltina and a N30 million school infrastructure project to be built in her honour.

According to a press release from the organiser, Ms Adeyemi also won the Maltina Prize for Best STEM Teacher, for which she received an additional N1.5 million.

The Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, who hosted the event, separately rewarded Ms Adeyemo with the three-bedroom apartment.

Governor’s intervention

Mr Sanwo-Olu commended the NB-FOETF for using its resources to recognise and support teachers, describing the initiative as an opportunity to deepen collaboration between the private sector and government.

He said the intervention demonstrated how corporate social responsibility could contribute to improving education in Lagos and Nigeria.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Speaking after she was announced as the winner, Ms Adeyemo expressed appreciation to the education trust fund, the Lagos State government and other partners for the recognition and rewards.

“I am excited, thankful and grateful about this competition and the rewards that have followed. This award simply means that I should keep giving my best.”

She said the award would also encourage her to contribute more to teacher development and STEM education.

“It’s a reminder that I have a responsibility not to relent but to keep giving my best, committing myself to teachers’ development in Lagos and Nigeria, keep advancing STEM education in Nigeria, and believing in the Nigerian children that tomorrow shall be great,” she said.

Other winners

Yusuf Cariyat of Wisdom International School of Excellence, Sauka, Lugbe, Abuja, emerged first runner-up and received N5 million, while Ephraim Inyangudo of Comprehensive Secondary School, Ediene Abak Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State, emerged second runner-up and received N3 million.

Seventeen other teachers who emerged as state champions received N1 million each.

The event also featured remarks from President Bola Tinubu, represented by the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Bernard Doro.

Mr Tinubu commended the education trust fund for its investments in classrooms, libraries and other learning facilities, and said the government was ready to partner with the fund on its planned long-term support for out-of-school children from 2027.

The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, also commended the initiative, saying the strong participation in the competition reflected the depth of teaching talent across the country.

Entries received

According to the NB-FOETF Corporate Affairs Director, Uzodinma Odenigbo, the competition received 2,510 entries from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) this year, representing a 30 per cent increase from the previous edition.

Of the entries, 2,243 were considered valid.

Mr Odenigbo said the competition had so far honoured 305 teachers, supported schools with educational infrastructure and delivered 11 school infrastructure projects.

The Chairman of the NB-FOETF and Managing Director of Nigerian Breweries, Thibaut Boidin, said the competition was established to celebrate teachers and recognise their contribution to society.

He said the 2026 edition was particularly significant as Nigerian Breweries marks 80 years, Maltina marks 50 years, while the education trust fund marks 32 years of investment in education.

“We see your commitment, the sacrifices, surprises that may never appear on a report card. We see the extra time you give to a struggling student, the patience, the courage and the optimism required to keep believing in the next generation. We honour you and we thank you,” Mr Boidin said.

The Maltina Teacher of the Year competition was introduced in 2015 by the Nigerian Breweries-Felix Ohiwerei Education Trust Fund to identify, honour and reward outstanding teachers across Nigeria.

Since inception, the Maltina Teacher of the Year Competition has produced eleven grand prize winners, and they include Rose Obi (2015), Imoh Essien (2016), Felix Ariguzo (2017), Olasunkanmi Opeifa (2018), Ezem Collins (2019), Oluwabunmi Anani (2020), Abanika Taiye (2021), Alaku Ayiwulu (2022), Adeola Adefemi (2023), Esomnofu Ifechukwu (2024) and Serah Yusuf(2025).

With her win, Ms Adeyemo becomes the 12th recipient of the national award.

About the competition

The Maltina Teacher of the Year competition was introduced in 2015 by the Nigerian Breweries-Felix Ohiwerei Education Trust Fund (NB-FOETF) to identify, honour and reward outstanding teachers across Nigeria.

The competition is supported by the Federal Ministry of Education and other education stakeholders, including the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), the All Nigeria Confederation of Principals of Secondary Schools (ANCOPSS) and the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN).

The NB-FOETF was established in 1994 with an initial capital of N100 million to support sustained interventions in education.

According to the organisers, the fund has worked across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones at the primary, secondary and tertiary levels.

World.title: Okorocha chasing shadows, Uzodimma says, vows to appeal court judgement
World.content:
Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma has vowed to appeal the Federal High Court judgement recognising his predecessor, Rochas Okorocha, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 elections, describing the former governor as “chasing shadows”.

Mr Uzodimma’s Chief Press Secretary, Oguike Nwachuku, said the governor considered the judgement a “travesty of justice” and was confident it would be overturned by the Court of Appeal.

“Obviously, the Governor will appeal the judgement which is a travesty of justice,” Mr Nwachuku told PREMIUM TIMES on Friday in response to questions about Mr Okorocha’s allegations against the governor and his (Okorocha) account of the disputed APC senatorial primary.

The governor’s response followed Mr Okorocha’s appearance on Arise News’ Prime Time on Thursday, where he claimed that he remained the dominant political figure in the APC in Imo State and accused Mr Uzodimma of relying on documents containing irregularities to secure the party’s senatorial ticket.

Mr Okorocha had declared that “the structure of APC in Imo State is Rochas”, insisting that his political influence in the state remained intact despite opposition from the governor’s camp.

In a PREMIUM TIMES report the former governor also alleged that documents supporting Mr Uzodimma’s emergence as the party’s candidate contained inconsistencies, including discrepancies in the primary’s date, the description of the exercise as a consensus arrangement and result sheets allegedly completed by one person across 144 wards and 12 local government areas.

Mr Nwachuku, however, dismissed Mr Okorocha’s account and insisted that the governor won the primary by an overwhelming margin.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Uzodimma’s account of the primary

According to the governor’s spokesperson, there was a direct primary in Imo West because Mr Okorocha rejected the consensus arrangement adopted in the other two senatorial districts.

He said political stakeholders in Owerri Zone, which produces the Imo East senatorial seat, and Okigwe Zone, which produces Imo North, opted for consensus arrangements that produced Prince Alex Mbata and Senator Patrick Ndubueze, respectively.

Mr Nwachuku said Mr Okorocha insisted on contesting against Mr Uzodimma across the 12 local government areas in Imo West.

He insisted that the governor won the contest with 230,464 votes against Mr Okorocha’s 1,098 votes.

The spokesperson said officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) were present during the exercise, while the APC National Assembly Primary Election Committee, led by its chairman and returning officer, Williams Kayoda a retired rear admiral supervised the process across the local government areas.

He maintained that the outcome was legitimate and accused Mr Okorocha of attempting to undermine the APC by challenging the result.

“Rochas Okorocha is simply chasing shadows and intentionally working against the interest of the APC he claims to be a founding member and the re-election of President Bola Tinubu,” he said.

Dispute over APC leadership

Mr Nwachuku also rejected Mr Okorocha’s claim to control the APC structure in Imo State, arguing that the party’s rules recognise sitting governors as leaders of the party in their respective states.

He said President Bola Tinubu remained the national leader of the APC, while Mr Uzodimma controlled the party’s structure in Imo State.

“By the APC rules, the governors are the leaders of the party in their states while the president is the leader in the country. I’m not aware that rule has changed,” he said.

He accused Mr Okorocha of attempting to personalise a party structure that belonged collectively to its members, adding that the former governor was unwilling to submit to the party’s leadership.

Mr Nwachuku also criticised Mr Okorocha’s eight-year administration in Imo State, describing it as a family system of government and blaming his performance in office for his alleged loss of political relevance.

He dismissed the former governor’s public celebration of the court judgement, arguing that the ruling would not survive an appeal.

“No responsible leader anywhere in the world will appear on television the way Okorocha did to celebrate a judgement he knows will be thrown out at the appeal for lacking in facts and for being against the rules of the party,” he said.

He also dismissed Mr Okorocha’s claims of continued popularity among voters in Imo West and the state.

Mr Nwachuku concluded his response with the expression caveat emptor, meaning buyer beware, urging the public to scrutinise the former governor’s claims.

Background to the court dispute

The Federal High Court in Abuja, presided over by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, had ruled in favour of Mr Okorocha in the dispute over the APC’s Imo West senatorial primary.

The court declared him the validly nominated candidate of the party and directed INEC to recognise him for the 2027 senatorial election.

The judgement followed a suit filed by Mr Okorocha challenging INEC’s recognition of Mr Uzodimma as the winner of the party’s 18 May primary.

During his interview, Mr Okorocha said he obtained certified copies of documents relating to the primary from INEC on 26 July 2026, while documents supporting Mr Uzodimma’s emergence were presented to the commission on 22 August.

He alleged that the later documents contained inconsistencies, including a discrepancy in the date of the election and the description of Mr Uzodimma’s emergence as a consensus candidate despite the existence of competing aspirants.

He further claimed that result sheets covering more than 300 polling units across 144 wards and 12 local government areas were completed by one person.

Mr Okorocha also questioned the circumstances surrounding a letter allegedly submitted to the APC national chairman by the Imo resident electoral commissioner, arguing that the document supporting his own claim was certified by INEC, while the one supporting Mr Uzodimma was certified by the APC.

He alleged that these discrepancies were part of the evidence that persuaded the court to recognise him as the winner.

However, Mr Okorocha’s allegations of document irregularities and forgery remain disputed by the governor’s camp. Mr Nwachuku insisted that the primary was properly conducted under the supervision of INEC officials and the APC’s national election committee.

The APC had also indicated that it would study the judgement and pursue available legal remedies.

The dispute is the latest chapter in the political rivalry between the two men. Mr Okorocha governed Imo State from 2011 to 2019 and subsequently represented Imo West in the Senate from 2019 to 2023.

World.title: South-East governors urge Ndigbo to shun deception and vote for Tinubu in 2027
World.content:
Governors Peter Mbah of Enugu State, Charles Soludo of Anambra State, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State, and Hope Uzodimma of Imo State have called on the people of South-East region to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election and ignore every form of deceipt and political distractions.

The governors made the call during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East flagged off by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu at Okpara Square, Enugu, on Saturday.

Speaking, the host governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, urged the people of the region to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms.

He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the federal government’s economic reforms.

“If I ask what future you want for your children, I’m sure you are seeing that future unfold gradually through the bold and courageous reforms of Mr President.

“It is through those reforms that enough money has been made available to all the states. Which is why in Enugu, when you look around you, you will see the Smart Green Schools, Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres, and numerous other projects and initiatives we have undertaken in just three years.

This is happening because of the bold and courageous reforms of Mr President and we know the job is not finished yet. A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“So, we must finish the journey we all started together. We must come out on January 16 with our PVC and ensure that the good work Mr. President is doing will continue.

“Don’t listen to any voice. Those voices telling us a different thing. We, the Igbos have gone to communities outside our zone to build businesses. And we also know how to build relationships. And that is being put to test. We are not a people that are ethnic bigots. We are a people that are strategic.

“And that is why we must all come out in our numbers and support Mr President to continue the good work. Support all our APC candidates to ensure that they are returned come January and February,” he emphasised.

Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-east, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women, including payment of hospital bills, in Enugu by the First Lady, within 48 hours.

“When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said.

Also speaking, Governor Uzodimma reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years, but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu.

He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructure and economic development in the South-East.

“We are now seeing good roads, electricity, health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said.

The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the federal government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development.

“We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said.

Like Mbah, Uzodimma added that the improved financial position of the state had enabled his administration to pay salaries and pensions consistently, including 13th-month salaries for workers.

In his remarks, Governor Nwifuru said that the number one mission for Ndigbo in 2027 elections was to re-elect President Tinubu, describing the APC as the only political party with a clear and identifiable manifesto capable of sustaining the country’s development and truly advancing the course of Ndigbo.

He dismissed suggestions of his involvement in any political coalition, stressing that his loyalty remained with the APC, urging urged supporters to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the 2027 elections.

Similarly, Soludo, represented by his Deputy, Dr Gilbert Ibezim, said the South-East had a responsibility to support Tinubu’s re-election in appreciation of his administration’s achievements, adding that the region stood to benefit more from continued collaboration with the federal government.

Also speaking, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, urged Igbos to embrace political inclusion by supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

Kalu said the Igbo had not produced a president of Nigeria in the past 60 years, and was therefore not party to any one-term arrangement for the Presidency of Igbo extraction by anybody.

He, however, stressed that the Igbo needed to to strengthen its political alliances across the nation to actualise a full two-term Igbo presidency in the near future.

He recalled that Tinubu, while serving as governor of Lagos State, maintained cordial relationships with Igbos and included them in his cabinet.

He commended the Tinubu administration for establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC).

He described it as a major step towards addressing the region’s developmental challenges.

Meanwhile, addressing the rally, the First Lady conveyed President Tinubu’s goodwill message and urged Nigerians not to be discouraged by the economic challenges associated with the President’s reforms, insisting that the country was moving towards prosperity.

She likened the process to childbirth, noting that although the period of labour could be painful, it ultimately led to delivery.

“Mr. President said I should greet everyone. We have done reforms and we are now in prosperity. Don’t allow anyone to deceive you. The worst is over. We are stepping into prosperity,” she said.

The First Lady described the empowerment initiative as an indication of the APC government’s commitment to translating its promises into practical interventions, noting that the party was combining political mobilisation with economic support.

The First Lady urged the women to mobilise support for President Tinubu and APC candidates in the forthcoming 2027 general elections, asking them to hold political aspirants accountable for their records of empowerment and development interventions.

Other dignitaries at the massive rally were Wife of the Vice President, Mrs Nana Shettima; wife of the Senate President, Mrs. Uloma Akpabio; wives of the South East governors; Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite; Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh (SAN); and Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim.

Also present were the APC Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Ben Nwoye; National Women Leader of the APC and Director-General of the Women Wing of the Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Mary Alile-Idele; South-East Zonal Woman Leader of the APC, Dr Oby Ajih; members of the National and State Assemblies, local government chairmen and other party stakeholders.

The rally by the Remi Tinubu-led Women Mobilisation Directorate of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, which kicked off in the South East, will also be held across the remaining five geopolitical zones of the country.

World.title: In Zamfara, 9 a.m is 9 a.m: How Lawal is killing ‘African time’ mentality, By Yusuf Ladan
World.content:
Nigerians are widely known for what is popularly described as “African time” a culture of lateness where an event scheduled for 9:00 a.m may not begin until 10:00 a.m or even 11:00 a.m.

Over time, this habit has become normalised in our society, with people often arriving late to appointments, meetings and official functions without considering the inconvenience it causes others.

However, my working experience as part of the press team of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has significantly changed my perception of time management and challenged my long-held African Time stereotype.

On my first day in Gusau, I approached government functions with the usual mindset, assuming that even when an event was scheduled for a particular time, there would always be some extra minutes before it commenced.

Like many Nigerians, I would sometimes add a few minutes to the scheduled time before setting out for an event, believing that punctuality was not necessarily a strict requirement.

But that assumption was quickly challenged.

On my first day attending an official function involving the governor, I arrived only to discover that I had been locked out just a few minutes before the scheduled commencement time.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It was then that I was told something that has remained with me: “Governor Dauda Lawal’s 9:00 a.m. means 9:00 a.m., and his 2:00 p.m. means 2:00 p.m.” That experience became a turning point for me.

Gradually, I adjusted to the governor’s schedule and developed the habit of arriving at least 30 minutes before his expected arrival.

For over a month of observing his official engagements, I have yet to witness Governor Dauda Lawal arrive late for a scheduled function.

In fact, there was an occasion when the governor arrived ahead of schedule while some participants were yet to arrive.

This consistency has gradually influenced the conduct of government appointees, political office holders, civil servants and other participants attending official functions.

People now understand that keeping to time is not negotiable because the governor does not compromise on punctuality.

Beyond the personal discipline it demands, this culture sends a strong message about leadership, respect for other people’s time and the importance of institutional efficiency.

When a leader takes time seriously, those working with him are compelled to do the same. It also helps to change the mindset that lateness is an acceptable part of our social and official engagements.

My experience in Zamfara under Governor Dauda Lawal has taught me that punctuality is not just about arriving early; it is about discipline, responsibility and respect for others.

Perhaps, one of the less-discussed changes taking place in Zamfara under Governor Dauda Lawal is this growing culture of punctuality.

In Zamfara, at least from what I have personally observed, African Time is gradually losing its place. Governor Dauda Lawal has made it clear that when time is fixed, it must be respected.

And that is a leadership lesson worth taking beyond the walls of Government House.

* Yusuf Ladan is a Gusau, Zamfara State-based journalist

World.title: 2027: Christian, Muslim youth groups sign peace accord ahead of elections
World.content:
Christian and Muslim youth organisations in Lagos have signed an interreligious peace accord, committing to reject political violence, religious intolerance and the use of young people as political thugs ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The accord was signed on Saturday at the South-West Zonal Interreligious Peace Accord Summit organised by the Youth Wing of the Christian Association of Nigeria (YOWICAN), in collaboration with the National Council of Muslim Youth Organisations (NACOMYO).

The summit was held at the Senator Oluremi Tinubu CAN Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja, Lagos, with the theme, “Building Bridges of Faith and Politics: Strengthening Peace, Unity, and National Development Through Christian-Muslim Collaboration.”

The groups said the 2027 elections would test Nigeria’s unity and urged young people not to allow politicians to recruit or manipulate them into violence.

In the communique issued at the end of the summit, the groups said the signing of the accord represents their collective determination to reject political violence, religious manipulation, hate speech and other divisive actions “capable of threatening the peace and stability of the country.”

They also called on Christian and Muslim youths to promote tolerance and peaceful coexistence in their communities, institutions and places of worship.

Peaceful coexistence

Speaking at the summit, the Chairman of CAN in Lagos State, Stephen Adegbite, said the peace accord aims to foster religious tolerance, reject political violence, and promote peaceful coexistence ahead of the elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Adegbite criticised politicians who make derogatory statements against their opponents.

“What we must do is what youths have done today; both Christians and Muslims have done well to bring peace and restore confidence in our great nation,” he said.

He urged young people to lead by example, saying the summit was intended to demonstrate that Christians and Muslims want peace before, during and after the elections.

“We don’t want anybody to be killed for any elective position,” he said.

Mr Adegbite also cited the Bible and the Quran as texts that promote peaceful coexistence.

Peace message to grassroots

The National Secretary of NACOMYO, Shehu Ibrahim, said the accord is particularly important as the country approaches the 2027 elections.

Mr Ibrahim said the organisation would take the message of peace to communities across the country, including through Imams, Friday prayers, Islamic schools and other religious gatherings.

He said the groups would mobilise young people at the grassroots to discourage violence during the elections.

Also speaking, the Lagos State APC Youth Leader, Damilare Orimoloye, said young people must understand that disagreements do not have to result in violence.

“Peace speaks against violence, how to tolerate each other, showing love amidst misunderstanding,” Mr Orimoloye said.

He added that disagreements were likely during the election period, making tolerance and peaceful communication important.

The South-West Chairman of YOWICAN, Nnamdi Obasi, said the summit was significant because Christian and Muslim youths needed to bridge existing gaps and avoid being used against one another.

He urged young Nigerians to remain united and resist attempts by politicians to exploit religious differences to create conflict as the 2027 elections approach.

What the accord says

The communique, signed by YOWICAN’s National Chairman, Orowolo Daniel, and National Secretary, Nehemiah Michael, alongside NACOMYO’s National Secretary II, Shehu Ibrahim, and its representative for the Southern Secretary, Mudashir Bello, outlined seven commitments.

Among them is a rejection of the recruitment and manipulation of young people as political thugs, as well as a commitment to religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence.

The groups also called on religious, traditional, community and political leaders to discourage intolerance, political manipulation and incitement to violence.

They said the peace message should extend beyond the summit to states, local government areas, communities, schools and religious institutions.

The groups further resolved that the peace accord should not end with its signing but should serve as a framework for continued dialogue, mutual accountability and peacebuilding between Christian and Muslim youths.

They urged Nigerian youths, political leaders, religious institutions and other stakeholders to work towards a peaceful and inclusive 2027 election.

World.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One world champion at age 20
World.content:
Mercedes’ Italian driver Kimi Antonelli celebrates winning the world championship title at the end of the Mexico City Formula One Grand Prix, at the Hermanos Rodriguez racetrack in Mexico City on November 1st, 2026. (Photo by Yuri CORTEZ / AFP)

Kimi Antonelli drove the perfect race to finish third in his Mercedes at the Mexico Grand Prix and seal his place in Formula One history as the youngest world champion.

Max Verstappen took the chequered flag but all eyes were on the young Italian who takes the crown at the age of 20 years and 68 days, more than three years younger than Sebastian Vettel in 2010.

He is the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
