World.title: CAF picks Nigeria’s Samson Adamu as new General Secretary
World.content:
Nigerian Samson Adamu has been appointed the new General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

CAF announced the appointment on Sunday, on its website following a comprehensive recruitment process conducted by the continental football governing body.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Adamu had been serving as acting General Secretary since March, following the resignation of Veron Mosengo-Omba.

Mosengo-Omba subsequently became president of the football federation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

CAF President, Patrice Motsepe, was quoted in the statement on its website as saying that the appointment followed a competitive recruitment exercise, during which the position was widely advertised and several candidates interviewed.

Adamu has worked with CAF for eight years, serving first as Director of Competitions and later as Director of Tournaments and Events.

“Adamu brings extensive experience in African football administration, having joined CAF in 2018 as Director of Competitions before subsequently serving as Director of Tournaments and Events.

“He has played a leading role in the delivery of several major continental competitions, including CAF’s flagship tournament, the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations,” Motsepe was quoted as saying.

A graduate of the FIFA Master programme in International Management, Law and Humanities of Sport, Adamu brings considerable institutional knowledge and experience to his new role.

NAN reports that Adamu is expected to oversee CAF’s day-to-day administration and support the implementation of its strategic priorities.

He is the son of Amos Adamu, a former Director of Sports in the then Ministry of Sports and a former FIFA Executive Committee member.

The appointment places Adamu among a distinguished line of CAF General Secretaries, including members of Egypt’s Fahmy family.

Mourad Fahmy served from 1961 to 1982, followed by his son, Mustapha Fahmy, from 1982 to 2010, and grandson, Amr Fahmy, who held the position from 2017 to 2019.

World.title: FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos sail into semi finals, to meet Brazil
World.content:
Nigeria’s Flamingos booked their place in the semi-finals of this year’s FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup finals after securing a 1-0 victory over Venezuela on Sunday night, with Azeezatt Oduntan scoring a late penalty in the 89th minute.

The quarter-final contest had been closely fought, with Nigeria creating several opportunities but finding Venezuela goalkeeper Valeria Rebanales a huge stumbling block. The Flamingos enjoyed much of the attacking play in the first half, but Rebanales produced a couple of saves to keep the scores level.

Midfielder Favour Nkwocha was also cautioned as Nigeria continued to press for an opening goal. Head Coach Hakeem Busari made his first change of the evening, introducing Precious Oscar for Oluwakemi Adegbuyi as Nigeria looked to find a way through.

The deadlock remained unbroken until the 88th minute, when the referee initially awarded Nigeria a penalty before being invited to the VAR monitor to review the decision. Following the review, the penalty was upheld, and Oduntan stepped forward to convert from the spot with a minute left on the clock, giving Nigeria the breakthrough.

Top scorer Oluebube Umejiaku had won the penalty for the Flamingos, setting up Oduntan to deliver the decisive moment of the contest. The victory sends Nigeria into the semi-finals, where they will face Brazil, who secured a 2-1 win over China in their quarter-final encounter.

World.title: Nathaniel Bassey becomes first African gospel artist to hit one billion YouTube views
World.content:
Nigerian gospel singer and pastor Nathaniel Bassey has surpassed one billion views on YouTube, becoming the first African gospel artist to achieve the milestone.

Bassey’s official YouTube channel, Nathaniel Bassey Main, has amassed more than 1.014 billion views and 5.24 million subscribers since its creation in 2011, according to figures displayed on the platform at the time of filing this report.

The achievement coincides with the October 2026 edition of the Hallelujah Challenge, the online prayer and worship programme

founded by the gospel minister in 2017.

The monthly initiative features midnight sessions of praise, worship and prayers, attracting participants from different parts of the world.

Initially launched as an online worship gathering, the Hallelujah Challenge has grown into an international Christian movement, with thousands of people participating in its live sessions and millions more watching recorded editions.

Bassey is known for popular gospel songs such as Imela, Onise Iyanu, Olowogbogboro and You Are God, which have contributed to his popularity among gospel music audiences in Nigeria and beyond.

The one-billion-view milestone has generated excitement among his followers, with some suggesting that the minister could explore opportunities to monetise the growing audience of his online worship sessions.

However, Bassey has maintained that the Hallelujah Challenge is primarily focused on worship and spiritual devotion rather than revenue generation.

Vanguard News

World.title: Catholic Diocese disowns Enugu APC campaign council list
World.content:
…Bishop Obodo demands removal of his name, warns of legal action

By Anayo Okoli

The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has disowned the inclusion of the Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu, Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, in the Enugu State All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council, saying he was listed without his knowledge or consent.

The Diocese also demanded the immediate removal of the bishop’s name and those of other Catholic priests allegedly included in the campaign council without their authorisation.

Obodo, who is also the Enugu State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, was reportedly named Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the APC campaign council.

In a disclaimer dated October 30, 2026, and signed by the Diocesan Chancellor and Secretary, Very Rev. Fr. Wilfred Chidi Agubuchie, the Diocese described the inclusion as unauthorised, misleading and a misrepresentation of the bishop’s political disposition.

The statement said the action was a “malicious act of misrepresentation and defamation,” adding that it undermined the bishop’s integrity and ecclesiastical reputation.

“The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has become aware of reports concerning the inclusion of the name of Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu and Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Enugu State, as Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the Enugu State APC Campaign Council, alongside the names of some Catholic priests.

“We categorically state that the inclusion of the Bishop’s name without his knowledge or consent is wholly unauthorised, misleading and unacceptable,” the statement said.

The Diocese stressed that the Catholic Church did not engage in partisan politics, participate in political campaigns or endorse political parties.

It said the Church remained politically neutral and committed to its spiritual mission and the promotion of peace, justice and the common good.

While acknowledging the right of individual Christians to participate in civic and democratic activities, the Diocese warned against using the name, office or identity of the Church and its ministers for partisan political interests.

“We therefore demand the immediate removal of Bishop Ernest Obodo’s name, as well as the names of all other Catholic priests included without their knowledge and consent, from the said campaign list and any related publications,” it said.

The Diocese further warned that any continued or subsequent unauthorised use of the bishop’s name, title, image or ecclesiastical office for partisan political purposes would attract appropriate legal action.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the Catholic Church is not a political campaign organisation and must not be presented as one,” the statement added.

World.title: Stop opposition politics, integrate with FG, Soludo tells South-East leaders
World.content:
Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged South-East political leaders to abandon opposition politics and embrace greater integration with the Federal Government.

Soludo made the call at a stakeholders’ meeting on Sunday in Awka.

The meeting had political leaders and grassroots mobilisers from the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party.

The governor said that the coalition of political parties in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election represented a new direction for the region’s political engagement.

According to him, the era of opposition politics, which became prominent in the South-East during the 2015 general elections, should give way to active participation in governance at the centre.

He said that considerable work was required at the grassroots to change public perception of the government and mobilise support for the president.

He argued that the 5,000 votes Tinubu received in Anambra in the 2023 presidential election had contributed to attracting significant projects to the state and the region.

“If 5,000 votes could attract these projects to our state and the region, imagine what would happen if we mobilised the electorate to give him massive support,” he said.

On the economic reforms of the government, Soludo acknowledged efforts to stabilise foreign exchange availability and address fiscal challenges, noting that, although progress had been made, more work was required.

He called for structural realignment of the coalition, saying existing campaign and mobilisation structures would be streamlined during the week.

The governor urged grassroots mobilisers to adopt door-to-door campaigns, drawing lessons from successful political mobilisation strategies used during the 1983 elections.

He also advised campaign teams not to be distracted by opposition criticism and verbal attacks on social media, but to remain focused on communicating what he described as the truth.

Soludo reaffirmed his commitment to long-term governance, saying that the decisions being taken by his administration were aimed at securing a prosperous future for generations to come.

Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Mr Sly Ezeokenwa, described the gathering as a landmark in the political history of Anambra.

Ezeokenwa said that the coalition was an unprecedented political alignment involving different parties united in support of Tinubu’s re-election.

He commended Soludo for providing leadership and facilitating the alliance, assuring that APGA would fully support the governor’s political direction.

“Our party structure is ready to execute the instructions and deliver results at the polls,” he said.

Also speaking, APC Chairman in Anambra, Sen. Emma Anosike, expressed appreciation for the development strides in the state.

Anosike said that the political realignment was aimed at positioning Anambra more directly within the government’s political and developmental framework.

He called for cooperation and solidarity among political parties, irrespective of their differences, to achieve the objectives of the coalition.

World.title: 2027: Otti warns supporters against disrupting opposition campaigns
World.content:
Threatens arrest for anyone obstructing rival parties

By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has warned Labour Party supporters against disrupting the campaign activities of opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that he has not authorised anyone to interfere with their democratic rights.

Otti said anyone found obstructing rival political parties from holding lawful rallies or other campaign activities would face arrest, irrespective of party affiliation.

The governor gave the warning on Sunday in Umuahia while flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he stressed that political competition must be conducted within the confines of the law.

He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadia, provided they followed the necessary procedures, obtained relevant approvals and paid the stipulated fees.

Otti added that he had directed security agencies to ensure that no political group was prevented from carrying out legitimate campaign activities.

“I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” he said.

Addressing party loyalists, the governor warned that membership of the ruling party would not confer immunity on anyone who attempted to undermine the democratic process.

“You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning.

“Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said.

Beyond campaign conduct, Otti challenged opposition parties to focus their campaigns on policy alternatives and the future development of the state rather than personal attacks or issues he said his administration had addressed.

He argued that political debate in Abia should move beyond the payment of salaries and pensions, road construction and environmental sanitation to broader development priorities.

“Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation.

“The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said.

He urged opposition parties to examine available performance data before making claims about the state, citing its ratings in the Citizen Satisfaction Index, State Performance Index and Fiscal Performance Ranking by governance-monitoring organisations.

“You should go and do your research first before coming out to open your mouth, because there are data everywhere to show what has been achieved. Evidently, the world knows that Abia is on the right track,” Otti said.

The governor also cited feedback from Abians at home and abroad, as well as development opportunities offered by multilateral institutions, as indications of progress under his administration.

“It would therefore be unthinkable that anyone will ever be allowed to return us to the old era of irresponsibility and misery,” he said.

Otti thanked residents for attending the campaign flag-off and urged Labour Party supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation across the state.

“This is your project, and as you return to the communities, knock on every door and remind our people that we still have a job to complete. Invite them to join the campaign so that together we can conclude the journey that began 12 years ago in faith and optimism,” he added.

The event featured the presentation of party flags to Labour Party candidates for the 2027 National and State Houses of Assembly elections.

Party members, candidates and supporters attended the ceremony, chanting solidarity songs in support of their respective candidates.

World.title: NDC chieftain tackles Kalu over Obi’s four-year presidency proposal
World.content:
Benjamin Kalu

By Anayo Okoli

ENUGU — A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Barrister Peter Agubuzu, has faulted the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, over his criticism of a proposal for the South-East to accept a single four-year presidential term.

Agubuzu described Kalu’s remarks as misplaced, urging him to focus on addressing the economic hardship and rising cost of living confronting Nigerians rather than dwelling on how long the South-East might wait to produce a President.

Kalu had reportedly criticised South-East stakeholders advocating a single four-year presidential term for the region, an arrangement attributed to the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) women’s rally in Enugu on Saturday, the Deputy Speaker reportedly said the Igbo could not afford to wait 60 years to produce a President who would serve for only four years.

Reacting, Agubuzu, a senior lawyer, said the immediate concern of Nigerians was the worsening economic situation and the need for leadership capable of addressing the country’s challenges.

He argued that Obi’s proposal was driven by the need to transform Nigeria’s economy from consumption to production and lift millions of citizens out of poverty.

“While Nigerians across the country are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because of the economic hardship they are experiencing and their fear of a worsening economic crisis if Tinubu is re-elected, our brother, the Deputy Speaker, is talking about 60 years.

“He forgot that Obi’s primary objective is to transform Nigeria from consumption to production to lift millions out of poverty. This is why Nigerians are chanting Tinubu Must Go,” Agubuzu said.

He maintained that the major concern of Obi was how to address the country’s economic difficulties and restore hope to millions of Nigerians struggling with the rising cost of living.

“What Nigerians are saying is straightforward: Peter Obi should come and salvage the country from the impending economic disaster they fear will follow if President Tinubu is re-elected.

“Nigerians are worried about their survival, their livelihoods and the future of their children. That is the urgent issue before us, not a speculative debate about waiting 60 years for an Igbo President,” he said.

The NDC chieftain further argued that discussions about a single presidential term should be considered within the broader context of national unity, equity and political inclusion.

He urged political leaders to pay greater attention to the concerns of ordinary Nigerians and focus on practical solutions to the country’s economic challenges rather than allow debates over regional claims to the presidency to overshadow demands for effective leadership.

World.title: POLITICS, ETHNICITY AND MORALITY NEED NOT COLLIDE
World.content:
The challenge is not to eliminate politics or ethnicity, but to ensure that neither overrides moral responsibility, contends GODWIN SOGOLO

Politics, ethnicity and morality are three distinct yet interrelated dimensions of human existence. Their interaction often complicates practical judgement and responsible citizenship. Politics concerns the acquisition, exercise and distribution of power; ethnicity refers to a collective identity rooted in shared ancestry, history and culture; while morality provides the principles by which conduct is judged as right or wrong, just or unjust, and responsible or irresponsible.

Of course, there are other dimensions of human existence – such as religion, etiquette and customs – all of which, like politics, are subject to moral evaluation. Through praise or blame, reward or punishment, society encourages responsible behaviour and discourages actions harmful to the common good. This reflects the recognition that laws and institutions alone cannot guarantee social order; mutual trust, shared values and a sense of obligation towards others are also indispensable.

There is, however, a school of thought which holds that politics should be exempt from moral scrutiny on account of its practical realities and peculiar demands. This position is commonly associated with the political philosopher, Niccolò Machiavelli, whose analysis of political power emphasises the realities of governance rather than idealised expectations of how rulers ought to conduct themselves. The underlying argument is that political leaders must contend with competing interests, uncertainty, opposition and the imperatives of national security: circumstances that may sometimes require decisions that depart from conventional moral expectations.

However, the distinctive pressures of politics do not make political conduct immune to moral judgement. They merely require that such judgement take account of circumstances, consequences and competing obligations. Political expediency may sometimes justify difficult choices, but it cannot serve as a blanket excuse for corruption, deception, oppression or the abuse of power. Since political decisions affect people’s lives, liberties, property and welfare, citizens must retain the right to evaluate their leaders by standards of justice, integrity and accountability. Otherwise, political necessity becomes a convenient justification for virtually any wrongdoing.

The same distinction applies to ethnicity. Ethnic identity is neither inherently virtuous nor morally objectionable. It can provide a sense of belonging, preserve cultural heritage and foster solidarity. The problem arises when ethnic loyalty is treated as an unquestionable obligation, requiring people to defend wrongdoing by members of their group or to distrust others simply because they belong to a different community. Ethnic solidarity need not entail moral blindness, just as national unity need not require the abandonment of cultural identity.

As we approach the 2027 elections, the challenge is not to eliminate politics or ethnicity, but to ensure that neither overrides moral responsibility. Nigerians are perfectly entitled to support candidates from their own ethnic communities, but ethnic affinity should not become the overriding criterion for political choice. There is, therefore, nothing inherently wrong with a Yoruba person supporting Bola Tinubu or an Igbo person supporting Peter Obi, provided such support is informed by genuine political convictions, considered judgement and legitimate interests, without compromising the fundamental values of honesty, justice, competence and the common good. Ethnic identity may influence political preferences, but it should never be allowed to substitute for independent judgement.

Similarly, opposition to a candidate from one’s own ethnic group should not be construed as an act of betrayal or disloyalty. Neither Charles Soludo nor David Umahi should be regarded as an Igbo traitor simply because their political positions or choices differ from those of other members of their ethnic community. In a democracy, political allegiance is a matter of individual conviction, not an obligation imposed by ethnic belonging. Indeed, the freedom to disagree with one’s kinsmen, without being subjected to accusations of disloyalty, is an essential expression of democratic maturity. Ethnic identity does not, in itself, establish merit, just as belonging to another ethnic group does not imply unworthiness.

The relevant questions should be what candidates stand for, the values they uphold, how they have conducted themselves in public office, what they have achieved and what they are likely to contribute to the country. These, rather than the accidents of ethnic ancestry, should provide the basis for political evaluation and choice.

In judging one another, our guiding principles must be consistency, objectivity and an unwavering commitment to the common good. We must be prepared to apply the same standards of judgement to ourselves, our political allies and our opponents, without allowing ethnic sentiment, personal interests or political affiliations to compromise our sense of fairness.

Ultimately, whatever our differences in ethnicity, political persuasion or personal convictions, we share a common aspiration: to see Nigeria prosper, become a more just and inclusive society, and fulfil its enormous potential. Our collective responsibility is not merely to secure a better country for ourselves, but also to ensure that we bequeath to generations yet unborn a nation that is more united, stable, prosperous and worthy of their hopes and aspirations.

The distinction between politics, ethnicity and morality is therefore essential to responsible citizenship. It does not mean that the three domains must operate in isolation. Rather, it means recognising their distinct purposes and refusing to confuse political advantage or ethnic solidarity with moral rightness. The conceptual challenge is to preserve these distinctions, while the practical challenge is to uphold them when political competition, communal loyalty, historical grievances and personal interests exert pressure on judgement.

The ultimate test of moral independence is not whether citizens have political loyalties or ethnic attachments, but whether they can subject both to critical moral scrutiny. A society demonstrates greater moral maturity when people can celebrate their ethnic identities without using them to justify injustice; participate in politics without surrendering their conscience; and condemn wrongdoing without allowing the identity of the offender to determine their judgement.

Clearly, therefore, politics, ethnicity and morality need not collide. Their interaction becomes conflictual – and even destructive – only when either political ambition or ethnic allegiance is allowed to override moral responsibility.

As Nigeria approaches 2027, we have an opportunity to demonstrate that ethnic pride can coexist with national solidarity; political pragmatism with moral integrity, and democratic competition with mutual respect. The overall test is whether we can make political choices that recognise both the diversity of our identities and the moral obligations we share as citizens of one nation.

Sogolo is an Emeritus Professor who has taught and conducted research in Philosophy for over five decades – at the University of Ibadan, Cardiff University of Wales and currently at the National Open University of Nigeria.

World.title: NOT JUST THE ODD UNCLE
World.content:
A few ‘family’ photos might be missing some familiar faces. The G20 photo was a no-goer when a number of leaders were not willing to stand alongside a Russian representative. It is hardly surprising given the Ukraine war they started.

Another family photo missing a few faces would be the British royal family Christmas meeting where Meghan and Harry probably won’t be invited and Andrew will be warned off completely.

These are the times when we should recognise that being a boring family, clear of any political power or influence, makes for happy family photos and uneventful afternoon naps after a big Christmas meal. There are a few families Santa won’t be visiting this year.

Dennis Fitzgerald,

28 Landale St.,

Box Hill, Vic., Australia

World.title: RMRDC AND NIGERIA’S INDUSTRIAL FUTURE
World.content:
William Johnson argues why policy continuity, raw material development and institutional reforms matter

Nigeria’s quest for industrial transformation requires deliberate policies, institutional stability and sustained investment in research and development. At the centre of this aspiration is the Raw Materials Research and Development Council (RMRDC), an institution with enormous potential to drive industrialisation, economic diversification, employment generation and national prosperity.

I believe the federal government should prioritise the effective implementation and strengthening of the RMRDC Act, 2022, rather than constantly pursuing legislative changes. Frequent policy alterations create uncertainty, weaken institutional stability and discourage long-term investment. The current leadership of the Council should consolidate the achievements of previous administrations, strengthen existing programmes and introduce improvements where necessary. Institutional progress should be built on continuity, not disruption.

Equally important is the need for Nigeria to increase its capacity to produce adequate quantities of quality raw materials before making mandatory value addition the immediate priority. While value addition is desirable, imposing a compulsory 30 per cent requirement without first establishing sufficient production capacity, processing facilities, reliable electricity, transportation networks and supporting infrastructure could undermine the country’s industrial objectives.

On the 30% proposal, the idea sounds patriotic but is unrealistic in practice. Nigeria exports raw materials like lithium, cocoa, sesame and solid minerals not because of a lack of ambition, but because of a lack of the basics for processing: stable power, affordable credit, good roads, industrial water and reliable ports. A law cannot legislate away these deficits. Forcing a miner in Nasarawa or a farmer in Taraba to add 30% value where there is no factory, cold chain or power does not create industry. It creates illegality.

The 30% figure is also arbitrary. Does it mean 30% of weight, price, labour content or processing stages? That vagueness gives officials wide discretion, which in Nigeria often means rent-seeking, delays at ports and bribes to certify compliance. Instead of stopping raw export, the rule risks becoming another tollgate for exporters.

It will also hurt the very people it claims to help. Smallholder farmers and artisanal miners cannot afford processing plants. Foreign buyers will simply move to Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire, Mali or the DRC where they can buy raw materials without a forced processing requirement. When buyers leave, farm-gate prices will collapse. The farmer will not suddenly become a chocolate manufacturer. He will become poorer.

Successful value addition in Asia did not start with export bans. It started with infrastructure, industrial parks, tax holidays, subsidised energy for manufacturers and technical training. Nigeria wants to copy the outcome without building the foundation. We cannot ban our way to industrialisation.

Any legislation on mandatory value addition must therefore involve broad consultations with relevant ministries, manufacturers, research institutions, the Nigerian Export Promotion Council and private-sector stakeholders. Nigeria must first strengthen agriculture and mining, invest in research and technology, improve logistics and develop infrastructure for competitive manufacturing.

Another critical area is the RMRDC’s Technology Incubation and Pilot Plant Programme, one of the Council’s most valuable strategic assets. Before technologies from this programme are presented to investors, they must undergo proper technical validation, commercial viability assessments and market feasibility studies. Investors must be confident that the technologies are reliable, economically competitive, scalable and capable of meeting market demand. This will reduce investment risks and improve commercialisation prospects.

Institutional continuity must also become a guiding principle. Successive leaderships should not abandon valuable programmes simply because they were initiated by previous administrations. They should preserve, strengthen and expand successful initiatives while introducing new ideas to address emerging challenges.

The welfare and professional development of staff must also receive greater attention. A motivated and adequately trained workforce is essential to achieving the Council’s mandate. Investment in modern laboratories, advanced equipment, digital transformation, research funding, staff capacity building and effective performance management will significantly improve institutional productivity and research output.

Ultimately, the federal government must recognise that a strong raw materials development institution is indispensable to Nigeria’s economic future. The RMRDC should be empowered to stimulate local production, encourage research and innovation, facilitate technology transfer and establish meaningful partnerships between research institutions and the private sector.

Nigeria cannot build a sustainable industrial economy on policy uncertainty, inadequate raw material production and abandoned institutional programmes. What the country needs is consistency, strategic investment, practical reforms and leadership that understands the importance of building on existing foundations.

Johnson writes from Lagos

World.title: Babalakin Inspects MMA2 in Preparation for Regional Operations
World.content:
Chinedu Eze

The Chairman of Bi-Courtney Aviation Services Limited, Dr. Wale Babalakin, has inspected the terminal at Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal Two (MMA2), Lagos, as preparations intensify for the commencement of regional flight operations.

A statement signed by the Head, Corporate Communications, MMA2 Ajoke Yinka-Olawuyi, the inspection of the facility follows the recent signing of the settlement agreement concerning the terminal concession, thus marking a significant milestone in the resolution of the concession dispute and paving the way for the terminal to advance preparations for regional operations.

During the inspection, Babalakin visited key areas undergoing preparatory works, including the regional arrivals area, the apron extension and the staff and concessionaire access gate. The acting Chief Operating Officer and Head, Aeronautical and Cargo Services, Mr. Remi Jibodu, led the team during the inspection and presented an update on the progress of the ongoing works and preparations.

He congratulated the team on the progress recorded so far and commended their efforts towards delivering the required infrastructure within the stipulated timeline.

Speaking on the preparations, the acting Chief Executive Officer of BASL, Mrs. Idunnu Oyebolu, said the company was pursuing a dual focus: ensuring readiness for regional operations while preparing for the anticipated increase in passenger traffic during the year-end travel period.

“As we put the necessary infrastructure and operational arrangements in place for regional operations, we are equally preparing for the anticipated increase in passenger traffic during the year-end season,” she said.

World.title: Lee Group Unveils $1.8bn Industrial Park in Ogun, Targets 29 Factories, 2,500 Jobs
World.content:
Abiodun to Perform Groundbreaking November 12 as Obasanjo, Trade Minister, Industry Leaders, Diplomats and Traditional Rulers Grace Event

A $1.8 billion industrial park being developed by Lee Group of Companies Ltd along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway in Ogun State is expected to accommodate more than 29 manufacturing factories, generate over 2,500 direct and indirect jobs and further strengthen the state’s position as a leading industrial destination in Nigeria.

The 450-hectare First Industrial Park, located within the Sagamu and Obafemi-Owode local government areas of the state, is designed to accommodate manufacturing businesses across several sectors, including soap and detergent production, PVC leather manufacturing, footwear production, mould manufacturing, food processing, cosmetics, recycling and export-oriented industries.

Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, is expected to perform the groundbreaking ceremony on Thursday, November 12, 2026, marking a significant milestone in the development of the industrial project.

Former President Olusegun Obasanjo, the Minister of Trade and Investment, captains of industry, traditional rulers, members of the diplomatic community and other prominent stakeholders are also expected to attend the ceremony.

The project is expected to attract substantial domestic and foreign investment, expand Nigeria’s manufacturing capacity and create employment opportunities while strengthening Ogun State’s growing reputation as a preferred destination for industrial development.

Among the businesses associated with the project is Aspira Products Stand, a subsidiary of Lee Group of Companies, which is identified by the project information as the largest detergent company by market share in West Africa. The company plans to establish its West African regional office within the Lee Group First Industrial Park.

The proposed regional office is expected to strengthen the park’s commercial significance and position it as a potential hub for manufacturing, distribution and other business activities serving markets across West Africa.

The development is projected to have a gross development value of $3 billion, reflecting the scale of the proposed industrial ecosystem and its potential contribution to economic activities within Ogun State and beyond.

Beyond the manufacturing factories, the industrial park will feature administrative offices, residential facilities, power and utility stations, banks, shopping malls, showrooms, bonded warehouses, truck and trailer parking bays, communication facilities, conference centres and recreational facilities.

These supporting facilities are designed to create an integrated industrial environment where manufacturing, logistics, warehousing, financial services and commercial activities can operate within a coordinated location.

The park’s location along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, particularly its proximity to the Sagamu Interchange, is expected to provide businesses with access to major markets, transportation networks and logistics services. The strategic location is also expected to facilitate the movement of raw materials and finished products while improving access to distribution channels across the country.

The project is further expected to stimulate economic activities in Sagamu, Obafemi-Owode and neighbouring communities through increased demand for transportation, freight services, vehicle maintenance, accommodation, restaurants, fuel stations and other supporting businesses.

With more than 29 manufacturing factories planned for the park, the developers project that the completed facility will generate over 2,500 direct and indirect jobs. Construction activities are also expected to provide additional employment opportunities, while the factories and associated businesses will create openings for skilled and unskilled workers, young people and women.

The concentration of manufacturing companies within a single industrial development is also expected to create opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises to supply goods and services to businesses operating in the park.

In addition, the presence of established manufacturing businesses and regional operations is expected to facilitate technology transfer, technical skills development and the strengthening of local production capacity.

The planned establishment of Aspira’s West African regional office is particularly significant to the park’s ambition of attracting businesses whose operations extend beyond Nigeria. Its presence could support regional distribution networks and encourage stronger commercial linkages between Nigerian manufacturers and markets across West Africa.

The industrial park is being developed against the backdrop of Ogun State’s expanding manufacturing base, supported by its proximity to Lagos, access to major transportation corridors and established presence of manufacturing companies across several industrial sectors.

Under the administration of Governor Abiodun, Ogun State has continued to pursue investments in infrastructure and other economic enablers aimed at strengthening its attractiveness to investors and expanding opportunities for businesses.

The new industrial park is expected to complement these efforts by providing dedicated infrastructure for manufacturing and related commercial activities, while creating an environment in which businesses can benefit from shared facilities and proximity to suppliers, distributors and service providers.

By bringing multiple manufacturing operations and supporting services together, the development is designed to improve operational efficiency, encourage collaboration among businesses and create opportunities for expanded production, distribution and export activities.

The developers have also indicated that the project’s sustainability framework will incorporate environmental, social and governance considerations, with emphasis on resource efficiency, waste reduction, recycling and engagement with host communities and other stakeholders.

These measures are intended to promote responsible industrial development and encourage more sustainable production practices within the proposed industrial ecosystem.

The November 12 groundbreaking is expected to formally mark a new phase in the development of the park, with stakeholders looking towards its potential to attract further investment, strengthen manufacturing activities and stimulate commercial growth along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway corridor.

When completed, the Lee Group First Industrial Park is expected to provide a platform for manufacturing expansion, employment generation and private-sector investment, while reinforcing Ogun State’s position within Nigeria’s industrial economy.

World.title: Presidency Justifies Power Rotation, Says South’s Completion Of Eight Years Sacrosanct
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency on Sunday justified the existing power rotation between the North and the South by umploring the North to honour the current eight-year tenure being served by the South to completion, in the interest of reciprocity and national stability.

Specifically, it said Nigeria’s national stability hangs by a slender thread, demanding that the North honour the unwritten power rotation pact and allow the South to complete its full eight-year tenure, warning that breaking this foundational trust could jeopardise the country’s unity.

Personal Assistant to the President on Radio and Broadcast (Office of the Vice President), Hajya Rahma Abdulmajid, stated this in Kano during the Grand Inauguration & Strategic Media Awards Ceremony of Matan Arewa 4 Tinubu Again (MATA).

According to her, Nigeria’s power rotation arrangement is not a sectional concession but a reciprocal compact that has stabilised the Fourth Republic.

In a veiled reference to former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, who she recalled attended and participated in the famous Kaduna meeting where the power rotation agreement was reached, Abdulmajid argued that the North cannot sacrifice the stability of Nigeria for the ambition of one man.

Tracing the origin to Kaduna, she noted that when military rule ended, patriots negotiated a framework for unity, maintaining, just as he said, “And present in that room was Atiku Abubakar himself, as later confirmed by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), George Akume.

“Chief Sunday Awoniyi, the great Northern elder, stood up in 1998 and declared that the North should not field a candidate, in order to heal the wounds of June 12 and soothe the pain of the South.”

She further listed other patriots who shaped the understanding to include Dr. Chuba Okadigbo, speaking for the South; Alhaji Abubakar Rimi, speaking for the North; Dr. Alex Ekwueme, and Dr. Okwesilieze Nwodo.

Insisting on the power rotation arrangement, the presidency said, “In 1999, when the guns of military rule finally fell silent, this nation did not just switch governments—we made a sacred promise. Our founding patriots gathered in Kaduna with one urgent, defining question echo-chambered in their minds: How do we keep Nigeria one?

“And from that sacred deliberation came a compact: not a sectional concession, but a reciprocal agreement. This gentleman’s agreement decreed that power must rotate between North and South every eight years—an arrangement to guarantee fairness, to ensure stability, and to guarantee that no Nigerian ever feels like a stranger in his own country.”

On how the arrangement worked, Abdulmajid said it survived because it was honoured.

“This is not fiction. This is our history. And how did it work? It worked because we honoured it. In 1999, we gave it to the South—Chief Olusegun Obasanjo, eight years, from 1999 to 2007. Then we gave it to the North: Umaru Musa Yar’Adua in 2007. But death, a painful death, cut his tenure short in 2010.

“His vice, Goodluck Jonathan from the South, took over. The North felt cheated. The North said our turn was not complete, and that agitation was legitimate. What happened? In 2015, power returned to the North. The late former President Muhammadu Buhari, eight full years, 2015 to 2023! The sequence was restored! The principle survived,” she stated.

The presidency contended that the agreement is a two-way street and the North has already taken its full benefit.

“My people, listen to me. The agreement is reciprocal; it is a two-way street. The North has already taken its full benefit after eight solid years under Buhari. You cannot eat your cake and still demand another man’s cake,” Abdulmajid said

The presidential aide stressed that stability requires reciprocity, recalling that the current President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, a Southerner, worked tirelessly for the late General Muhammadu Buhari to emerge victorious when the North demanded power must return after Jonathan’s tenure.

“That same logic applies today. You cannot abandon a principle when it becomes inconvenient. If you do, you tell the world that the agreement was never a principle at all—merely a temporary tactic. And if we destroy trust today, what will we use to negotiate tomorrow? Let us be honest. Much of this noise against the South completing its term is not a matter of principle. It is personal ambition,” she queried.

Attributing opposition to the South completing its term to personal ambition, Abdulmajid said, “Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar tells us zoning is “self-defeating.” But he participated in and benefited from zoned arrangements in 2015 and 2019 when they favored his ambition! When rotation opened the door for him, it was acceptable. When it stands in his way, it becomes “intellectually dishonest.”

“Shall we sacrifice Nigeria’s stability for one man’s ambition? The North’s genuine interest is not served by that; the North’s interest is stable inclusion. The guarantee that power will return to you only lives if we honour the compact today.”

The presidency appealed to the North not to break the sacred promise that binds nation, urging the people of the region to rise together and complete the Southern tenure, describing it as not merely an election.

“This is for our honour. This is for reciprocity. This is for the enduring stability and peaceful coexistence of our great nation. That is exactly what the re-election of Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a second term stands for. That is the future we build today,” it added.

Also speaking, Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, corroborated Abdulmajid’s position, saying the unity of Nigeria can only be guaranteed by fair play and inclusivity.

The governor who was represented by his Director-General of Media and Publicity, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, argued that reversing the existing rotational arrangement will paint the North in ignoble light, even as he urged the region to maintain the status quo by re-electing President Tinubu for a second term.

In his remarks, former Governor of Jigawa State and immediate past Minister of Defence, Mohammad Abubakar Badaru, said the Renewed Hope Administration of President Tinubu has benefited the North more than any other part of Nigeria.

Badaru listed major completed road projects to include the 88km Zuba-Jere section and the 81km Abuja-Kaduna section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano Highway commissioned in October 2026, the 77km Kaduna-Pambeguwa road, Yakasai-Badume-Damargu-Marken Zalli roads in Kano, and the Jimeta Bridge in Yola.

On social infrastructure, Badaru cited completed health facilities such as Gadon Kaya PHC in Kano, three Polio Emergency Centers in Katsina, Kano and Sokoto, pharmacy lab at ABUTH Zaria, 50-bed mental health center at UNIMAID, and infertility center at ATBUTH Bauchi, plus ongoing upgrades at Bichi General Hospital and deployment of 79 CNG ambulances.

World.title: Tinubu Has Not Deviated An Inch from His Electricity Pledge, Says Alake
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) has said that President Bola Tinubu has not deviated from the 2023 campaign pledge to fix electricity.

It added that the administration’s quest to fix the electricity market and power sector is ongoing work.

It spokesperson, Dele Aleke, in a statement issued Sunday said as President Tinubu seeks Nigerians’ mandate for a second term in office, he would proudly present his scorecard in the power sector and clearly tell Nigerians what remains to be done,

Alake recalled that at a meeting with members of the Organised Private Sector (OPS) in Lagos ahead of the 2023 elections, then candidate Tinubu promised to tackle systemic problems in the power sector and end estimated billing.

His exact words, according to Alake: “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver.

“A fair assessment of the pledge should consider the full statement alongside the administration’s record since 2023.”

The spokesperson listed measures taken by the administration to fix the sector including the signing of the Electricity Act, 2023 on June 9, within two weeks in office, liberalising the sector and allowing states to participate in generation, distribution and transmission. Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger have set up their own regulatory agencies.

He recalled taking on over N6 trillion legacy debt accumulated from 2015 to 2025 and creating a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified debts to 21 Gencos and Discos.

Alake noted that the first and second tranches have raised over N1.2 trillion.

He added: “Launching the Presidential Metering Initiative to close the over 7 million metering gap, with over 1.5 million customers metered in the last three years.

“Aligning tariffs to cost to restore market liquidity, creating Service Bands with different tariffs, while protecting low-income households.”

Alake also mentioned the Rural Electrification Agency connecting universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power, plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre built over 60 years ago and build an East-West super grid.

He stressed that part of government’s effort included reviewing the Presidential Power Initiative (PPI) started by former President Muhammadu Buhari; signing an Acceleration Agreement in December 2023 with German partners, with FEC approving first batch of 5 TCN substations in December 2024 and second batch of eight new substations and upgrade of four existing ones in June 2026.

Alake noted: “Fixing the electricity market and power sector is ongoing work. President Tinubu has not deviated an inch from his commitment.

“As he seeks Nigerians’ mandate for a second term in office, he will proudly present his scorecard in the power sector and clearly tell Nigerians what remains to be done.”

World.title: Delimi RISE Project Launched In Kaduna To Mobilise Youths for Peacebuilding
World.content:
John Shiklam in Kaduna

The Delimi RISE Project has been launched in Kaduna State to strengthen youth participation and leadership in peacebuilding ahead of the 2027 general election.

The initiative is supported by a civil society organisation, Strengthening Peace and Resilience in Nigeria (SPRiNG) programme, funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), and implemented by Strategy, Research and Development (SRD), a pan African peacebuilding organisation established in 2022.

Executive Director of SRD, Richard Ali, said in a statement that the project would target 80 young people between the ages of 18 to 35 in Igabi, Jema’a and Kaura Local Government Areas of the state.

Ali said the initiative would begin with a “Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) style workshop, followed by peace public squares in the three local government areas and a Community of Practice to implement peacebuilding activities”.

According to him, the project would promote inclusion across ethnic, religious, gender and disability lines.

“As a peacebuilding organization, we advocated for co-existence, spaces that create equal opportunities without bias,” the statement added.

The training will cover women, youth, peace and security, peacebuilding and conflict prevention, youth leadership and participation, inclusive governance, gender equality, disability and social inclusion, as well as safeguarding and conflict sensitive approaches.

He added that the project would create opportunities for young people to participate actively in peacebuilding and community engagement.

“The project would provide young people with opportunities to contribute meaningfully to peacebuilding, promote constructive community engagement, and strengthen local resilience ahead of the 2027 elections,” Ali said.

World.title: Anneline Kriel on Donovan Marx farm attack: ‘Nothing has changed’
World.content:
Former Miss South Africa and Miss World Anneline Kriel has reacted to the news of North West farmer Donovan Marx’s attack, labelling it “cruel suffering”

The beauty queen has been vocal in showing support for farm murders and invasions, including the recent White Cross project display in Washington.

ANNELINE KRIEL REACTS TO DONOVAN MARX FARM ATTACK

On her Facebook page, Anneline Kriel reacted to the attack on North West farmer Donovan Marx.



She shared: “My heart breaks for Donovan Marx and his loved ones. No human should ever have to go through such cruel suffering. I pray with all my heart for Donovan and that God will give his family strength during this heartbreaking time.

“How much more suffering must our farming communities endure? Every life is precious, and no family should have to live in fear. May God protect our farmers and their families”.

Anneline – who won Miss South Africa and Miss World in 1973 – added that “nothing has changed” since her public protest to farm attacks in 2017.

The blonde former beauty queen also reposted a screenshot of a tweet by MK Party MP Andile Mngxitama – whom she has previously clashed with over farm attacks – which claimed Donovan Marx’s attack was “symbolic to denote the refusal of land thieves to listen”.

FARM ATTACK VICTIM TO ADVOCATE

In 2017, Anneline Kriel spoke about being a victim of a farm attack. She claimed that a young woman, who had befriended her stepdaughter, had been murdered on a farm in Stellenbosch.

“I will continue to fight this injustice”, Anneline posted on her platform last year.



Last month, Anneline Kriel shared her support for Erns Roets’s White Cross Project, which was erected in front of the Washington Monument.

“The planting of 3,000 crosses at the Washington Monument is a powerful gesture of remembrance, honouring those who have lost their lives and bringing attention to a cause that deserves to be heard.

She continued: “Thank you for standing up, raising awareness and ensuring that these lives are not forgotten. Every life matters. Every victim deserves to be remembered”.

World.title: ‘Loved-up’ Sacha and Sarah Langa make first couple appearance [video]
World.content:
Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Sarah Langa spotted together. Images via TikTok

Sarah Langa and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu have made their first public appearance as a couple. This followed days of speculation about the model and Springbok player’s relationship status.

An image of the famous flyhalf with an ex-girlfriend, and multiple deleted IG and TikTok posts, also sparked chatter about their romance

SACHA AND SARAH LANGA MAKE GLAM COUPLE APPEARANCE

Over the weekend, Sarah Langa and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu attended Skins South Africa’s Meet The Creators influencer event in Stellenbosch.



Sarah – a model and businesswoman – wore a black tuxedo-style dress, while her partner also wore black from head to toe.

The couple arrived together and, for the first time, happily posed for pics.

According to socialite Craig Jacobs, Sarah and Sacha, who have a nine-year age gap, were “loved-up”, and showed each other plenty of affection.

Take a look…

@craigsalist Loved up Sarah Langa and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu spotted on Thursday at the Skins Cosmetics launch in Stellenbosch. ♬ She's Got It – Maverick Rabbit

BACK ON AGAIN?

Over the past few days, Sarah Langa and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu sparked rumours that they had called time on their relationship, again.



The model deleted pictures and posts that feature her younger partner.

One includes a TikTok video where the model brags about receiving a Chanel handbag from her boyfriend. Another is a picture of her embracing the rugby star, which she labelled the “love of my life”.

Sacha also set tongues wagging after he deleted an image of Sarah Langa from his latest IG post.

This comes after an image of the rugby player and another woman, model Robyn Mia Peters, set tongues wagging this week. The pic reportedly dates back several years, to when the duo was dating.

World.title: Sushi and champers: Sithelo gives birth to baby girl in style
World.content:
Sithelo Shozi has given birth to her fourth child – her third daughter – with her husband, Zim businessman Kudzaishe James Magura.

The DJ and media personality gave the public a look into her delivery room, filled with sushi, champagne and elaborate flower arrangements.

Sithelo has three other children; two daughters, Florence and Coco, with ex, Andile Mpisane, and a firstborn son, Makhosini Maseko, whose father is businessman Phillip Maseko.



SITHELO SHOZI’S LUXURY LABOUR

On her social media platforms, Sithelo Shozi shared a look at the aftermath of the birth of her fourth child.

The 32-year-old had her own private room, adorned with pink balloons and elaborate floral arrangements.

She shared: “Birth plan: A sushi boat and blanc de blanc (champagne) immediately after.

The mother-of-four added that her husband had spoiled her with a luxury push present – a Hermès Birkin!

To top it all, Sithelo’s husband, Kudzaishe James Magura, doted on her hand and foot!

Take a look…



‘DEADBEAT DAD’ EX

Last month, Sithelo Shozi’s ex, Andile Mpisane, clapped back at her comments that he was a “deadbeat dad” to her two daughters, Flo and Coco.

Andile clapped back: “My responsibilities and commitment as a father should not be judged on the basis of speculation, assumptions or one-sided narratives. I have continued to contribute towards my children’s education, including paying their school fees, and I remain committed to their well-being and future.

Andile claimed that his access to his children had been “limited” and that he had recently “reconnected” with them.

World.title: Leon Schuster on Eugène Terre’Blanche prank: ‘I nearly died’ [video]
World.content:
Leon Schuster has claimed his candid camera prank with members of the Afrikaner Weerstandsbeweging (AWB) – whose leader was Eugène Terre’Blanche – was one of his most frightening experiences yet.

The veteran TV actor and comedian reflected on his most memorable movies in an interview with SABC’s Leanne Manas.

The 75-year-old also shared a health update and divulged some of his biggest regrets.



LEON SCHUSTER ON MOST FRIGHTENING TV PRANK

Although he pranked Eugène Terre’Blanche directly, Leon Schuster recalls setting up an elaborate prank in Ventersdorp, the home of the AWB leader.

Schuster told Leanne Manas about his early 90s fake tollgate prank, which fooled and angered many members of the AWB community.

Disguised as a black security guard, Schuster demanded that drivers pay a R50 toll for “reconciliation and development”.

He recalled: “Those okes are far, far right. They drive in their bakkies with their guns on the seat next to them; they will fire! They got so pissed off. I nearly died that day”.

The now 75-year-old said that he was threatened with an AK47, and even assaulted by a few.

The clip made it into his 1997 candid camera, Panic Mechanic.



Take a look…

BRINGING SOUTH AFRICANS TOGETHER

During his interview with Leanne Manas, Leon Schuster added that he had no ill intent behind his candid camera pranks, some of which have courted controversy for its portrayal of “blackface”.

He shared: “I’m a prankster, and I’ll die a prankster. It’s all part of the culture of this land”

“It’s important you know your audience. I try to give the people what they want. I’m so sorry I can’t make one final candid-camera movie. But one more clap and my neck will break”.

He added: “I want to be remembered as that okie from the Free State who stood firmly on the ground, who didnt a swollen head, and who contributed somehow to unify our nation through my movies”.

World.title: Siya Kolisi’s got the sauce! Springbok captain extends business empire
World.content:
Siya Kolisi’s officially got the sauce – after collaborating with Nando’s to create a new condiment. The news comes days after reports that the Springbok captain joined restaurant group Life & Brand Portfolio as a stakeholder.

SIYA KOLISI UNVEILS NANDO’S SAUCE

On social media, several content creators have teased the release of Siya’s Sauce, in collaboration with Nando’s

The sauce – which will reflect the flavours of the Springbok captain – will officially be rolled out in stores on Tuesday, 3 November.



The launch coincided with the opening of the new Nando’s restaurant in Stellenbosch.

EXTENDING HIS BUSINESS INTERESTS

Last month, Siya Kolisi announced that he had acquired a 5% stake in South African restaurant group Life & Brand Portfolio, which owns brands including Tiger’s Milk, La Parada, Harbour House and Old Town Italy.

The Springbok captain is expected to contribute to marketing, business development and the conceptualisation of new restaurant offerings, bringing his ideas and South African cultural influences into the group’s brands.

Siya has also expressed an interest in creating experiences that bring people together through food, sport, music and community events, while using the partnership to support youth and community development.

In a statement, the 35-year-old said of his new role: “It’s a big honour for me. I think I’m at the stage of my life where I’m closer to the end of my career. And it’s daunting to think about what you’re going to do after



He added: “I think the idea is how we can bring more people together. Doing sports, making it more fun, having competitions and all kinds of things. I think we want to bring people together to talk”.

World.title: Da Cruz has a plan for Kaizer Chiefs’ biggest problem
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have fallen 12 points behind Mamelodi Sundowns after another inconsistent spell in the league.

A series of draws has proved particularly costly, leaving Amakhosi struggling to keep pace with their title rivals.

FERNANDO DA CRUZ: KAIZER CHIEFS NEED WINNING RUN TO REVIVE TITLE CHALLENGE

Da Cruz admits that the situation has become more complicated following their latest setback. However, the French tactician believes the return of injured players could give his team the consistency they have lacked throughout the campaign.



“It’s more difficult today [Saturday] after this game, but the PSL is a long journey, there are 21 fixtures remaining. When we recover our injured players, where we have been unlucky since the beginning of the season, we will have more consistency in our performances, because we made a lot of draws this season,” Da Cruz said.

The Amakhosi coach believes his team have dropped points in matches where they were capable of collecting maximum points.

However, he also acknowledged that a lack of experience has contributed to their inability to turn promising performances into victories.



For Da Cruz, the immediate priority is getting his injured players back and building the momentum needed to close the gap at the top of the standings.

“Normally, many draws, we deserved to win these games but because of our lack of experience, we didn’t win these games. But we will turn it on our side when we recover our squad and for sure, in one moment we must have some positive dynamic with a few wins in a row to continue this journey. We must keep a positive mindset,” he added.

Chiefs cannot afford many more dropped points if they are serious about challenging for the Betway Premiership title.



With Orlando Pirates and Sundowns setting the pace, Amakhosi need to put together a strong run of results rather than relying on their rivals to slip up.

Da Cruz, however, remains convinced that the campaign is far from over. His message is clear: Chiefs must stay positive, recover their squad and start winning consistently if they are to make a serious challenge for the championship.
