World.title: Nkana sanctioned over ilampi chants
World.content:
Nkana Football Club says it respects the ruling issued by the Football Association of Zambia -FAZ- Disciplinary Committee dated 30th October 2026.

The ruling follows a complaint lodged by the Zambian Premier League -ZPL- concerning the chanting of political slogans by a section of supporters during the MTN Super League fixture against Makeni All Stars FC at Nkana Stadium on 10th October 2026.

In a statement issued by Media and Communications Manager Mike Mubanga, the club says it was asked to show cause why disciplinary action should not be taken and subsequently submitted its response expressing regret and outlining measures to prevent recurrence.

In its ruling, the Disciplinary Committee found the club guilty and imposed a fine of K100,000 alongside a sanction requiring the club to play its next five home matches at a neutral venue situated at least 300 kilometres from Nkana Stadium without spectators.

The Committee however, having considered the club’s remorse and remedial measures, ordered the partial suspension of the implementation of the five-match sanction to provide the club an opportunity to demonstrate improved conduct for the remainder of the season.

Nkana FC says it is committed to complying with the directives and will continue engaging relevant football authorities to ensure similar incidents do not recur.

The club notes the ruling has significant financial, logistical and sporting implications and would deprive the Kalampa faithful of the opportunity to support their team at home.

The club has therefore appealed to supporters to exercise restraint, respect football rules and refrain from chants or conduct that could expose the club to further disciplinary action.

World.title: Nkana content with derby draw against Power
World.content:
Nkana coach Elijah Tana has expressed satisfaction with the goalless draw against Power Dynamos in the Kitwe derby played at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola on Saturday.

Near misses were the hallmark of the derby as Nkana keeper William Mtonga denied Power a win with crucial saves in both halves.

It was a match Super League champions Power dominated with Nkana showing flashes of brilliance.

Power striker Andy Boyeli came close to opening the scoring when he missed from inside the box with keeper Mtonga off his line after 14 minutes.

There were also misses from Boyeli’s teammates Joshua Mutale and Ismael Ankobo in the first half before the crossbar denied Power.

Nkana striker Lazarus Kambole will go home kicking himself after misdirecting a shot within the box when set up by winger Charles Zulu.

In a post-match comment, Tana said he was happy with the one point Nkana earned from the derby.

“I’m happy with the clean sheet. Credit to the boys for getting one point from the derby,” Tana said.

“I told my boys at half time to be cautious. This is a new team with energetic boys so I will keep pushing on the boys,” he said.

Tana further saluted the conduct of the usually controversial Nkana supporters.

“Our fans should continue conducting themselves well like they did today. I’m happy with the conduct of our fans and they must continue,” he said.

Meanwhile, Power assistant coach Linos Makwaza lamented the missed opportunities in the derby.

“It was a very tough game. Nkana played with positive energy and as Power Dynamos we created a lot of chances,” Makwaza said.

Nkana are third in Stream A with ten points and Power are placed fifth on the table with seven points after five matches played.

New Minister of Youth and Sport Likando Mufalali was among thousands of spectators who thronged Levy Mwanawasa Stadium for the biggest match on the local football front.

World.title: Energy expert welcomes splitting of ministries
World.content:
An energy expert, Bornface Zulu, has described the creation of the Ministry of Petroleum and Ministry of Electricity as a strategic governance reform.

Mr Zulu says the decision to split the Ministry of Energy into the two ministries reflects the growing complexity of Zambia’s energy sector and the need for specialised leadership, accountability and policy focus.

Speaking in an interview with the media Mr Zulu says Electricity and Petroleum have evolved into distinct industries with different technical demands, investment requirements and national security implications.

He said managing both under one ministry increasingly risked diluting attention and slowing critical decision-making.

Mr Zulu added that one ministry was expected to simultaneously address load shedding, generation planning, transmission investment, fuel security, storage infrastructure and international petroleum market developments which became unsustainable in the long run.

“For many years, the Ministry of Energy was responsible for electricity generation, transmission, power trading, renewable energy development, fuel procurement, petroleum storage, strategic reserves, and broader energy policy. While this structure worked historically, the rapid expansion of both subsectors created what can be described as a governance capacity challenge,” he said.

Mr Zulu further commended the decision saying it is in line with regional best practices citing Angola and South Africa.

He said Zambia is not alone in adopting specialized approaches to energy governance stating that as the energy sector becomes larger and more complex, governance structures must evolve accordingly.

“South Africa restructured aspects of its energy governance framework to provide greater attention to electricity security and power sector reforms. Angola similarly maintains separate institutional arrangements for petroleum and electricity oversight, recognizing the unique strategic importance of each sector,” Mr Zulu said.

Government recently increased the number of ministries from 24 to 30 with the Ministry of Energy among those that were split into the Ministries of Petroleum and Electricity.

World.title: Malawi: Police Confirm Egyptian Deputy Ambassador Beaten in Lilongwe Attack
World.content:
A senior Egyptian diplomat has been hospitalised after being attacked and beaten in Lilongwe, sparking a police investigation into the shocking assault.

National Police spokesperson Gladys Chiwaula confirmed that Egypt's Deputy Ambassador to Malawi was admitted to a hospital in the capital after the attack.

"Police are following up on the matter and will give more details later," she said.

Chiwaula gave few details.

She did not say where the attack happened, what led to it, or how serious the diplomat's injuries are. Police have also withheld the deputy ambassador's name.

Officers say they are investigating, but the incident is likely to raise alarm over the safety of foreign envoys in the country.

World.title: Africa: From Commonwealth Connections to Economic Opportunity - Expanding Africa-Caribbean Trade Linkages
World.content:
guest column

When Commonwealth leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda this November, they will confront rising trade tensions, geopolitical shocks and supply chain disruption alongside longstanding challenges, such as high debt, limited affordable finance, climate exposure and poor connectivity.

Across Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean, these pressures make diversifying markets, attracting productive investment and building resilience through trade even more urgent. They also increase the importance of regional and cross-regional value chains that can withstand disruptions to established trade relationships.

One opportunity lies in plain sight: stronger Africa-Caribbean economic connections. Shared history, culture and diaspora relationships provide a foundation, as do common ambitions to diversify exports, add value locally and create opportunities for small businesses, including those led by women and young entrepreneurs.

The institutional landscape is also changing. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is building a framework for trade including goods, services, investment and digital commerce, while the Caribbean is deepening the CARICOM Single Market and Economy.



Connecting these integration efforts across the Atlantic could help firms aggregate supply and demand, build scale, and develop regional value chains. and access larger markets. A bigger, more integrated market can improve the commercial case for investment and the economics of cross-regional trade.

Forthcoming analysis by the International Trade Centre (ITC), undertaken with the support of Afreximbank, points to considerable unrealised trade potential between Africa and the Caribbean. But the numbers tell only part of the story.

In a survey of 1,175 businesses and business support organisations only 10% of African companies and 12% of Caribbean companies reported trading with the other region. Yet among those that did, 79% of African firms and 82% of Caribbean firms described their experience positively or very positively. The challenge is less about potential than removing barriers to scale.

Businesses struggle to access reliable market information, trusted partners and appropriate finance, as well as to navigate standards and move goods efficiently.

These constraints are not new. Low trade volumes weaken direct transport links; poor connectivity raises costs; limited commercial relationships restrict information; and smaller transactions are harder to finance.

The priority is to tackle these challenges in a comprehensive way.

Physical distance remains particularly costly. ITC estimates freight costs on African exports to the Caribbean at almost 20% of shipment value, compared with just over 8% for African exports globally. Caribbean exports to Africa face costs approaching 22%. Limited routes and fragmented networks continue to undermine viable trade. Scheduled direct air services between Lagos and Barbados, launched in 2026, illustrate how improved connections can support business travel, tourism and wider services.

Access to finance depends not only on the availability of capital, but on whether viable opportunities can be connected to appropriate financing. Businesses need guidance on available funding and lender requirements, and financial institutions need appropriate instruments and ways to manage risk. Trade finance, working-capital facilities, guarantees and risk-sharing mechanisms can all bridge these gaps.

Payments also matter, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Slow, costly or uncertain transfers can derail transactions. More efficient cross-border payment systems would reduce both transaction costs and risks. Africa's Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) offers useful lessons for simplifying payments as financial links with the Caribbean deepen.

Beyond trade volumes, value creation extends beyond goods. Services, digital solutions and the creative industries can generate more value within both regions. Africa and the Caribbean have globally recognised cultural assets and extensive diasporas, yet much of the creative value is captured elsewhere. Creators and firms need finance, workable payments, intellectual property expertise, distribution channels and direct access to buyers and investors. Supporting creative businesses, rather than only promoting cultural exchange, would generate more revenue and help jobs remain in local economies.

Governments and institutions can create the enabling environment, but businesses will ultimately determine whether a new chapter in Africa–Caribbean economic relations succeed, especially for SMEs.

Commonwealth trade and investment platforms can connect policymakers, investors, entrepreneurs and business leaders. They offer a way to identify obstacles that no single firm or government can resolve alone. Success, however, means introductions becoming contracts, investment reaching viable enterprises and businesses entering new markets.

The Commonwealth brings an existing economic advantage to this endeavour. The opportunity is to make that advantage work more deliberately for Africa–Caribbean commerce, where physical distance, limited market information and still-thin commercial networks continue to constrain trade.

Through its Working Group on Trade and Investment, member countries are developing a workplan to expand intra-Commonwealth commerce. Cooperation on compatible regulations, mutual recognition of standards and qualifications, and simpler border procedures can help realise these gains.

Close 

ITC's work on investment promotion and digital trade to women's economic empowerment, small-state resilience and emerging Africa–Caribbean business linkages can advance this agenda. Afreximbank's Global Africa vision brings the finance, investment and commercial infrastructure required to turn diaspora ties into sustainable economic relationships.

These capabilities are complementary. Trade policy can open markets; finance helps businesses act; and enterprises sustain commercial relationships.

The practical test is clear: identify viable opportunities, mobilise investment, resolve logistics, finance and payment barriers, connect SMEs to customers and investors, use digital trade to overcome distance and retain more value within regions. Progress should then be measured in transactions, market access and sustainable business relationships.

As leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda, they can demonstrate how a connected Commonwealth can convert partnerships into investment, enterprise and shared prosperity.

World.title: South Africa: African Horse Sickness Confirmed in Western Cape's Cederberg
World.content:
The Department of Agriculture has confirmed a case of African horse sickness (AHS) in a single horse on a property in the Cederberg Local Municipality in the Western Cape, prompting movement restrictions and intensified surveillance to contain the disease.

Laboratory tests conducted by the University of Pretoria's Veterinary Genetics Laboratory confirmed the presence of AHS virus serotype 7 on the property, which is located within South Africa's established AHS Protection Zone.

Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp said the case was detected through the country's veterinary surveillance systems, enabling authorities to respond swiftly and implement containment measures.

"The swift detection of this case in the Cederberg Local Municipality is a good example of how South Africa's veterinary surveillance system works. As a result, the authorities were able to move quickly to the affected area and take the required stringent actions as stipulated in the Animal Diseases Act and deploy containment protocols," Aucamp said.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In accordance with the Animal Diseases Act, 1984 (Act 35 of 1984), and the Western Cape Department of Agriculture's AHS contingency plan, an outbreak containment area has been established and movement controls implemented.

Horse movements within the controlled area ordinarily require a permit issued by the State Veterinarian: Boland. However, the department has advised that no permits will be issued for moving horses out of the affected area, while investigations and surveillance continue.

Veterinary Services, working with authorised veterinarians and industry partners, have also commenced intensive surveillance, tracing and census activities to determine the extent of the outbreak and identify any additional cases.

The department has urged equine owners in the controlled area to cooperate with Veterinary Services and report any animals showing signs consistent with AHS, including unexplained fever, swelling of the head or neck, breathing difficulties or sudden death.

Horse owners are also encouraged to take precautions against Culicoides midges, which transmit the disease. Recommended measures include stabling horses, where possible, from two hours before sunset until two hours after sunrise, avoiding low-lying and wet areas, and appropriately using registered insect repellents and insecticides.

The department has strongly discouraged AHS vaccination at this time, explaining that the currently registered vaccine is live-attenuated and that vaccination during periods of vector activity could result in the vaccine strain being spread by midges, potentially worsening the situation.

Close 

"While there is no proof of large-scale disease activity outside the said property, the department is focused on total vigilance and calls on all horse owners to refrain from AHS vaccination during this period. Veterinary Services will continue to monitor the situation closely and will provide updates as additional information becomes available," Aucamp said.

The department said international trade partners will be notified of the outbreak, with further information on the implications for international trade to be provided in due course.

Updates on containment measures, movement restrictions and permits will be issued by the Western Cape Department of Agriculture. Further information is available from Veterinary Services and at www.myhorse.org.za

World.title: Kenya: No, Kenyan Pastor Victor Kanyari Was Not Killed in a Road Accident
World.content:
No, Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari was not killed in a road accident

IN SHORT: A fake Citizen Digital news graphic claims Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari died in a road accident. But the image is fabricated and uses an old photograph of a separate crash.

Social media posts circulating in Kenya feature what appears to be a Citizen Digital breaking news alert, dated 5 October 2026. It claims that pastor Victor Kanyari has died in a road accident along Kangundo Road in the capital, Nairobi.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The graphic shows Kanyari alongside a badly damaged white vehicle surrounded by onlookers.

Collectively, the posts we sampled received more than 162,000 views and 2,000 likes.

Who is Kanyari?

Kanyari is a Kenyan preacher who heads the Salvation Healing Ministry in Nairobi. He made headlines in 2014 after a KTN investigation exposed staged miracles at his ministry and his controversial KSh310 donation scheme, which he later acknowledged was intended to lift him out of poverty.

Kanyari was previously married to gospel singer Beatrice Wairimu Mbugua, popularly known as Betty Bayo. They had two children. Bayo died of leukaemia on 10 November 2025, prompting a custody dispute between Kanyari and the children's stepfather, Hiram Gitau, popularly known as Tash.

On 26 October 2026, a court awarded Kanyari legal custody but ordered a gradual transition, allowing the children to remain temporarily with Tash.

The dispute, along with his active social media presence, has kept Kanyari in the public eye. He has also announced plans to contest the Kasarani parliamentary seat in Kenya's 2027 general election.

Citizen Digital is the online news platform of Citizen TV, owned by Royal Media Services.

But did the broadcaster report Kanyari's death in a road accident? We checked.

Old accident photo used in fake graphic

We found no credible news reports confirming Kanyari's alleged death or a corresponding report on Citizen Digital or Citizen TV's social media accounts.

In contrast, Kanyari's social media accounts feature recent photos and videos of him going about his usual activities.

A reverse image search revealed that the photo of the wrecked vehicle had been shared on Facebook on 27 June 2024, more than two years before the supposed news alert.

Close 

The earlier post was captioned: "Bad accident on Ngong road joining on to Karen road. Multiple casualties."

The vehicle and onlookers match those in the circulating graphic, confirming the photograph predates the alleged October 2026 crash.

The graphic is fabricated. It uses an old accident photo to support a false claim about Kanyari's death. His recent public activities also contradict the rumour.

World.title: Kenya: 46 Ebola Contacts Set for Discharge From Quarantine On November 3
World.content:
Nairobi — Public Health Principal Secretary May Muthoni says 46 contacts under quarantine are expected to be discharged on November 3 after completing the required monitoring period.

Muthoni has directed health teams to prepare the necessary discharge packages and support for those completing quarantine.

"We must also be able to complete the full 21 days of followup and every person leaving quarantine must receive the agreed discharge package and support... we must also continue to follow up the nine contacts outside Kenya with the countries concerned," she said.



She said every person leaving quarantine must receive the agreed assistance as authorities maintain surveillance to prevent further transmission.

The PS urged response teams to ensure all arrangements are in place ahead of Tuesday's planned discharge.

"Kenya is making progress in containing the Ebola outbreak, with no new cases reported in the last 10 days, following coordinated efforts by the Ministry of Health, County Governments and development partners," Muthoni stated.

So far, the country has recorded nine cases and two deaths;.

Following confirmation of the first Ebola case on 6 October, the health ministry conducted "robust contact tracing of anyone who may have been exposed", the World Health Organization (WHO) says. By 22 October, all contacts had been traced, both in Kenya and internationally, and placed in quarantine, it adds.

The government says that the confirmed cases so far are connected and there is no evidence that the virus has spread to the community.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Four in Plateau Community Despite Curfew
World.content:
The attackers reportedly stormed the community at about 8 p.m. and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to contain insecurity.

At least four people were killed after gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night.

The attackers reportedly stormed the community at about 8 p.m. and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to contain insecurity.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

A resident of Barkin Ladi, Bulus Jok, said the gunmen operated freely for some time, shooting indiscriminately.

"The gunmen struck the community around 8 p.m. despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically," Mr Jok said.

He added that the attack threw residents into panic, leaving four people dead.

Mr Jok expressed concern that the incident occurred despite an early warning reportedly sent to relevant authorities a day before the attack.

"It is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack," he said.

The Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the incident.

Mr Tengwong condemned the killings, describing the attack as unacceptable and expressing concern over the continued assaults on communities despite security measures.

He urged security agencies to intensify surveillance, strengthen their presence in vulnerable communities and respond promptly to intelligence and early warning reports to prevent further attacks.

The latest incident adds to the series of attacks on communities in Plateau State, raising fresh concerns about the effectiveness of security measures, including curfews, in protecting residents.

Efforts to reach security operatives for official confirmation and further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

World.title: Ethiopia: U.S. Customs Releases Ethiopia-Made Solar Cell Shipments After Supply Chain Review
World.content:
Addis Abeba — US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has released shipments of solar cells manufactured at a Japanese company's facility in Ethiopia following a review of its supply chain documentation, SolarQuarter reported.

TOYO Co., Ltd., a Japan-headquartered solar manufacturing company, announced on 29 October that CBP had completed its review after the company submitted documentation demonstrating the traceability of its supply chain, including the origins of polysilicon and wafers used in manufacturing the solar cells.

The company said it cooperated with US authorities throughout the review process and provided detailed documentation on the sourcing of its production materials.

The release of the shipments comes as TOYO seeks to expand its international manufacturing operations and strengthen its presence in the US market. The company operates a manufacturing facility in Humble, Texas, and is pursuing certification under CBP's Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) programme, which is designed to strengthen supply chain security and import compliance.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

TOYO Chief Executive Officer Takahiko Onozuka welcomed the completion of the review, expressing appreciation for what he described as CBP's professional approach. He said the company remained committed to transparency and regulatory compliance as it expands its US operations.

Onozuka also stressed the importance of providing customers with confidence in the origins of solar products through greater supply chain traceability.

The development highlights the importance of supply chain documentation and regulatory compliance for solar manufacturers operating across multiple countries, particularly as scrutiny of the origins of imported products increases.

The release of the shipments follows an ongoing US investigation into whether solar cell manufacturers operating in Ethiopia are circumventing existing American trade duties on Chinese solar products.

In July 2026, Addis Standard reported that the US Department of Commerce had launched a country-wide investigation into imports of silicon solar cells from Ethiopia to determine whether they were circumventing longstanding antidumping and countervailing duty (AD/CVD) orders on Chinese solar products.

The investigation followed a petition filed in May 2026 by eight US solar manufacturers -- DYCM Power, First Solar, Qcells, Silfab, Solx, Suniva, Swift Solar and Talon PV -- alleging that two manufacturers operating in Ethiopia, TOYO and Origin Solar, were using Chinese-origin wafers to produce solar cells in Ethiopia before assembling them into solar modules locally or in Vietnam for export to the US.

According to the petition, nearly 70% of finished solar modules exported from Ethiopia contained Chinese components and underwent processing allegedly covered by existing US trade restrictions. Solar Power World reported that imports of Ethiopia-origin solar cells and modules, which were virtually nonexistent before July 2025, reached an estimated $277 million in the second half of that year, with shipments continuing to increase in 2026.

The petitioners argued that the surge in exports coincided with increased shipments of key solar manufacturing inputs from China to Ethiopia. Both TOYO and Origin Solar subsequently submitted factual information to the Department of Commerce in response to the allegations.

The investigation is expected to reach a preliminary determination by 10 December 2026, with a final decision anticipated around 10 May 2027. In the meantime, US Customs and Border Protection was instructed to suspend liquidation of relevant imports and apply cash deposit requirements pending the outcome. Any duties imposed could be applied retroactively to the investigation's initiation date.

Close 

The dispute first emerged publicly in May 2026, when Addis Standard, citing Reuters, reported that a coalition of US solar manufacturers had petitioned the Department of Commerce to investigate imports from Ethiopia over alleged tariff circumvention.

The petition came weeks after Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated solar manufacturing facilities at Hawassa Industrial Park on 25 April 2026. According to state media, the facilities included TOYO Phase 2, Origin and Lumintech, which were expected to have a combined annual production capacity of 11.3 gigawatts.

At the inauguration, Abiy said the projects reflected Ethiopia's ambition to expand its industrial base and renewable energy sector.

World.title: Ethiopia: 'Ethiopia's Return to a Sea Port Is Inevitable': Navy Commander Calls for Regional Maritime Cooperation
World.content:
Addis Abeba — Ethiopian Navy Commander Vice Admiral Kindu Gezu has called for closer regional cooperation and dialogue on maritime security, saying Ethiopia's return to a seaport is inevitable and requires stronger engagement with neighboring countries.

"Since Ethiopia's return to a sea port is inevitable, working closely and through dialogue with regional countries is essential," Kindu said on Friday, a day after the conclusion of a regional maritime security forum organized by the Ethiopian Navy Headquarters, according to the army.

The forum brought together naval commanders and representatives from Yemen, Oman, Djibouti, Somaliland, and Puntland to exchange experiences and explore joint approaches to maritime search and rescue operations and regional security challenges. ENDF said the forum was organized with the support of the European Union.

Kindu described the gathering as "the first of its kind in Ethiopia" to discuss regional maritime search and rescue plans, saying it demonstrated the Ethiopian Navy's growing capabilities and readiness to engage in regional and continental maritime affairs.



He also highlighted growing security challenges around the Strait of Hormuz, warning that threats in the area could increasingly affect the wider region. No country, regardless of its strength, could independently ensure maritime security or resolve emerging challenges, he said, emphasizing the need for countries of different sizes to pool their capabilities.

"The participating countries of the forum must work together to solve the problems observed in the region," Kindu said, adding that regional cooperation was essential to addressing maritime threats and ensuring safe maritime movement.

Ethiopian Navy Deputy Commander for Operations Commodore Jemal Tufisa said the forum had helped establish practical foundations for regional cooperation through cross-border information sharing, identifying areas of concern, and conducting joint operational exercises.

"We trust that upon returning to your respective countries, you will translate the lessons gained from the workshop into action, working effectively on regional maritime security and performing tasks with international acceptance," Jemal said.

Rear Admiral Kenneth Nyagah, a search and rescue project expert, and Master Kuraja Mishini, manager of the Djibouti Code of Conduct, commended the Ethiopian Navy's initiative in creating communication channels for information sharing, coordinated decision-making, and joint responses to regional threats. Both expressed their commitment to continued cooperation.

Close 

The forum concluded on Thursday with discussions on "existing maritime security conditions and potential future scenarios", including the actions participating countries should take in responding to specific emergencies and threats.

"TODAY" co-host Savannah Guthrie issued a new plea for information about her missing mother, Nancy Guthrie, on Sunday, nine months after the 84-year-old was abducted from her Tucson, Arizona, home.

Guthrie shared an old drawing made by her daughter, Vale, showing a blue umbrella in the rain and the words, "I know it might not seem like it, but I really need my mommy."

"Found this old drawing from my daughter today," Guthrie wrote on Instagram. "It says so much about how I feel."

"The world goes on, things appear ‘normal’ — as we try to keep going and be strong, especially for our young kids — but it’s not and it never will be," she continued.

SAVANNAH GUTHRIE URGES PUBLIC TO HELP FIND MISSING MOTHER NANCY IN EMOTIONAL MOTHER’S DAY POST

THREE MONTHS AFTER NANCY GUTHRIE'S ABDUCTION, SHERIFF'S OFFICE RENEWS PLEA AS KEY QUESTIONS REMAIN UNANSWERED

Nancy Guthrie was reported missing Feb. 1 after she was last seen at her home in the Catalina Foothills area near Tucson shortly before 10 p.m. Jan. 31.

Authorities believe she was taken against her will.

A masked, armed individual was captured on the home's doorbell camera footage, apparently tampering with the device.

The FBI and Pima County Sheriff’s Department have not identified a suspect, and no arrests have been made.

SAVANNAH GUTHRIE WAS 'SURPRISED AND DISMAYED' BY DOUBTS SHE WOULD RETURN TO 'TODAY' AFTER MOM'S DISAPPEARANCE

Guthrie has continued to push for answers about her mother’s disappearance while returning to work on "TODAY."

During a June appearance on "TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle," she rejected the idea that she had forgotten about her mother.

"I know maybe people wonder, ‘What’s going on? How is she able to do that job? Is she not thinking about it? Did she forget?’ No. Never," Guthrie said.

"It’s always with me. I cry every morning on the way to work, and I cry every morning on the way home," she added.

SAVANNAH GUTHRIE DELIVERS 'VERY SPECIFIC' MESSAGE TO MOM'S KIDNAPPER 25 WEEKS AFTER HER ABDUCTION

In August, six months after her mother's disappearance, Guthrie and her siblings also issued a statement asking for information about their mother.

"Every day, we wake up and try to be strong and go on — because that’s what our joyful and resilient Mom taught us to do. But make no mistake — our hearts are in ruins," Guthrie wrote. "Cam and Kristine, Annie and Tommy, Mike and me — we spend every waking moment thinking of her, longing for her, looking for her."

The Pima County Sheriff’s Department said Friday the Nancy Guthrie Task Force was continuing to work with laboratories to advance DNA analysis.

"Earlier this month, investigators traveled to Florida to meet with lab scientists to see what more could be done to advance this case," the department wrote on X. "A number of ideas were discussed, and we continue to work with all our partners to solve this case."

The agency reminded the public that no tip is too small.

Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos previously said Guthrie "did not leave on her own."

NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER

Authorities released the contents of two ransom notes in July. The first, sent Feb. 2, claimed Guthrie was safe and demanded $4 million in bitcoin for her release.

The second, sent four days later, claimed she had died shortly after being kidnapped.

Investigators said the notes contained distinctive writing patterns and asked anyone who recognized the style to contact authorities.

FLORIDA STATE FIRES AD MICHAEL ALFORD, AS MIKE NORVELL’S SEAT REACHES A BOILING POINT IN TALLAHASSEE

Unfortunately for Florida State fans who were sick of losing, Norvell had secured a contract extension that included a buyout that will pay him $50.3 million to hit the unemployment line.

"We have made the decision to change the leadership of our football program," President Richard McCullough said. "We thank Mike Norvell for his commitment and service to Florida State and wish him and his family the very best. We understand the deep passion of Seminole fans and share their high expectations for this program."

Florida State hiring a new AD, while also making the move on Norvell

Adding to the ongoing problems at FSU, the school announced in September that athletic director Michael Alford was being fired, creating a conundrum for school officials who were hoping Norvell would win enough games this season to gain enough support from fans to return in 2027.

To make matters worse for those within the FSU administration, social media had a field day this weekend over a plane flying a banner that called for the school to fire Norvell, even if it incorrectly spelled the head coach’s name.

Right now, we are living in an era of college sports where, if you get too far behind, you'll be lucky to recover, given the ever-changing world of NIL and the transfer portal.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S MEGA ROSTERS AREN’T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON PROVE

You can't sell the future when school officials are essentially operating its football program on a year-to-year basis, considering the amount of money needed to field a roster.

Also, Mike Norvell was obviously waiting around to see when the school would finally make a decision, as he hosted a number of recruits on Sunday.

World.title: Federal judge dismisses Trump attempt to interfere in Alaska Senate race
World.content:
A federal judge in Alaska on Sunday dismissed the Trump administration’s lawsuit seeking to separate and preserve certain ballots in the state’s upcoming Senate election, where GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola.

In the last week, Peltola’s campaign has faced scrutiny after The New York Times reported the campaign and other Democrats recruited a candidate — Dan J. Sullivan — to run for the Senate with the same name as the incumbent senator.

Citing potential voter confusion, the Trump administration sought to separate and preserve ballots with votes for Dan J. Sullivan, arguing that if the incumbent loses, it may be because people voted for the other Sullivan by mistake.

In her ruling, U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason voiced concerns about voters’ right to a secret ballot.

“The absence of any explanation from the United States as to how its requested relief could redress its alleged injury while simultaneously maintaining the secrecy of the ballot is telling,” Gleason wrote.

Later, she added: “Requiring the segregation of ballots cast by voters for Daniel J. Sullivan so that these voters can be further investigated by law enforcement is not a remedy that this Court can or should order as it clearly violate Alaskans’ right to a secret ballot.”

The lawsuit also sought to block the certification of the Senate election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. On Saturday, the Republican-led state government in Alaska implored a federal judge to prevent that effort in a court filing.

In response to the ruling, a spokesperson for Peltola’s campaign told NBC News, “No sham investigation or baseless lawsuit from a weaponized Department of Justice is going to stop Alaskans from electing Mary on November 3rd so she can lower costs for Alaska’s working families. Alaskans will choose their next U.S. Senator — not Dan Sullivan or his DC allies.”

Shortly after the judge’s ruling, the Justice Department appealed.

“The court dismissed the case on procedural grounds but did not dispute the argument of the United States that Daniel J. Sullivan (a/k/a Decoy Dan) entered the race as a frivolous candidate to confuse voters. DOJ plans to file a notice of appeal. Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes,” a department spokesperson said.

Republicans have criticized Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot for months, after he won a primary bid to be the fourth candidate on the general election ballot in August. The senator and his GOP allies long accused Democrats of recruiting the second Sullivan, a charge Peltola and her campaign have repeatedly denied.

President Donald Trump accused Dan. J Sullivan of committing a “criminal act” Sunday on Truth Social.

“The Fake Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr., has DISAPPEARED! Nobody can find him, including Law Enforcement. He knows that he committed a Criminal Act,” the president wrote.

Last week, the Times report cited on-the-record comments from Peltola’s former campaign manager, who was fired in August, about the campaign’s efforts to recruit a second Dan Sullivan to run for office. The campaign manager and several unnamed sources said operatives from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee joined the effort. Elisa Rios, the campaign manager who was fired, later sought to retract her comments.

On Sunday, the senator called Democrats’ effort “rigged and corrupt” in a CNN interview. He added that no matter the outcome, “I’m going to accept the election results.”

World.title: Democrats in key battlegrounds throw Joe Biden under the bus on the border
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Democratic candidates in 2026 battleground races are directly criticizing Joe Biden’s handling of border security when he was president, seeking to neutralize a political vulnerability and signaling a new path for the party on the thorny issue.

Candidates are throwing the ex-president under the bus on border policy in key states that will decide control of the Senate and some battleground House races across the country.

“I called out Joe Biden for failing us on the border,” Texas’ Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico says in a recent ad airing in the closing stretch of his neck-and-neck race against Republican Ken Paxton. He also criticized Biden in July for having “failed us on our southern border” as he rolled out his own border security plan.

He’s not alone.

In Kansas, a longtime Republican stronghold, Democrat Adam Hamilton criticized Biden in a recent debate with Republican Sen. Roger Marshall.

“I want to be crystal clear, first of all: Immigration at the border under Biden was a disaster. That is how we ended up where we are today,” he said. “Second, what we did in response to that has been a disaster for people across the state of Kansas.”

Hamilton, like other Democrats in areas that voted for Trump in 2024, paired his critique of Biden with criticism that the current president has gone too far on enforcement. Polls show many Americans have soured on Trump’s handling of the issue in the wake of immigration officers fatally shooting two Americans in Minnesota and one in Maine this year.

Still, the comments reflect a recognition that the issue of border security remains a vulnerability for Democrats as Republicans continue to accuse them of promoting “open borders” in a bid to mobilize their base and win swing voters. Biden’s ratings on the issue tanked amid a surge in migrant crossings during his presidency, which Trump successfully weaponized in 2024.

Entering office in 2021, Biden inherited a Covid-era migration surge that intensified in the United States after he made good on his pledge to roll back Trump-era policies and restrictions, allowing more asylum-seekers to stay in the country as their cases were being considered. The collective result was a huge spike in border crossings that became associated with the Biden presidency and brought down his approval ratings.

Even as Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 38%, polls show border security continues to be one of his highest-polling issues, although that number has fallen from the highs of his early second term.

“The Biden administration failed at the border,” Democratic House candidate Paige Cognetti said at a debate Thursday night.

Cognetti, who is vying to unseat Rep. Rob Bresnahan, R-Pa., in a highly competitive Scranton-area working-class district, later added: “The Biden administration did fail. We need to make sure that the border is secure. It’s a good thing that it is. We do need to make sure that the pathways to citizenship are there.”

In South Carolina, Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews said in a debate, “Democrats have failed on the border.”

Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said it’s “very smart” for candidates to distance themselves from Biden and that “there’s nobody contesting that interpretation” that he blundered on the border.

In the 2024 election, “immigration was playing a major, major role, and it was energizing Republicans. And it was the best issue among swing voters for Republicans,” she said. “ICE has gone too far, and that has backfired now.”

She added that the “best messaging” on immigration is “some control for the border plus a humanitarian process for immigration.”

Iowa’s Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek traveled more than 800 miles to Laredo, Texas, to film an ad at the border touting his support for tougher enforcement.

“I came to the border to meet firsthand with the people who work to keep it secure. What happens down here affects us up in Iowa, so we’ve got to address it,” Turek says in the ad. “I voted with Republicans to allow law enforcement to arrest and deport criminals.”

Weeks earlier, he released another ad speaking to Iowans and vowing that he would “work with anyone” to fix immigration — “including President Trump, to secure the border.”

Closer to the border, Democrat Johnny Garcia is trying to win Texas’ redrawn and Republican-friendly 35th Congressional District against GOP nominee Carlos De La Cruz.

Garcia criticized Trump’s ICE raids as detrimental to the economy. But at a recent forum, he also blamed Biden’s policies for failures at the border and referred to a fatal smuggling conspiracy in 2022 that led to the deaths of dozens of people.

“We’ve also gotten to see, unfortunately, how Biden got it wrong on the border,” Garcia said. “I’ll admit that every single day. We got to see one of the largest migrant fatalities in this district in south San Antonio, with 53 migrants that were locked in a trailer.”

“So we can’t afford to just turn a blind eye to our border,” he added. “But at the same time, we can’t turn a blind eye to what we’re seeing happening on our streets.”

World.title: Sen. Tim Scott dodges on whether he would accept the results of the Alaska Senate race
World.content:
Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., declined to say whether he would accept the results of the Alaska Senate race if Democrat Mary Peltola wins following a bombshell report from The New York Times about Democrats’ alleged efforts to recruit a candidate with the same name as the Republican incumbent.

Asked on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” whether he would accept the election results if Peltola is certified to have won the Senate seat, Scott did not directly answer the question.

“Dan Sullivan is going to win, Kristen,” he told moderator Kristen Welker. “You know that, and that’s the only thing I’m going to tell you because it’s the truth.”

Scott went on to criticize Democrats for allegedly working to recruit a candidate with the same name as Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, a controversy that exploded last week following a report from The New York Times.

“What I can tell you about the truth is you can’t trust Mary Peltola’s campaign and the collusion between her campaign and the DSCC,” said Scott, who also serves as the chairman of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, the GOP counterpart to the DSCC.

The New York Times reported Wednesday that Democrats allegedly sought to recruit a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan. The report said the efforts allegedly involved members of the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which works to elect Democrats to the Senate.

Following the report, the DSCC said in a statement that it “is not involved with Dan J. Sullivan.” Peltola, too, said she “knew nothing about any other candidates on the ballot except for me and the incumbent.”

Asked a second time whether he would accept the election results, Scott dodged the question.

“Number one, Dan Sullivan, the real Dan Sullivan, will win,” said Scott. “And number two, it actually is a federal offense to confuse voters.”

NBC News has previously reported that people who worked to recruit the challenger Dan J. Sullivan did not necessarily violate the law.

Elisa Rios, Peltola’s former campaign manager who was fired in August, participated in interviews with The New York Times, but later said she retracted “all statements made regarding the 2026 Alaska Senate race.”

Before The New York Times report was published, the Justice Department filed a lawsuit in Alaska seeking to block the certification of the results of the Senate election if Dan S. Sullivan loses. The DOJ cited potential voter confusion over having another candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.

In the aftermath of the Times’ report, President Donald Trump has said that both Peltola and the challenger Sullivan should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted.

On Thursday, Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a Republican, said he was ordering a state investigation to determine whether the alleged “scheme violated Alaska’s laws and whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted.”

Democrats have a sizable advantage in the battle for control of Congress days ahead of the midterm elections, a new national NBC News poll finds, with voters clamoring for change and voicing all-time high disapproval of President Donald Trump.

Registered voters prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress by a 7-point margin, with Democrats leading Republicans 52%-45% — 2 points more than in last month’s poll. That includes a 21-point lead among independents.

The president’s disapproval rating has climbed to 60%, a new high mark across his two terms in the NBC News poll. And for the first time in 30 years of NBC News polling, more voters say they are dissatisfied with their financial situation (51%) than satisfied (49%).

A fire burns in Frankfurt's city center on Oct. 31. Andreas Arnold / dpa/picture alliance

Rioters looted stores and set fire to barricades in Frankfurt on Saturday as demonstrations across Germany called for lower living costs and better education.

Tens of thousands of people took to the streets in more than 30 cities, including Berlin and Frankfurt, in protests organized by the campaign group Gen Z Regelt, or Gen Z Takes Charge.

France, Italy, Serbia and Spain have seen protests against the cost of living, among other causes. As the demonstrations began Saturday afternoon in Paris, protesters were pictured holding a banner that read: “We do not need tear gas for our future to be blurry.”

Stewart shared a photo of herself in tattered clothing, holding a clipboard that read, “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” She posed with a tired expression and makeup meant to look like dirt on her face.

The photo was the third slide in an Instagram carousel promoting her candle collection on QVC.

World.title: Jet crashes in Florida, killing all nine people on board
World.content:
All nine people on board a Learjet 60 jet died in a “cataclysmic” crash in Florida on Sunday afternoon, officials said.

The flight, which departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, crashed near Cresthaven around 12:50 p.m., the Federal Aviation Administration said.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said all nine on the flight died. He called the crash a “horrific tragedy” on social media, adding, “Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost.”

The identities of the people on board have not been released.

Video showed a crater in the middle of a road engulfed in flames.

In distressing air traffic control audio, a woman can be heard saying, “Mayday, mayday. We’re descending 10,000 feet per minute.”

She later frantically yells, saying the jet was descending at 20,000 feet per minute.

“We’re gonna crash into the ground 722 Bravo Delta,” she can be heard saying, followed by a scream.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis described the crash as “cataclysmic.”

“It looked like a missile going down. It left a big crater on the side of the road,” DeSantis told reporters after the crash.

He said the crash spewed a large amount of debris that spanned a “pretty significant distance” but that there were no reports of anyone on the ground being injured or killed.

The aircraft is registered to an LLC in Delaware, according to FAA records.

The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the crash.

The Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said an aircraft incident was under investigation in the area of Military Trail, and all northbound and southbound lanes are closed until further notice.

World.title: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke
World.content:
Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., was hospitalized Saturday after a stroke, a spokesperson for the senator said Sunday.

The senator “started experiencing numbness in his arm while at his son’s hockey game,” Allison Herwitt, Murphy’s chief of staff, said in a statement.

“He was taken to a local hospital, where it was discovered he had experienced a stroke,” she added. “He was transferred to Johns Hopkins for further monitoring and is responding well to treatment. The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery.”

Murphy, 53, is not up for re-election this year but has traversed the country on behalf of Democratic candidates running for elected office.

The senator was slated to be in New Hampshire today, campaigning alongside Rep. Chris Pappas, the Democratic nominee for Senate there.

Murphy, an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump, said Thursday at an event in Washington for the Middle East Institute that Trump’s plan to possibly resume the war with Iran after the midterms “insane.”

Earlier this fall, Murphy was one of over a dozen lawmakers whose offices received letters containing suspicious substances.

World.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula 1 champion ever at 20 years old
World.content:
At the opening race of the season in Australia, Russell seemed to solidify his front-running status with a victory, as Mercedes fulfilled expectations by building the fastest car under the new regulations that began this year. But from there, it has all been downhill for the 28-year-old British driver, as Antonelli won the next five races to establish himself as the clear favorite.

“Kimi surprised us all with his maturity. Obviously we knew he had speed and all this talent. I think not many people expected that he was, this year, so quick and beating a very strong teammate like George,” former Haas F1 team principal Guenther Steiner told NBC News. “I didn’t expect it. He’s a 20-year-old with the mind of a 30-year-old experienced F1 driver. That made him what he is.”

Antonelli took the lead of the championship in the third race of the 2026 season, and he never relinquished it. A critical juncture came when Antonelli won in Canada and Monaco while Russell failed to score points in either race because of a mechanical failure and pit-timing error by F1. Antonelli’s lead ballooned to 68 points after the sixth race.

Antonelli had some bad luck of his own in subsequent races, and Russell made up ground. But it wasn’t enough. And as Russell has acknowledged, Antonelli has outperformed him throughout the season, with more pole positions and race wins as well as superior speed when both drivers had an equal opportunity.

Another former F1 team boss, Otmar Szafnauer, said Antonelli’s championship-winning season can be attributed to three things: “His mental preparedness, raw talent and great attitude.”

“He is able to mentally compartmentalize to his advantage,” Szafnauer told NBC News, by staying consistent under pressure.

The Italian all but guaranteed his title last Sunday with a victory in Austin, Texas, prompting even his rivals to concede defeat.

“The truth is he’s been at a higher level than me this year,” Russell told reporters Thursday.

“This season, we have the best car, and I’m not able to achieve these results. So, yeah, it’s quite strange and certainly has us scratching our heads a little bit,” he said.

After four years in a Mercedes that was capable only of occasional race wins, Russell finally got his title-winning car. But it was Antonelli who made the most of it. The new generation of F1 cars — with less downforce and more reliance on electrical power — has forced competitors to rethink their driving styles.

The new cars reward Antonelli’s aggressive style of braking late and attacking corners with sharp turns. He’s also more comfortable than others driving at the limit with a loose-handling car that tends to slide underneath him.

By contrast, the 2026 cars punish Russell’s preference for smoother inputs and gaining lap time by getting on the throttle early on corner exits. That approach, which served him well in the previous generation of cars, eats up tire life and battery power in the newer machines. Russell has said adjusting his approach feels “like a golfer changing his swing.”

The defining moment of the rivalry came at the Italian Grand Prix, when Antonelli started 19th and hunted down Russell to win the race. It was a statement victory that underscored his advantage over his teammate.

World.title: Jet from Texas crashes near homes in Palm Beach, Florida, killing 9 on board
World.content:
A business jet with nine people aboard nose-dived and crashed near homes in Florida late Sunday afternoon, killing everyone inside, officials said.

No one on the ground was injured, Gov. Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference. Approximately 600 people have been evacuated from the crash site near a mobile home park in Cresthaven, local officials said.

The Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County just before 1 p.m., according to the Federal Aviation Administration. The agency said the aircraft had left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was bound for the Bahamas.

Details about what may have caused the crash had not yet been shared.

"It was like a missile coming down and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere. And to have those people on board, it's really a tragic way to see people pass away," DeSantis said.

Law enforcement responds to a plane crash in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. AP Photo/Mark Elias

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed on X that all people on board have died.

"Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost," Duffy wrote.

Air traffic control audio captured the pilot's last communications with the ATC tower before the aircraft went down. The pilot can be heard saying they were descending 10,000 feet per minute, according to the audio on LiveATC.net. The pilot later declared an emergency, yelling, "We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute."

The pilot is later heard telling the tower: "We're gonna crash ... We're out of time."

The National Transportation Safety Board said Sunday it is launching a go-team to investigate the crash, and investigators are expected to arrive later Sunday and Monday morning.

Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, told the Associated Press that the jet was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.

"This is definitely a tragedy," he said.

Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky.

The Palm Beach Sheriff's Office said all northbound and southbound lanes of Military Trail near Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North were closed until further notice.

World.title: Stevens endorses Rogers amid rift with El-Sayed
World.content:
Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday amid a rift with Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed that has come front and center in the final sprint to Election Day.

"Our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away, and he's right," Stevens said in a video posted on social media Sunday. "And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today."

Stevens appeared alongside Rogers at a Detroit church on Sunday.

Stevens, who narrowly lost to El-Sayed in Michigan's Democratic primary in August, where she was heavily supported by the Senate Democrats' campaign arm, called on El-Sayed last week to condemn an outside group's ad linking U.S. military aid to Israel to rising grocery prices, which she characterized as antisemitic. El-Sayed accused Stevens of "relitigating a primary that ended three months ago," although he has also clarified that the ad "was not made by me" and said he disagrees with its contents.

Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, right, and Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., attend a service at Perfecting Church, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. AP Photo/Jose Juarez

El-Sayed pushed to return the attention to the issues facing Michigan voters as he takes on the GOP candidate, Rogers. But Rogers praised Stevens on Friday for calling on El-Sayed to denounce the ad, and for expressing concerns raised by Michigan Jewish voters.

"Representative Haley Stevens is a courageous leader who deserves the respect of every Michigan voter," Rogers said in a post on X. "She has conducted herself with nothing but class since the Democratic primary, a primary where a majority of voters did not vote for her party's nominee."

Speaking to reporters after he appeared with Stevens at the Detroit church Sunday, Rogers said he was honored to receive her support.

"This is more a statement about standing together against hate and the future of this state and this country than it is anything else," Rogers said.

Rogers said he got the call Sunday morning from Stevens, and the two decided to appear together at the church. He said he and Stevens talked about what was better for the future of the state. And he noted that Stevens reminded him at the end of their call that she remains a Democrat.

Responding to the endorsement on Sunday, El-Sayed said, "I actually don't think about Haley Stevens."

"This is a state of 10 million people who deserve a lot better from their government. I'm a lot more focused on the 9,999,998 that are not the ones who are talking about."

Stevens said she's "not trying to harm" the Democratic Party with the move, insisting that she isn't "turning her back on Democrats."

"It is this one vote," she said. "And I will tell you why: Because when you see hate, when you see us standing with Hasan Piker, and repeated hate, it's not acceptable."

"That's it. It's my personal and private decision," Stevens said. "It's a Michigan moment, and everyone is entitled to their opinion."

Stevens said she "meant it" when she previously endorsed El-Sayed. But she added, "He chose to close his campaign by saying I wasn't welcome."

The appearance with Rogers came after Stevens had been expected to appear with El-Sayed at a unity event Sunday alongside Rep. Jim Clyburn of South Carolina. But El-Sayed said Saturday, "I would rather not distract from the key issues of this campaign."

Stevens' fiancé, Jason Turkish, said last week that he is voting for Rogers.

Democrats stunned by reversal, Trump praises Stevens

After Stevens endorsed Rogers, top Democrats expressed their continued support for El-Sayed's candidacy, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.

"Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors," Schumer said in a statement.

In a post on X, Schumer called it a "despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens."

Democratic Rep. Debbie Dingell of Michigan said Michiganders "want leaders focused on making their lives more affordable."

"That's what they're talking about, not Congresswoman Stevens' continued efforts to get attention," she said in a statement. " If we are going to fight to improve the lives of working men and women in Michigan, we must stay focused on electing Democrats up and down the ballot, and that includes electing Abdul El-Sayed as Michigan's next senator."

Michigan Democratic Party chair Curtis Hertel posted on social media that Stevens is "not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future."

President Trump praised Stevens for backing Rogers.

"Her following is huge, and the level of respect from the People of Michigan, especially our African American and Jewish populations, is virtually unparalleled," Mr. Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Haley said what few people are willing to say. She showed great and almost unprecedented loyalty to the Great People of Michigan with what she did."

He told reporters later: "That was a big move, I think. Nobody expected that, but it's a smart thing to do because El-Sayed would destroy our country. So I thought that was fantastic."

Appearing with Mr. Trump in Iowa for a campaign rally, House Speaker Mike Johnson said he spoke to Stevens after she endorsed Rogers and "encouraged her to stay safe and keep speaking the truth."

More broadly, Republicans cited the move as they billed El-Sayed as too liberal for the state.

"Democrats who feel Abdul has abandoned them have a home with Mike, who is building a winning coalition of Democrats, Independents, and Republicans to save Michigan from El-Sayed's radical, terrorist-sympathizing agenda," Republican National Committee spokesman Hunter Lovell said in a statement. "The center of Michigan politics has moved, and Abdul is on the wrong side of it."

Stevens' team resigns after endorsement

Ahead of Stevens' endorsement of Rogers and her appearance on Sunday, her longtime chief of staff resigned, with a number of staff members expected to follow soon.

In a statement first shared by CNN, Stevens' former chief of staff Justin German said he and the team are "shocked and heartbroken" by her decision to support Rogers and that they are "wholeheartedly supporting" El-Sayed for Senate.

"This election is too important to sow division or stand on the sidelines," German wrote. "Those of us who are Michigan voters are supporting Democrats up and down the ballot and have been working all season to elect strong Democratic majorities to the House and Senate — we will continue to do so."

"Hello, as of November 1st I am no longer with the Office of Congresswoman Haley Stevens," an automated email reply from Stevens' former communications director, Logan Basch, reads.

Joetta Appiah, Stevens' former press secretary and campaign spokesperson, said in a statement that Stevens is "walking back on everything her campaign stood for."

"Michiganders deserve better, and they need to stay focused on what matters, which is electing Abdul to the Senate to stand up to Donald Trump, hold his administration accountable, and fight to lower costs for Michiganders," Appiah said. "We cannot let this distract us from Tuesday."

60 MINUTES will feature Ross Douthat's exclusive interviews with Michigan Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers.

World.title: Sanders says GOP rhetoric about El-Sayed "should appall" Americans
World.content:
Washington — Sen. Bernie Sanders decried some of the rhetoric from Republicans in the Michigan Senate race, as the GOP has leaned in heavily on attacks on Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed's ethnicity and religion.

"That level of racism, overt absolute racism, is frankly disgusting and should appall every decent American," Sanders said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan."

Sanders, who's supported El-Sayed's campaign, specifically referred to comments made by Republican surrogates, including President Trump and GOP Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas. Republicans have called El-Sayed a supporter of the Muslim Brotherhood, and implied that electing him could even be deadly to Americans. El-Sayed, who would be the first Muslim senator, has denied any connection to the Muslim Brotherhood and condemned the comments. The Trump administration earlier this year designated certain chapters of the Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist groups.

Sanders said, "What Cruz and Trump and Vance and others are saying is disgusting."

"The fact of the matter is that Abdul is running an extraordinary campaign, and I think what you're going to see is a good victory in Michigan for him," Sanders said. "People will rebel against that type of ugliness."

The Vermont independent also condemned s in the Michigan Senate race, saying, "I have never in my life seen such disgusting, racist, fearmongering ads as those that are taking place in Michigan right now."

"They are calling Abdul El Sayed — who's a medical doctor — they're calling him a terrorist, a jihadist, really disgusting things," Sanders said. "And the fact that any Republican would stand behind those horrible ads is a disgrace."

Sanders also weighed in on the rift between El-Sayed and his former primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens, who called on El-Sayed last week to condemn an outside group's ad linking U.S. military aid to Israel to rising grocery prices, which she characterized as antisemitic. El-Sayed accused her of "relitigating a primary that ended three months ago." And on Saturday, he reiterated that the ad "was not made by me," adding that he disagrees with its contents.

Sanders said, "Haley Stevens lost a very, very close primary. I can understand being upset about that." But he stressed that during a midterm cycle of paramount importance, Michiganders will see the bigger picture.

"So the people in Michigan understand, 'Sure, we have disagreements with Abdul on this and that issue,'" he said. "But from what I can see, all over the state, people are standing up. They're going to stand with Abdul, take on somebody who will be nothing more than a rubber stamp for the Trump administration. That's Mike Rogers."

Shortly after Sanders' appearance, Stevens publicly endorsed Rogers, saying "I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," adding that she sees what is on the ballot is "who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now."

El-Sayed on Sunday did not reference Stevens by name but instead said "this is a state of 10 million people who deserve a lot better from their government. I'm a lot more focused on the 9,999,998 that are not the ones who are talking about."

On "Face the Nation," Sanders referenced his own family's history to illustrate his view on how some Jewish Michiganders feel about El-Sayed's criticism of Israel.

"I am Jewish. My father's family was wiped out by Hitler. Anti-Semitism is an extraordinarily disgusting and dangerous ideology that has killed millions and millions of lives in the last century. We cannot tolerate anti-Semitism, period," Sanders said.

But Sanders argued that, "To be critical of a racist, extremist government in Israel, and to say that American taxpayers should not spend a nickel supporting that government is not anti-Semitism."

"It is attacking a right-wing government, and I would say the same about any other government on earth," Sanders said. "Does not reflect the nature of the religion of the people who are in that country. So I reject that."

World.title: Judge tosses lawsuit seeking to delay certification of Alaska Senate race
World.content:
A federal judge in Alaska has thrown out the Trump administration's lawsuit seeking to block certification of the state's Senate election results in this week's midterm elections if the Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan loses.

U.S. District Judge Sharon L. Gleason wrote in a 20-page order Sunday that the Justice Department did not have proper legal standing to bring the suit last week. The suit asked Gleason to block the state's election results from being certified because a teacher named Daniel J. Sullivan is also on the state's ballot, alleging that his candidacy deliberately sought to confuse voters by running with the same ballot name and party affiliation as the state's incumbent senator.

The Justice Department argued that Daniel J. Sullivan's name on the ballot potentially diverted voters, and the Democrat running in the race, Mary Peltola, would benefit as a result.

Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, hands out candy at a Halloween event outside the Big Lake Lions Club, on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in Big Lake, Alaska. AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson

Gleason said she could not grant the injunction that the Trump administration sought "because the United States has failed to establish the redressability prerequisite for Article III standing."

"More fundamentally, the United States provides no workable plan as to how it proposes to segregate ballots cast for Daniel J. Sullivan on Election Day and then conduct a court-ordered unspecified 'investigation' of those ballots in a manner that would preserve voter secrecy," Gleason wrote, adding that the Justice Department "failed to satisfy its burden to show that its alleged injury is redressable by a court order."

The Justice Department filed a notice of appeal on Sunday.

Earlier, a DOJ spokesperson told CBS News that the federal judge dismissed the case on procedural grounds "but did not dispute the argument of the United States that Daniel J. Sullivan (a/k/a Decoy Dan) entered the race as a frivolous candidate to confuse voters.

"Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes," the spokesperson said.

The suit, which argues Sullivan's candidacy violates the National Voter Registration Act, was amended on Thursday to include recent reporting by The New York Times on alleged efforts by people associated with Peltola's campaign to find candidates who could draw votes away from the Republican senator. It included a second claim for relief, arguing the court needs to intervene under the Constitution's Supremacy Clause in order to allow the government to enforce the law and prevent a "conspiracy."

Peltola's campaign responded to the Times story by saying the campaign "has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign."

"I am not interested in tricking voters," Peltola said during a recent campaign event.

Sen. Sullivan on Sunday told CNN's "State of the Union" that he thought the presence of a second Sullivan on the ballot would impact the election, saying: "I'm sure I'm going to lose a lot of votes to that trickery."

He also said he doubted Peltola's claims that she had no idea her top political aides were involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan to run as a way to confuse voters.

"There is no way this went on for a year that they weren't informing her," Sullivan said. "She got caught lying, and she's still lying to the Alaskan people, the media, to all of us."

In addition to the civil lawsuit, the Justice Department is also criminally investigating an alleged plot to add Daniel J. Sullivan to the state's ballot and has issued subpoenas targeting several Democratic officials believed to be tied to the effort to recruit him to appear on Alaska's ballot. Nobody in the race has been charged with a crime.
